# Decisions log

Purpose: what the owner asked for and why things are the way they are. Newest last. Check here before
"fixing" something that looks odd; it may be deliberate.

1. **PvZ-like with free-moving troops;** no tower path. The back line (`baseX`) only moves forward.
2. **Tiny RPG sprites.** Shadows are separate so only the body hops when cheering.
3. **Winning:** no walk-back animation. Troops cheer in place while the back line moves up, then
   retake their drop spots.
4. **HP after a win** is restored only if a healer is alive. Every game starts with one free priest.
   Every healer heals after a win: itself, then melee, then long range, only the hurt.
5. **Formation** healer | long range | melee, later melee split into heavy (cavalry, spear, axe) and
   front (soldier, knight, berserk). The ranks matter only while setting up; in battle troops
   maximise their range and long range kite.
6. **Navigation:** whoever wants to pass goes first, and the idle troop gives way and comes back. It
   applies to ALL troops, healers included.
7. **Healers** follow the army at the back line, advance only to reach the hurt, fall back, and ignore
   fresh troops spawned at the back. Their range was raised (96) so long range don't block them.
8. **Monsters** stay 2 tiles inside the right edge. The field always spans the full screen width.
9. **Auto-save after every won wave.** "Ulang" deletes the save.
10. **Deploy zone** can be bought wider, up to 30% of the view (70% stays battleground). Replaced by 54:
    the zone follows the capacity.
11. **Camera** follows the troops, the back line comes along, and later the camera keeps the battle
    line mid-screen.
12. **Game over** when every troop is dead, too. Then the monsters cheer.
13. **Loot:**
    - Items are per troop TYPE with unlimited stacking (later capped by awakening recipes: 30).
    - Relics are per troop (e.g. lifesteal).
    - The drop rate was lowered to 8% on request.
    - The potion became +5 HP/s regen, and base regen is 0.
14. **Tap-to-spawn** replaced drag-to-deploy. Troops march in from off screen left. Repositioning by
    drag before a wave remains.
15. **Buying +Zona** moves the army up to the new front. Replaced by 54: buying capacity moves nobody.
16. **Backgrounds:** the Valley pack replaced all others. The field is only the dirt road, stacked
    twice. Replaced by 228: the band above the field is GandalfHardcore's Normal BG layers, and the road gave way to a
    grassy floor built from that pack.
17. **HUD is a book:**
    - Floating on the right between waves (landscape); below the field on portrait/mobile.
    - Pack buttons, frames, HP bars and cursor.
    - Small bag grid.
    - No zone or spawn lines.
18. **Windows only, with hot reload;** never make the owner quit the game to see a change. The platform
    part was replaced by 21 (the Mac); the hot reload rule still holds.
19. **Knowledge base (this folder):** every agent reads docs/README.md first, and every document has
    one purpose.
20. **Monsters grow:** every wave raises HP and damage, and monsters come in ranks (normal, elite,
    high elite, mini boss, boss) with the same sprite but stronger stats. The HP bar colour shows the
    rank.
21. **Development moved to the owner's Mac** on 2026-09-27 ("lanjutkan development game ini di sini").
    - A macOS desktop target (`macos/`) was added and is now the one the game runs on (dev-workflow.md).
    - The hot reload rule from 18 is unchanged: never make the owner quit the game to see a change.
    - The Windows setup is kept documented in case the owner goes back.
22. **The main agent orchestrates;** other work goes to sibling agents ("aku mau kamu jadi orkestrator
    dan pekerjaan lain kamu berikan kepada sibling agent untuk mengerjakannya"). This widens the
    test-agent split in testing.md to all work.
23. **Upgraded troops cost more, a little** ("ketika soldier di upgrade maka harga spawnnya juga naik
    tapi tidak besar"). It applies to every troop type (items are per type; the owner's example was
    the soldier): each item the type took adds 10% of its base price (loot-items-relics.md). Relics,
    held by one troop, don't change the price.
24. **Kill gold depends on the monster's rank** ("emas drop setiap tier musuh berbeda, monster biasa
    dan boss beda drop emasnya"): the type's base gold ×1 normal, ×2 elite, ×3 high elite, ×5 mini
    boss, ×10 boss (the necromancer: 400). This replaced the earlier ×1/×2/×4/×10 (normal to mini boss) and
    the boss's plain 40. The necromancer's raised skeletons pay nothing, so a boss can't be farmed. The wave-win
    bonus is unchanged (units-and-combat.md).
25. **Welcome screen** ("tambahkan welcome screen ke game ini"; nothing more specified, so these are
    defaults, ui-hud.md):
    - Shown on launch after the loading dial: the valley drifting with a squad marching, and "Tower
      Defense" on a pack parchment panel.
    - "Lanjutkan" only when a save exists, showing its wave; "Main Baru" starts fresh and, over a
      save, needs a second tap within 3 s ("Yakin?") because it deletes the save.
    - Drawn on the Flame canvas by `Board`, not as a Flutter overlay, so the pack's pixel cursor stays.
    - Going back to it from a game is `Board.showWelcome()`, for a later "Menu Utama" button.
26. **Supports catch up with fast melee** ("troops bisa ketinggalan jika troops melee-nya terlalu cepat
    sementara long range atau healernya tidak di-upgrade sepatunya"). A long range or healer that fell
    more than its rank's place plus 1.5 tiles behind the melee walks as fast as the fastest melee until
    it is back. It stays at its own speed when kiting, falling back, and before or after a wave.
    Melee keep their boots' edge (formation-and-navigation.md).
27. **Hovering loot explains it** ("setiap item ketika di-hover maka akan memunculkan informasi dari
    kegunaan item tersebut"): every item and relic in the book (bag slots and the troop rows' stat
    icons) shows a tooltip with its name, its effect in real numbers, how it stacks, the price step,
    how to use it and the count (ui-hud.md). The words are built in game.dart from the rules' own
    constants so they can't drift from the balance. It is the one place with how-to text in the UI.
    Touch has no hover, so a long press (0.4 s) shows it, and that press is then no tap.
28. **A wave meter at the top centre** ("perlu ditambahkan meter wave di tengah atas yang menunjukkan
    sudah berapa banyak dalam 1 wave tersebut monsternya terspawn"): while a wave is on, a pixel bar
    over the field fills as the wave's monsters come on, with crossed swords and "spawned/total"
    (ui-hud.md). The total is everything the wave spawns from its queue (mini boss, boss and queued
    escorts too); the boss's raised skeletons don't count. Once all are out the bar turns gold and stays
    full until the wave is won. It keeps clear of the battle bar and of a book opened mid-fight.
29. **Two kinds of necromancer: one summons, one only heals** ("enemynya juga ditambah ada yang bisa heal,
    misal necromancernya dibuat jadi 2 jenis necromancer: yang bisa spawn enemy lain dan ada yang bisa
    cuma heal saja"). The summoner is the boss as before. The new healing necromancer (`necro_healer`)
    never attacks. It heals the most hurt monster in reach, the boss included, and stands behind the
    monster front the way the priest stands behind the troops (units-and-combat.md,
    formation-and-navigation.md). The details were defaults the owner was told:
    - One per wave from wave 4 and two from wave 10, and on boss waves the last one escorts the boss.
    - It gets tiers and kill gold like any monster.
    - It is drawn as the necromancer recoloured in memory (teal robe, gold hood), with no new asset files.
    - Its heal is 6.7 HP/s at wave 1 against the priest's 10, so one healer makes it worth killing
      without making it unkillable.
30. **Troop awakening** ("aku mau tambahkan fitur troops awakening, jadi ketika status dari troops sudah
    masuk ke status titik tertentu maka dia akan awakening dan warna dari troops tersebut akan berubah
    serta efek dari serangannya juga akan berubah, lalu harganya akan naik secara drastis. Ini akan
    membuat player tidak bisa spawn troops dengan harga murah tapi status tinggi."). The trigger was then
    made a recipe with caps ("setiap awakening troops punya batas atas attribute, jadi user tidak bisa
    naikkan cuma 1 attribute saja melainkan harus naikkan attribute yang lain untuk trigger awakening dan
    baru bisa naikkan lagi status dari troops tersebut. Contohnya knight: misal untuk awakening harus
    naikkan attack sama shield 3x, speed dan attack speed 2x maka akan membuat awakening; selagi user
    belum awakening maka user tidak bisa buat knight di-upgrade attacknya jadi 4x.").
    - Per troop type: `awakenRecipe` is both what it needs and the cap per item kind; kinds outside it
      never go on the type. Up to 3 levels, each the recipe once more (loot-items-relics.md).
    - Each level triples the price, recolours the type's troops (gold, violet, crimson) and their hit
      effects; no stat bonus. Items past a cap in old saves stay.
    - At level 3 the caps stay: the type is finished (the alternative, unlimited items after level 3,
      would bring back one-stat stacking).
    - The book shows it under each troop's info ("awakening ditampilkan juga di bawah informasi
      troops"; "maksud aku juga butuh tampilkan informasi troops itu sekarang sudah awakening ke
      berapa"): the level as a number in words ("Belum bangkit", "Bangkit 2", "Bangkit 3 (Maks)") and
      the next level's recipe as have/need per item. On the field, 1–3 pips by the HP bar.
31. **Melee reach has a ceiling** ("item bow harusnya tidak bisa ditambahkan ke troops melee secara
    berlebihan karena mereka punya maksimal jangkauan serangan, misal 1,7 box area"): `meleeMaxRange`
    1.7 tiles at every awakening level; a melee type at it takes no more bows. No base range exceeds it.
32. **Every monster attribute grows with the wave** ("semakin tinggi wave maka base attribute enemy juga
    ikut naik, misal di wave 10 monster biasa HP-nya 10 tapi di wave 20 jadi 15, dan begitu juga dengan
    attribute yang lain"). HP (+15% of the base a wave) and damage (+6%) already grew, faster than the
    owner's example, so they stay. Added: walking speed +2% a wave (capped at +50%), attacks per second
    +1% a wave (capped at +25%) and long range reach +1% a wave (capped at +25%); melee reach never
    grows. A monster healer's heal is its damage, so it grows with it and comes faster; its reach
    doesn't (the necro healer doesn't shoot). Tiers still multiply on top; kill gold still has no wave
    scaling (units-and-combat.md).
    - Attacks per second first grew +2% a wave (cap +50%). A probe (same army and items under each rule,
      6 seeds) found waves 15–25 then needed ~25–30% more troops than before the change (wave 20: 36
      instead of 28), so that growth was halved. At +1% the extra is 0–2 troops at waves 10–20 and 6 at
      wave 25.
    - From wave 16 HP and damage grow +30% / +10% a wave (72).
33. **Bookmarks on the book** ("di book ui tambahkan bookmark untuk entry point ke settings dan entry
    point ke setting battle field (ui yang sekarang)", then "ui mulai di book dipindahkan jadi bookmark
    di atas book, begitu juga dengan emas dan gelombang, coba carikan icon untuk hal tersebut";
    ui-hud.md):
    - The style is the owner's reference pictures ("maksudku bookmark yang ini ya"): the Cute Fantasy UI
      pack's own book tabs and ribbon flags (Book_UI.png, supplied by the owner then). Square icon tabs
      on the top edge switch pages, "Medan Perang" (the book as it was, crossed swords) and "Pengaturan"
      (gear); the open one is paper-coloured and runs into its page. Ribbons out of the right cover carry
      Emas (orange, coin), Gelombang (red, sword: the pack has no flag) and Mulai (green, play; white and
      tucked in during a wave), moved off the right page. On phones the ribbons stand on the top edge.
    - Nyawa, not named, stays on the page. The battle bar uses the same icons.
    - Defaults (nothing more specified): Pengaturan holds the Musik and Efek volumes (0–100% in steps of
      10, − / + and tappable notches), heard at once and kept in settings.json apart from the save, so a
      new game keeps them; plus "Menu Utama" back to the welcome screen. The book opens on the battle
      field, and the settings page doesn't pause the battle.
    - Then the book grew ("size booknya dibuat lebih tinggi lagi dan lebih lebar lagi"): in landscape it
      spans from 26% of the width to the ribbons and stands taller; its page content scales with it.
    - And the wave meter (28) no longer moves aside for an open book ("ketika open book, meter wave
      jangan ikut terdorong"): it stays at the top centre, and the book keeps below its band.
34. **One relic per troop, refused, not swapped** ("1 troops hanya bisa memegang 1 artefak dan jika user
    mau assign lagi maka akan tertolak dengan window message troops tersebut sudah punya artefak"): a
    troop that holds a relic refuses another (it stays in the bag), and a small message window says
    "Pasukan ini sudah punya artefak". The window (`showMessage`) is reusable for other refusals; it
    closes on a press or after 2 s. There is still no way to take a relic off (not asked for).
35. **A won wave's loot is counted, not repeated** ("hasil loot tidak perlu ada 2 kali item yang sama,
    cukup tampilkan Nx<item> dimana N adalah jumlahnya"): the "MENANG!" popup shows each kind once as
    "Nx" + icon, items then relics (`lootCounts`), "1x" included so every entry reads the same.
36. **The cursor pack's swords are the game's cursor** ("gunakan ini untuk cursor dalam game", with
    PixelRPGCursors Lite). Its crossed swords are the mouse cursor everywhere, drawn sharp at its own
    32 or 64 px art by pixel ratio, with the tip as the hotspot. Its hourglass turns under the mouse on
    the loading screen, the game's only wait (ui-hud.md, assets.md).
    - The Lite pack has no hand or pointer, so the old hand over tappable things is gone. The full,
      paid pack has more cursors and pressed states.
    - Touch shows no cursor, not even while dragging (it used to show the hand under the finger).
    - `ui_click.png` stays: it is the click sparks, not the cursor.
37. **The game is called "Path of Hero"** ("nama game dirubah ke Path of Hero"), in everything the
    player sees: the welcome title, the macOS window, menu bar and app menu, the Windows/Linux window
    titles, the Android label and the web page. The bundle id, the app and binary names, the Dart
    package, the save folder and the repo keep `tower_defense`. Changing the bundle id would move the
    sandbox container and lose the save; the rest is internal (dev-workflow.md). The ids and the macOS app's
    name changed later, before the first public build (133).
38. **The cursor is back to the Cute Fantasy one** ("kembalikan tampilan cursor ke sebelumnya"): 36 is
    undone. The pack's arrow, and the hand over anything tappable or draggable and while dragging, from
    `ui_icons.png` at 2×; the loading screen shows only the dial. The PixelRPGCursors Lite images and
    `tool/import_cursors.py` are removed; the pack stays in the gitignored `raw_assets/` (ui-hud.md,
    assets.md).
39. **A troop counter at the top left, broken down by type on a click** ("di ujung kiri atas ada
    counter jumlah pasukan yang di-breakdown menjadi tiap type troops, untuk detailnya user harus click
    baru keluar dropdownnya", issue #25): the number of living troops, always shown, on the battle bar's
    panel, level with the wave meter. A press drops a list down: each type on the field with its book
    sprite, name and count (ui-hud.md).
    - Defaults (nothing more specified): types with none are left out; the list folds on another press
      on the counter or on a press anywhere else (which then does what it would); a press on the list
      does nothing else. An awakened type's sprite shows in its level's colour.
    - Troop types got names for it (`troopTypeNames`: Prajurit, Ksatria, Pendekar, Pemanah, Penombak,
      Pendeta, Kapak Berzirah, Penyihir, Templar), shared with the rest of the UI. Names are content,
      not labels, so the rule that labels show just values still holds.
    - The count's panel grows with its text, so it can later read "used/capacity" (#26); the rows have
      room beside the name for a mark (#24's Hero).
40. **Score and scoreboard, local now, a server later** ("tambahkan score dan score board, untuk backendnya
    nanti pakai server tapi dibuat ada adapternya untuk bisa pakai local dan server http call, jadi
    walaupun servernya belum siap bisa pakai adapter localnya dulu untuk tulis score player ke board";
    scoreboard.md, ui-hud.md):
    - One `ScoreRepository` interface with a local-file adapter (scores.json) and an HTTP one. With a
      server set (`--dart-define=SCORE_SERVER=…`) every score is also kept on the device, and what the
      server didn't take waits in an outbox and is sent later, so no score is lost while it is down.
    - Defaults (nothing more specified): kills score by rank (10 / 25 / 50 / 150 / 500), a won wave n
      100·n, lives left 50 each at the end; the raised skeletons score nothing, like their gold. The
      player's name is asked once, at the first game over, and kept (player.json), apart from the save.
      The board shows the best 10 with the player's last entry lit.
    - The score shows at game over and on the board only, not live during play (the orchestrator's call,
      open to the owner). A server that can't be reached is told with the message window ("Server
      tidak tersedia").
41. **Every troop has a first and a last name** ("aku butuh dibuatkan name generator, jadi setiap troops
    yang di-spawn itu nantinya akan punya nama dan namanya dibuat jadi punya first name dan last
    name"). The defaults, as the owner was told:
    - Short fantasy names from two lists of 48 (lib/names.dart), never shared by two living troops.
    - Drawn with dice of their own, so they don't change the waves or the drops.
    - Saved with each troop; troops from older saves are named on load. The free healer is named too.
    - Shown in a small nameplate when the pointer rests on a troop (a long press on touch), and in
      messages about a troop: "Kira Thorn sudah punya artefak" (units-and-combat.md, ui-hud.md).
42. **The summoner necromancer spends MP and chooses what to raise** ("semakin tinggi wavenya maka monster
    yang bisa di-spawn sama musuh necromancer semakin tinggi levelnya, maksimal sampai 1 tingkat di bawah
    level dari si necromancer sekarang, misal dia spawn sebagai mini boss, maka maksimal yang bisa dia
    spawn adalah high elite. Dan setiap spawn anak buah itu akan menguras MP dari si necromancer, semakin
    tinggi yang di-spawn maka semakin banyak MP yang digunakannya. Di sini kita harus buatkan AI untuk si
    necromancer untuk mengambil keputusan paling optimal untuk spawn monster tier apa").
    Details are in units-and-combat.md.
    - **Ceiling:** one tier below its own, and no higher than the wave allows.
    - **Mini boss slot:** from wave 8 the necromancer takes it at 1/3.
    - **MP:** it has MP with regen, and each tier's minion costs more MP than the one below, by more than
      the tier's strength grows.
    - **The AI:** a deterministic scorer that can wait. Safe, it saves for the best tier; pressed, it
      spends on what it can afford now.
    - **Deviation 1, costs:** the brief's 10/25/60/150 MP made higher tiers worth LESS per MP, which
      contradicts "save for the more efficient tier", so the costs are 10/22/45/110.
    - **Deviation 2, the wave gate:** tied to the elite rolls (elites from wave 3) it made the first boss
      raise elites: a probe lost 60% of wave-5 games. So each boss after the first raises one tier
      higher (wave 5 skeletons, 10 elites, 15 high elites, 20 mini bosses).
    - The necromancer as mini boss pays the mini boss gold ×5 (200), more than a regular mini boss
      (35–50). Flagged to the owner.
43. **The healing necromancer stays at the back, heals for MP, and swings when it can't heal**
    ("nekromancer healer jangan terlalu depan, harusnya dia lebih sering di belakang untuk support dan
    bisa attack ketika sudah tidak bisa heal"; then "bukan menembakkan bolt gelap yang lemah tapi melee
    attack"). Details are in formation-and-navigation.md.
    - **Position:** it rests behind the rearmost monster and keeps two tiles outside every troop's
      reach, backing off when one comes closer. It steps up only as far as a heal needs.
    - **MP:** each heal costs 8 of its 40 MP.
    - **Swing:** when it can't heal, it swings its scythe (melee, weak) at a troop that reached it. It
      never charges.
44. **Healers can't walk while healing** ("healer tidak bisa jalan ketika sedang melakukan heal"). It
    applies to every healer, the priest and the healing necromancer: 0.6 s after starting a heal (or a
    swing) it stands still, doesn't step aside and isn't shoved. The after-win heals too.
45. **Agents stopped by a usage limit are woken by cron** ("buat 1 script yang user bisa pasang ke cron
    system untuk wakeup setiap agent yang kena limit"): `scripts/wake-limited-agents.sh`, see
    dev-workflow.md. It reads the transcripts, waits for the reset time, then stops + resumes the session.
46. **Defence; HP and MP only through awakening** ("di book ditambahkan 2 icon lagi yaitu MP dan HP, MP dan
    HP hanya bisa naik lewat awakening"; "perisai itu menaikkan defence dari troops, jadi ada defence dan
    ada HP, damage kena hp = defence troops - attack enemy"; "MP untuk troop: skill tiap troop").
    - The shield gives defence (`shieldDef` per shield) instead of HP. A blow does its attack minus the
      target's defence, but at least 10% of itself and at least 1, so nobody is untouchable. Monsters
      have no defence for now.
    - HP and the new MP (with MP regen) rise only through awakening: +25% of the base per level. MP is
      shown in the book but not spent yet (troop skills come later), so the field's MP bar stays
      the necromancers'.
    - The book shows HP (heart) and MP icons with the other six stats, two lines of four.
    - Old saves keep their shields, now as defence; a saved troop's HP is cut to its new most.
    - The templar's recipe trades shields for speed ("templar tambahkan item speed untuk awakening dan
      kurangin shield untuk awakeningnya"): sword 2, shield 2, boots 2, bow 1, potion 3.
47. **Awakening in the book as stars, details on hover** ("tulisan 'belum bangkit' di-takeout, diganti
    dengan star saja di bawah sprite troopsnya, lalu ketika bintangnya di-hover baru kelihatan next
    awakening butuh apa saja"): the text strip under each row is gone; three stars under the sprite show
    the level, and hovering them (long press on touch) shows the next awakening's recipe as have/need,
    or "Maks".
48. **A potion makes a healer heal more** ("racikan untuk troops healer itu bukan hanya menaikkan regennya,
    tapi juga ketika melakukan heal, heal yang dia lakukan lebih banyak lagi HP yang didapat targetnya"):
    on a healer type each potion also adds `potionHeal` 3 HP to every heal (the priest's base heal is 12),
    on top of the regen. Other troops' potions stay regen only.
49. **A won wave also tells who fell** ("ketika wave selesai, jika ada troops yang gugur juga
    diberitahukan"; ui-hud.md). The "MENANG!" popup gets a red "Gugur:" line under the loot, with each
    fallen troop's book sprite in grey. Defaults (nothing more specified):
    - Up to 3 fallen: each by its own name and its type, "Aldo Ash (Ksatria)" (the names of 41).
    - More: each type once as "Nx", like the loot (35), so the line stays short.
    - No line when nobody fell. A fallen troop's relic still goes back to the bag as it falls (34); the
      popup doesn't repeat that.
50. **Troops and items on separate pages; items are given item first** ("ui dari troops dan item perlu
    dipisahkan, cuma aku belum kepikiran kalau dipisahkan bagaimana caranya aku bisa assign item ke type
    troops"; the owner then chose "Pilih item dulu"; ui-hud.md):
    - The book has three tabs: Pasukan (the troops over both pages, 5 + 4, no scrolling; Nyawa, +Zona and
      x2 under them), Tas (items and relics) and Pengaturan.
    - In Tas a tapped item lists every troop type on the facing page with taken/cap; the ones that can't
      take it are greyed with why ("Tidak cocok", "Bangkit dulu", "Batas maks", "Jangkauan maks").
      Tapping a type gives it the item. A spread, not a popup: nothing covers the book, and it suits touch.
    - Relics still go by dragging onto a troop on the field; tapping one says so.
    - Dropping an item on a troop row is gone (rows and bag are on different pages). Dragging an item onto
      a troop on the field stays as a shortcut to its type.
    - Troop names (`troopTypeNames`, shared with the troop counter): Prajurit, Ksatria, Pendekar,
      Pemanah, Penombak, Pendeta, Kapak Berzirah, Penyihir, Templar.
51. **The game can be paused** ("tambahkan pause di dalam game", issue #33): a pause button at the top
    right (in the battle bar during a wave), Esc or P, and the window hiding pause it (`Game.paused`:
    nothing moves or counts down) and open a "Jeda" panel: Lanjut, Pengaturan, Menu Utama. Lanjut, Esc /
    P or a press off the panel resumes (ui-hud.md).
    - Defaults (nothing more specified): Pengaturan opens the book's settings page and the game stays
      paused there; leaving it brings the panel back. Menu Utama and "Lanjutkan" come back paused. The
      music plays quieter while the panel shows; the Mulai ribbon can't start a wave while paused. The
      pause isn't saved.
    - Losing focus alone doesn't pause, only the window hiding (minimized, another Space): the owner
      watches the game while typing in the terminal, and agents screenshot the unfocused window.
52. **Relics only from strong monsters; a mini boss every 3 waves** ("5% dari setiap high elite, dan 10%
    mini boss dan 30% dari boss. mini boss hadir setiap 3 wave dan boss hadir di setiap 5 wave", after a
    relic dropped in wave 1; loot-items-relics.md, units-and-combat.md):
    - `relicChance` by tier in one table: normal and elite 0, high elite 5%, mini boss 10%, boss 30%. The
      boss no longer drops one for sure. About 12.7 relics over waves 1–30 instead of about 28.
    - A necromancer's raised minions drop no relic whatever their tier (the orchestrator's call, like the
      gold they don't pay), so a stalled boss can't be farmed.
    - A mini boss every 3rd wave (3, 6, 9…), the boss every 5th; waves 15, 30… bring both, the mini boss
      first. The necromancer may still take the mini boss slot from wave 8 (so from 9) at 1/3, so those
      waves can hold two necromancers.
53. **Awakening colours only what is round a troop** ("ketika troop awakening cukup shadow, partikel, dan
    outline di sekitarnya yang berubah menjadi warna biru -> crimson -> gold", issue #34). This replaces
    30's whole-sprite recolour (gold, violet, crimson):
    - An awakened troop keeps its own colours. Its 1 px outline, ground shadow and rising sparks take its
      level's colour: level 1 blue, 2 crimson, 3 gold.
    - Its hit bursts and shots are recoloured toward the colour, as before.
    - The book row's sprite, the Tas page's type list and the troop counter get the outline. The book's
      stars and the field's level pips use the same colours.
    - The outlines are built once at load, in memory; drawing one costs one more image per troop.
54. **+Zona became +Kapasitas: the army has a size limit** ("zona -> maksimal jumlah troops"; the owner
    chose "+Zona jadi +Kapasitas"; camera-and-field.md). It replaces 10 and 15.
    - `capacity` troops may be alive at once. Defaults (not specified): 6 at the start (the free healer
      counted), +2 per purchase, priced like the old +Zona (75, then 25 more each time). A troop bought
      over it is refused with "Kapasitas penuh". The troop counter shows alive/capacity.
    - The deploy zone isn't bought any more: it is as wide as the capacity needs (8 per column, at least
      3, still at most 30% of the view; 58 made it a column per purchase), so capacity tops out at what
      the widest zone holds.
    - Buying capacity doesn't move the army forward (15 did); a wider zone is used from the next troop.
    - Old saves: each zone column bought counts as one capacity purchase (same prices), and nobody saved
      is cut (capacity at least the saved army).
55. **A magic staff for the casters** ("tambahkan tongkat sihir ke item yang di-drop oleh monster dan
    rubah kebutuhan dari sorcerer dan healer untuk menggunakan tongkat sihir", issue #30;
    loot-items-relics.md). Defaults (nothing more specified):
    - `Item.staff`, "Tongkat Sihir", drops like any item, each of the 7 kinds as likely.
    - It is magic power. On the wizard it multiplies damage ×1.25 per staff, like the sword it replaces,
      so the wizard's numbers don't change. On a healer it adds 3 HP to every heal, like the potion does
      (#28), so the heal never compounds and the order items came in doesn't matter.
    - Only the casters take it, and they take no sword. Recipes: the wizard staff 2 instead of sword 2;
      the priest staff 2, shield 2, bow 2, gloves 2, potion 2 (was shield 3, bow 2, gloves 2, potion 3).
      Both stay at 10 items a level.
    - Heals stay sane: the priest's heal per cast is 24 / 36 / 48 at levels 1 / 2 / 3 (was 21 / 30 /
      39), 153 HP/s at level 3 (was 124). Its own regen and defence are a little lower.
    - The icon is drawn for the game (tool/draw_icons.py), since no pack on this machine has a staff.
      The Tas page lays out 4 items to a row (4 + 3).
56. **Every 10th wave a troop becomes a Hero** ("setiap 10 wave ada 1 troops yang secara random jadi
    Hero dengan efek attributenya x3, dan troops biasa selagi dia ada attributenya naik jadi 0.3", issue
    #24; units-and-combat.md, ui-hud.md):
    - At the start of waves 10, 20, 30… one living troop that isn't a Hero yet becomes one, picked with
      dice of its own (`Game.heroes`), any type. It stays one until it dies, so there can be several.
    - Defaults (nothing more specified): "attribute ×3" is every stat a troop fights with: HP, damage
      or heal, defence, regen, MP and its regen, walking speed, reach, and 3× as many attacks (the pause
      / 3). A melee fighter's reach still stops at 1.7 tiles. Splash, shot speed and price stay.
    - "0.3" read as +30%: while a Hero lives every other troop's stats are ×1.3 the same way, troops
      bought meanwhile too. Two Heroes don't give more.
    - HP a troop gains comes with it (a Hero made at full health stays full); when the aura ends with
      the last Hero's death the others' HP and MP are only capped, never lowered to death.
    - Saved per troop. Announced in the message window ("<name> menjadi Hero!") with the upgrade burst
      and the win jingle. Its look can't be an awakening's (those colour the outline, shadow and sparks
      blue / crimson / gold, 53): a white halo on the body and the pack's gold crown above the HP
      bar; the crown also marks its type in the book row and the troop counter. "Hero <name>" in the
      nameplate and the MENANG! popup's fallen line.
    - Balance (an auto-player over waves 1–30 with the capacity of 54, 6 seeds, the same build with and
      without Heroes): in the 4 runs that got past wave 5, with Heroes all reached wave 30 with every
      life and lost no troop in waves 10, 20 and 30; without, all 4 were lost, at waves 15–18, after
      losing 0–4 troops at wave 10. Wave 10 ends in 31–33 s instead of 40–53 s. (The other 2 runs
      stalled in wave 5 either way, before any Hero.) The owner's numbers as asked; from wave 10 on the
      Hero decides the run.
57. **Capacity is cheaper** ("harga nambah kapasitas dikurangin lagi"): +Kapasitas costs 40, then 10 more
    each time (40, 50, 60, …) instead of the old +Zona's 75 + 25 (`capacityPrice`, `capacityPriceRise`).
58. **Every capacity purchase widens the deploy zone a column** ("harusnya menambah kapasitas akan
    menambah jumlah row spawn"; the owner chose "kolom zona deploy"): the zone is 3 columns plus one per
    +Kapasitas bought, at once, still at most 30% of the view (then purchases add capacity only). It
    changes 54's "as wide as the capacity needs"; old saves count their purchases as before.
59. **Troop healers hurt dark monsters by healing them (holy damage)** ("selain heal, healer juga bisa
    menyerang tipe monster dark, dengan melakukan heal ke mereka; jika di-heal sama troops maka akan
    mengurangi darah mereka"; then "hanya 0.8 yang masuk; jadi misalkan heal 10 ke ally, kalau dijadikan
    serangan cuma 8 dmg"). Details are in units-and-combat.md.
    - **Dark** = the undead: every skeleton kind and both necromancers (so their raised skeletons too).
      The bat and the were-beasts are living creatures, so not dark.
    - **Healing comes first:** a troop healer smites only when no ally it could reach needs healing. It
      smites a dark monster already in its range for `holyShare` 0.8 of its heal, and never steps up for
      one (healers stay at the back, 7).
    - The smite is a normal blow (gold, loot, relics), shown as the heal burst in white and silver: a
      heal is green, or an awakened healer's blue, crimson or gold (53), so a smite never looks like one.
60. **Hurt troops fall back to the healers** ("troops yang nyawanya tinggal setengah ke bawah mundur ke
    belakang untuk di-heal sama healer"; formation-and-navigation.md). Defaults (not specified):
    - At or below 50% HP a troop falls back toward the nearest troop healer until well inside its reach
      (half of it), not to the back line, and fights on at 80% (the gap keeps it from flickering). Only
      while a troop healer lives; healers don't do it themselves.
    - Falling back it doesn't chase but still hits a foe in reach; give-way (6) still applies. Healers
      take the ones falling back first.
    - Probe (18 troops with 3 priests, no items, 8 seeds, with holy damage in both): deaths per wave
      0.9 → 0 at wave 5 and 0.4 → 0 at wave 10, wave time unchanged (29 s, 34 s). At wave 20 that army is
      wiped either way (33 → 32 s).
61. **A stalled wave's monsters march on the base** (issue #39, "a boss wave can stall forever"; found
    by the #24 balance probe; the orchestrator chose the watchdog and the message; units-and-combat.md):
    - The stall: a necromancer boss raises skeletons forever (its MP regen pays for every cast). With the
      army down to 1–2 archers, a skeleton is always their nearest foe, so the boss was never shot while
      the necro healer mended it. The monsters chased the kiting archers instead of walking to the base.
      Nothing died or leaked, so wave 5 never ended.
    - The rule: with no progress by the wave's own monsters for `stallTime` 30 s (none nearer the base or
      at a new low of HP, none dying, leaking or spawning; raised minions don't count), every monster
      marches straight on the base, through the troops. They stop attacking, summoning and healing.
      Troops still hit them, and a leak costs a life. "Monster menerobos!" says so once.
    - Not a summon budget: that would change every boss fight, while the watchdog never fires in a wave
      that is being won or lost.
    - Probe (the #24 auto-player, 30 seeds to wave 20, main with the retreat (60) vs the fix): the 21
      seeds that never stall play identically, wave for wave (the same time, lives, gold, score, army
      and fallen). The 9 that stalled in wave 5 now march 97–130 s into it and end it 8–15 s later,
      losing 3–9 lives; with the 1–2 troops left they all fall in waves 6–9. (Before the retreat, 5 of
      the 30 stalled.)
62. **Tooltips in the UI pack's tooltip frame** ("di UI pack ada tooltips, pakai itu untuk menampilkan
    popup item description", issue #38; ui-hud.md):
    - The item, relic, HP / MP and star tooltips and the troop nameplate use the pack's tan panel with a
      pointer instead of the wooden crate. Its text is dark (brown title, green effect line, brown ink).
    - The frame is aimed at what it tells about rather than put by the cursor. It sits above the target,
      pointing down at it; where there's no room above, it sits beside it with the pointer on its side.
    - The message window and the Jeda panel keep the crate: they point at nothing, and the dark crate
      reads over both the field and the pages.
    - Only the tan row of the sheet is imported (one small image). The other six colours are there if a
      kind of tooltip should get its own.
63. **Lives are a bar beside the troop counter** ("ubah jadi bar nyawa saja di samping jumlah troops",
    after asking what the heart next to the gold meant; ui-hud.md): a segmented bar, one red segment per
    life, dark when lost, the lost one blinking white; beside the counter (under it on a phone, where the
    wave meter takes the top centre). The heart and number left the battle bar, and the "Nyawa" line left
    the book. Lives rules unchanged.
64. **Heroes nerfed: 2 attributes ×3, fitting the role; the aura +15%** ("hero terlalu op, yang dinaikkan
    cuma 2 attribute saja bukan semua dikali 3x"; the owner chose 2 random ones and a +15% aura, then
    "tetapi harus kontekstual, kalau troop melee maka range jangan dinaikkan"; issue #41; changes 56;
    units-and-combat.md, ui-hud.md):
    - A new Hero rolls 2 different attributes with the Hero dice from its role's pool (`heroPools`); only
      those are ×3:
      - melee: HP, power, defence, attack rate, speed (never range: melee reach is capped anyway);
      - long range: the same plus range;
      - healers: HP, heal power, defence, rate, speed and range.
    - Defaults (the orchestrator's calls):
      - defence only for types whose recipe has shields (the only source of defence);
      - MP in no pool until troop skills spend it (#10), a one-line switch (`heroMp`);
      - HP ×3 is the most HP, its regen stays;
      - a Hero's other attributes get the aura while another Hero lives.
    - The aura is +15% on everything (`auraBoost` 1.15), no stacking, as before.
    - A Hero saved before this has no rolled attributes: it rolls them on load, so the nerf reaches old
      saves too.
    - The nameplate and a tooltip on the book row's crown show the 2 attributes as the book's stat icons,
      "x3" each.
    - Probe: the full-economy auto-player (capacity, troops, items, relics) over waves 1–40, 6 seeds, run
      on the #24 Hero, the nerf and no Heroes. One seed falls in wave 6 in all three; the other 5:
      - #24 Hero: all 5 reach wave 40 with every life, losing 1 troop in all over waves 10–40.
      - Nerf: all 5 reach wave 40 with every life, losing 29 troops in all (2–12 a run).
      - No Heroes: 2 runs lost (waves 22, 26); the other 3 lose 16–35 troops each.
      - Wave 10 ends in 34–38 s with the nerf (31–38 s with the #24 Hero, 38–47 s without).
    - So the Hero still carries a run, but no longer makes the army untouchable.
65. **The right-edge clamp lets a monster's own steps left stand** (issue #42, found by the #39 tests'
    worker; camera-and-field.md):
    - The bug: the clamp put an entered monster past `rightLimit` back to its tick-start x. That undid
      its own steps left as well as shoves, so once the view glided left past it, it stood there for
      good. This happens whenever the front troop is within 2 tiles of the view's left edge: an army of
      back-liners, or a priest left alone. The monster never came to fight, and even the stall march
      (61) couldn't end the wave. Repro: the free priest alone against one bat in wave 1; the bat stood
      at x 288.77, and the wave never ended.
    - The fix: max(rightLimit, min(its x now, its x at the tick's start)). A shove right is still
      stopped, the view gliding left still doesn't drag it, and a step left stands.
    - The same repro now marches about 30 s after the bat stops to fight the priest (which can't hurt
      it and out-heals it). The bat leaks, lives go 10 → 9, and the wave ends. That is now a test.
    - Normal play: the old clamp also held newly entered monsters for a moment whenever the view glided
      left. In the #39 A/B probe (the auto-player, 30 seeds to wave 20, main vs the fix), 29 seeds' wave
      times shift by fractions of a second to a few seconds from wave 2–3 on. Single seeds flip both
      ways around the fragile early boss waves (2 more lost, 2 more saved). In aggregate there is no
      shift: 19 of 30 reach wave 20 either way, and the total wave time is within 0.3%.
66. **The wake script reaps revived old sessions and keeps worker names** (issue #43, after the daemon revived
    4 old generations at 20:25 on 2026-09-27; dev-workflow.md):
    - Reaping: each run stops an old generation when it is in the state as resumed, alive, not mid-turn, and
      a later generation of its chain is alive. Successors and sessions outside the state are never
      touched.
    - Names: the resume passes the chain's first `custom-title` (the `-n` name), not the listed name.
      - Why names were lost: a resumed session gets an AI title on its first turn, and its display name
        (`agent-name`) follows it. The script then passed that name on.
      - Claude Code has no way to keep the display name, so ListAgents still shows the AI title after a
        worker's first turn. The `[ref]` addresses it.
67. **Every troop type has one automatic skill, paid with MP** ("MP untuk troop: skill tiap troop", issue
    #10; the owner approved the proposed nine as they were: "Setujui semua"; units-and-combat.md,
    ui-hud.md):
    - One skill per type, cast by the troop itself during a wave when its rule holds, for MP and with a
      cooldown: Bertahan (soldier), Tebasan Melingkar (knight), Amukan (swordsman), Hujan Panah (archer),
      Tusukan Tembus (lancer), Doa Pemulihan (priest), Hantaman (armored_axeman, the one stun), Ledakan
      Sihir (wizard), Perisai Suci (knight_templar). No button: the player picks the army, the troops
      pick the moment.
    - The skill's name pops up over the caster; the effects reuse the existing bursts.
    - "di kepala troops perlu ditambahkan informasi MP juga": every troop shows its MP bar on the field,
      in the monsters' style, right under the HP bar (the orchestrator's brief). Under a bar that sits on
      the head it would cover the head, so a unit with MP has the pair raised by the MP bar's height; the
      necromancers' bars got the same order, one layout for both sides. The crown stays above the bars.
    - Heroes can roll MP now (`heroMp` true, the switch 64 left for this): a Hero that rolls it holds 3×
      the MP and gets it back 3× as fast, so it casts far more often.
    - **Tuned down, modest on purpose** (the orchestrator: skills should feel good and matter early, not
      make the late game easier; #36 retunes globally, so every number is a named const beside
      `troopSkills`). The approved first numbers made the auto-player (every type in its build) survive
      wave 30 where it lost around wave 20 without skills; the tuned ones cast every 12–16 s with smaller
      effects. On main with Heroes, capacity and the stall fix (61), 12 seeds: without skills 5 of 12
      runs are broken by the wave-5 boss and lost by wave 7, the rest survive wave 30; with them all 12
      get through wave 5 (0–1 fallen) and survive wave 30. From the same save, waves 10 and 20 play out
      the same with or without them. With the Hero nerf (64) and `heroMp` the same holds; the 7 seeds
      that survive either way lose 76 troops over 30 waves without skills, 61 with them.
68. **The Tas page previews an item's price** (issue #12: "the price doesn't preview its rise"; the
    orchestrator's call, which the owner may veto; ui-hud.md, loot-items-relics.md):
    - The issue asked for the price beside the blue stat preview on a troop row. Since the book split
      nothing drops on a troop row (rows and bag are on different pages), so that preview never showed.
    - The preview went where items now go on types: the Tas page's list. A type that can take the item
      shows "Harga <now> ▸ <after>" under its name, the new price in the stats' old preview blue. A type
      that would refuse it shows no price, only its red reason.
    - The price comes from `Game.priceWith(type, item)`: `priceOf` with the item tried on and taken
      back, so it is the price after the drop, an awakening that item completes included (×3), not a
      second formula.
    - While an item is dragged out of the bag onto the field, the list shows that item's types, and the
      row of the troop under the pointer lights (red when it can't take it).
    - The dead drop preview on the troop rows (blue stats, red shade) is gone.
69. **The Soldier has one shadow on the field and none under its drag ghost** (issue #11, the orchestrator's
    call, the owner may veto: "a double shadow is a glitch"; assets.md, testing.md):
    - The pack bakes the Soldier's shadow into its strips (rows 55-59, colour (83,69,69)), and the game
      also draws its shadow file (the knight's) on the ground. The book cleared the baked one from the
      start; since #34 (53) `onLoad` clears it from the field strips too, which the drag ghost draws, so
      the fix had already shipped. This makes it a stated rule with a test (`test/sprites_test.dart`).
    - On an idle Soldier the two shadows cover the same pixels in the same colour, so nothing showed. It
      showed on an awakened one (its coloured shadow under the brown baked one, the outline round both),
      in its last death frames (the lying body's baked shadow runs past the ground one), and under the
      drag ghost (the other troops' ghosts have no shadow).
    - No other troop's strips have a shadow baked in.
70. **The sky's white top gets a soft blue** (issue #44, "white band across the top of the window above
    the backdrop"; camera-and-field.md): not a layout gap. The scene covers the window on every screen.
    The valley pack paints its far layer's sky as a white haze (its top 160 of 580 rows plain white),
    and the band's crop starts inside it: about 40 px of blank white at 713 px, seen whole on the welcome
    screen and partly behind the HUD in battle. Moving the crop below the white would scale the whole
    band up 18–57%, so the art keeps its framing and a sky blue fades into the haze over the far layer's
    top 22 world units instead (the orchestrator's "fitting fill").
    - Reopened: the live window still showed the band after the fix. The running app did have it (its
      VM service's main.dart holds `_skyFade`), but the two live screenshots, taken 8 minutes apart,
      were the same frame: the walking squad and the drifting hills hadn't moved. The window wasn't
      repainting (hidden or covered; Flutter on macOS draws no frames then), so a window capture showed
      the last frame from before the restart. A save shaped like the owner's (wave 45, 48 troops,
      baseX 52576) frames exactly like a fresh game offscreen: the save only moves the camera sideways.
      The sky now also fills everything above the band's top (`_skyAbove`), and the welcome screen lays
      the sky colour under its scene, so no framing can show a gap.
71. **Shared agent infra lives in `<agents>/`, never in a job dir** (issue #46; agent-workflow.md,
    dev-workflow.md):
    - The mailbox (`reports/`) and the test queue (`testq/`) lived in the first orchestrator's job dir,
      `<a session's job folder>/`. A job's tmp dir is cleaned when its job goes away. That session,
      by then a revived old generation (decisions-log 66), was stopped, and the folder was deleted with
      it (2026-09-28, about 02:00): the reports, the signal files and the queue's history.
    - Now `<agents>/` holds `reports/`, `testq/` (its `PROTOCOL.md` owned by the test-runner)
      and `logs/` (`dev-macos.log`, which the run command wrote to its own `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp` before).
      A `README.md` there lists them. An old session's job folder keeps `reports/` and `testq/` as symlinks to it,
      for compatibility only.
    - The rule: anything another session or a later run needs goes under `~/.cache/`. A job dir is only
      for a session's own scratch files.
72. **Monsters grow twice as fast from wave 16** (issue #36, the owner's pick of the probe's
    recommendation: "+30% base HP / +10% base damage per wave from wave 16 (was +15% / +6%)";
    units-and-combat.md). Through wave 15 nothing changes; from wave 16 every wave adds `waveHpLate` 0.30
    of the base HP and `waveDmgLate` 0.10 of the base damage instead of `waveHp` 0.15 / `waveDmg` 0.06
    (`waveGrowth`, from `waveLateFrom` 15). Shields, awakening and the Hero rule stay as they are.
    - Why: #36 was opened when the late waves were too hard (after shields became defence, #9), but
      Heroes, skills and cheaper capacity turned that round. On main 91ac392 an auto-player (every type in
      its build, 18 seeds) cleared every wave to 40 losing 0.6 troops a wave in waves 10–30, and none
      after. Raising shieldDef, the aura or awakening's HP only made it easier; the late growth is the
      knob that makes waves 16+ cost troops. Probed rates (18 seeds each, cleared wave 40): +25% / +9%
      17, +30% / +10% 16 (1.4 troops lost a wave in waves 10–30, runs lost at waves 27 and 30), +40% /
      +12% 9, +60% / +18% 0.
73. **The MP bar is the HP bar's capsule, in blue** (issue #45, "mp skill barnya pakai dari sprite ui";
    ui-hud.md): the pack's thin white bar with its 1 px blue track read as a plain line. The MP bar is now
    the HP bar's own capsule under it (sharing its bottom rim, same width and scale), filled with the
    pack's blue strip. The pair's bottom stays where a lone HP bar's is, so it clears the head as before.
    Elite monsters already fill their HP with that blue strip, and the healing necromancer (any tier) and
    the necromancer have MP, so a monster's MP is cyan instead: the pack's cyan over its blue, drawn like
    the tier fills the pack has no strip for. An elite healing necromancer shows blue HP over cyan MP.
    Troops keep the blue; their HP is always green.
74. **The wave starts from a button of its own, shown only between waves** ("button next wave di pindah
    jangan di ribbon, karna akan membuat seperti menyatu dengan informasi koin dan wave dan harusnya hanya
    muncul di preparation battle saja, in battle harusnya tidak muncul"; issue #49; ui-hud.md):
    - The Mulai ribbon under Emas and Gelombang became the pack's green button with the white play arrow
      and "Mulai". The ribbons now only tell the gold and the wave.
    - It shows only while a wave can start (`Game.canStartWave`: no wave on, not over), the cheer after a
      win included; during a wave it is neither drawn nor pressable. While paused it shows white and takes
      no press: the brief left hidden or disabled open, and disabled keeps it in place under the Jeda
      panel's dim.
    - Where: the top centre, in the wave meter's band. The meter only shows during a wave, so the button
      hands its spot to the meter of the wave it starts. The brief's example, the field's bottom right,
      fits a 1266×713 window (a 126 px strip right of the book) but not phones: in landscape the strip is
      66 px there, and in portrait the field's bottom right sits right over the gold and wave ribbons,
      what the owner asked to get away from. The top centre is free in every layout, book open or closed:
      the book stays below the band, and the band is the sky over the field (never the deploy zone),
      between the troop counter and lives bar on the left and the pause button on the right.
    - A gentle cue: its rim lights up (the pack's own lit variant) half a second in every 1.6 s, and while
      the pointer is on it. No key starts a wave (none did before).
75. **HP and MP share one box: 65% HP on top, 35% MP under it** ("hp dan mp di buat jadi satu box yang
    sama tapi dari 100% tinggi box itu 65% adalah hp dan 35% adalah mp"; issue #52; ui-hud.md):
    - A unit with MP (every troop, the necromancers) has one pack capsule, 2 px taller than a lone HP bar
      (12×8 instead of 12×6; the two capsules of #45 were 11 tall), its inside split 65 / 35. Units without
      MP keep the plain HP capsule.
    - The box grows upwards from where a lone HP bar ends, so it stays clear of the head; the relic icon and
      the level pips sit at its middle, the crown above it.
    - Colours unchanged: HP green (troops) or by rank (monsters), MP blue (troops) or cyan (monsters), so an
      elite necromancer's blue HP still reads apart from its cyan MP; the HP fill's shade row lies between them.
76. **Every Hero rolls one of five skills of its own; the first 18 are built** (issue #48 branch 1; the owner:
    "setiap jenis troops yang jadi hero punya skill unique random untuk setiap type troops kamu coba sediakan 5
    jenis skill unik untuk setiap jenis troops", then of the 45 proposed "setuju tapi pakai bahasa inggris";
    units-and-combat.md "Hero skills", ui-hud.md):
    - 45 skills, five per troop type, each fitting its role and unlike its #10 skill and the other four. A
      new Hero rolls one with the Hero dice right after its attributes, on top of its #10 skill. Names and
      lines are English (the owner's call); the #10 skills keep their Indonesian names.
    - One big moment a wave, not a second #10 skill: an MP cost, 20–45 s cooldowns, ready again at every
      wave's start. While it is ready and wanted but short of MP, the Hero keeps its MP for it rather than
      spending it on its #10 skill ("saving up"), so the big moment isn't starved by the small one.
    - Guard rails from the design: during a stalled wave's march nothing that moves or holds monsters casts
      (the watchdog stays in charge, #39); no skill makes a Hero untouchable; the boss is never stunned,
      shoved or hexed and takes half a slow or curse.
    - Built as one core plus the skills in branches (2a moves, 2b shots and zones, 2c guards and AI, 3 the
      revive and the hex), with game.dart the shared hotspot: everything lives in `lib/hero_skills.dart`
      (a part of game.dart) and game.dart only calls in from one line per hook. The effect store
      (`Unit.effects`, timed `Status`es) has every hook the 45 need from branch 1 on, so the later branches
      only add skills; only built skills are rolled, and all 45 ids exist from the start, so a save never
      meets an unknown one.
    - Balance, the design's check (the #41 auto-player: full economy, waves 1–40, seeds 1, 2, 3, 6, 8, 9;
      the same dice, only the casting on or off, so the first Hero and its skill match and the runs drift
      apart from its first cast): every run reaches wave 40
      without losing a life either way. Troops lost in waves 10–40: 94 with Hero skills, 103 without (−9%;
      single seeds swing both ways, 33 vs 16 and 4 vs 17, so it is within the noise), total wave time the
      same (10,936 s vs 10,935 s). The target was "at most ~30% fewer": the skills matter without deciding
      runs. A Hero casts its skill about once or twice a wave (the most, Cleave, 80 times over waves 10–40
      with two knight Heroes); Holy Nova and Blessing rarely find their moment with this healthy army.
77. **Auto: the next wave starts by itself 5 s after a win** ("tambahkan auto start wave dan ini di
    prioritaskan"; issue #68; ui-hud.md):
    - An "Auto" toggle beside the start button, beside the wave meter during a wave (so it can be turned on
      mid-wave), orange while on; settings.json keeps it per device, like the volumes. Off by default.
    - While on, each won wave counts 5 s (`autoStartDelay`) down on the start button ("Mulai 5" … "Mulai 1")
      and then starts the next wave as Mulai does. The player can press Mulai early, place troops and use
      items meanwhile. Real seconds: x2 doesn't hurry it.
    - Only a win starts the countdown: not before the first wave, not after loading a save or another game,
      and not when Auto is turned on between waves (the next win does; the orchestrator's brief: "only after
      a win"). It waits while paused and while the Hero splash shows (`Board.holdAutoStart`, for #47 to set),
      stops when Auto is turned off or Mulai is pressed, and never runs after a game over.
78. **Attack rate is no Hero attribute any more** (issue #69, "keluarkan attack speed dari pool attribute
    hero yang di enhance"; units-and-combat.md "Heroes"):
    - `HeroStat.rate` is out of every role's pool. The enum keeps it, because old saves name it.
    - A saved Hero that rolled it rolls just that pick again on load (`_rerollOutOfPool`), like a pre-#41
      Hero gets its roll:
      - with the `heroes` dice, from its pool without its other pick, which stays in its place;
      - a Hero with nothing out of its pool draws no dice.
    - Tests in `test/hero_rate_test.dart`. Three game_test.dart Hero tests changed:
      - the pool test no longer expects rate;
      - the attribute test's archer dice went from 4 to 43, so it still rolls range then MP;
      - the save-order test's dice went from 10 to 4 (MP then HP), which is still out of the pool's order.
79. **A new Hero gets a splash screen** ("ketika ada troops yang jadi hero ada pengumumannya yang di kasi
    lihat ke user", then "ketika hero bangkit perlu di bautkan splash screen beserta skill unique yang dia
    punya"; issue #47; ui-hud.md, units-and-combat.md):
    - It replaces the message window's "<name> menjadi Hero!", which was easy to miss. A first version,
      a banner at the top that paused nothing, was dropped for the splash before it was merged.
    - The screen dims. A tan panel pops in with the UI pack's ribbon across its top (`ui_ribbons.png`,
      newly imported): "<name> (<type>) menjadi Hero!". Inside:
      - the Hero big: its idle sprite with its halo and crown, a gold burst and slow gold rays behind it;
      - its 2 rolled attributes ×3;
      - its own skill (#48): its mark, English title in dark gold, and English description.
    - Heroes now come when every 10th wave is WON, not at its start ("setelah wave 10 baru muncul hero
      baru, bukan di awal wave 10"): `_crownHero` moved from `startWave` to the win path, before the
      between-wave save and never with a lost game. The splash opens once the win's cheering is over
      (or when the next wave is started, if that comes first), and pauses nothing: a first take paused
      the wave, dropped with the move. A tap, Esc / P or 4 s close it.
    - Hotfix: "wave 0" won (a monster leaking in before the first wave, only in tests) crowned a Hero,
      whose skill, on unseeded dice, could knock the next leaker back and flake the lives test. Now only
      wave > 0 counts.
    - At most `heroMax` 5 Heroes alive at once ("hero yang sudah mati maka slotnya bisa di pakai lagi"):
      with 5 living, a 10th wave's win crowns nobody and shows no splash; a fallen Hero frees its place.
      A first reading, 5 per game with a saved counter, was dropped for this before it was merged.
    - A gold ring round the Hero on the field, under the dimming, shows which troop it is.
    - The Auto countdown (77) waits for it, from the win until it closes (`Board.holdAutoStart`).
    - `Game.heroMade` (drained like `casts`) replaces `newHero`: one entry per troop crowned, none on load
      (an old Hero rolling its attributes on load isn't news).
    - The ribbon title, the portrait and the lines are separate pieces, for the Hero skill cut-in (#51).
80. **Hero skills that move units: branch 2a's seven** (#48; units-and-combat.md, "Hero skills" and "Forced
    movement"; ui-hud.md):
    - Shield Bash, Spear Sweep, Guardian Leap, Death Leap, Cavalry Charge, Chain Hook and Spear Wall, built
      on five primitives in `lib/hero_moves.dart` (knockback, leap, drag, charge, brace). A unit being moved
      does nothing else and nobody shoves it; a hop or a charge passes through the others rather than
      bulldozing them ahead.
    - Guard rails: the boss is never shoved, dragged or stunned, and the necromancer never stunned; a mini
      boss goes half as far and is stunned half as long; a knockback never sends a monster past the right
      edge (#42); all but Death Leap wait out a stalled wave's march (#39).
    - Where the design left room:
      - Cavalry Charge aims at the farthest foe 3–6 tiles ahead (none nearer than 3), not the nearest:
        charging the nearest, it would hardly ever run through another foe on the way, which is the skill.
      - Guardian Leap leaps only at a foe out of the knight's own reach, as the design has it for Death
        Leap; a foe in reach it just fights.
      - Spear Sweep counts and hits only the foes ahead (its half circle faces the monsters). It and Shield
        Bash knock back away from the base.
      - The axeman stands still while its hook pulls.
81. **Buttons light up under the mouse and sink when pressed, with a click** ("ui button harusnya ada
    effect ketika di hover dan di click"; issue #54; ui-hud.md):
    - One rule for every tappable (`buttonLook`): disabled shows nothing; pressed wins over hover; touch has
      no hover, only the press. A shut page tab comes out 2 rows; the book's rows (troop rows, the Tas
      page's type rows) show the lit card, and a shade darker while pressed.
    - The buttons use exactly the pack's three looks (the owner, shown the first version: "kalau button ini
      animationnya [3 states] itu state biasa, di hover dan di press", with UI_Buttons.png's first three
      as the picture): normal, hover (lighter, the face 1 px lower), pressed (darker, 2 px lower), for
      every colour (`ui_buttons.png`). The first version had used UI_ALL.png's lit rim (column 4) and
      pushed-in frame (column 11) instead.
    - The press is animated: pushed in for at least 0.08 s (a quick click shows too), then back up through
      the hover look for 0.08 s (`pressLook`), the label moving with the face.
    - Presses still act when the pointer goes down (the troop rows when it comes up), as before. Changing
      that to act on release (so sliding off cancels) would change every button's feel, so it wasn't done
      here.
    - A click: the pack has no UI sound, so `tool/gen_sfx.py` synthesises one (`Sfx.click`, a 45 ms soft
      tock; our own sound, no licence). The troop rows keep their placing / error sounds.
82. **Elites' HP bar is silver: blue means MP** ("ini yang warna biru darahnya diganti dengan warna yang lain
    karena warna biru sudah melambangkan MP"; issue #62; ui-hud.md, units-and-combat.md):
    - The elite HP fill was the pack's blue strip; now it is silver (0xD9DEE8 over a 0x8C94A3 shade, the
      orchestrator's pick), drawn by hand like the higher ranks. The ranks read red, silver, gold, purple,
      orange, and no HP bar is blue.
    - An elite necromancer's raised minions' summon circle is tinted silver too (it follows the HP colour).
    - Monsters' MP stays cyan over blue (#45 chose it apart from the elites' blue HP); it still reads as MP.
83. **The pointer presses when it clicks** ("cursor juga ada animationnya ketika click"; issue #72;
    ui-hud.md):
    - The pack's pointer (UI_Icons.png, already drawn since the cursor went in) has two press frames
      beside its arrow. A click plays them: the first for 0.05 s, the second while held, and back through
      the first when the button comes up (`cursorFrame`), on the same press as the buttons.
    - The pack has no pressed hand, so over a tappable the hand dips a sprite pixel for the same time
      rather than turn into the arrow mid-click.
    - It is the UI pack's pointer, not PixelRPGCursors (the owner had those reverted); the click sparks
      (Pointer_Click_Anim.png) stay.
84. **Ten Hero skills that change the damage rules or what units do** (issue #48 branch 2c; decision 76;
    units-and-combat.md "Hero skills", ui-hud.md): Last Stand, Parry, Duel of Honour, Shared Wounds,
    Whirlwind, Veil of Light, Giant's Rage, Mana Shield, Holy Taunt and Bastion of Faith, as designed and
    approved, now rolled. Branch 1's hooks held: game.dart only lets `Stats._with` take a splash; the rest
    is three new statuses in `lib/hero_skills.dart` (`duel`, `killHeal`, `giant`), read in the hooks there.
    - Small changes to the design's rules, each so a cast isn't wasted or a Hero thrown away:
      - Parry needs a melee foe in reach, since shots aren't blocked.
      - Shared Wounds needs the knight above half its own HP: a hurt knight taking half an ally's blows only
        swaps who dies.
      - Duel of Honour skips the healing necromancer (it mends and never fights a chosen foe) and a
        necromancer raising the dead, as Holy Taunt does.
      - None casts over its own effect while that lasts: Veil of Light and Shared Wounds skip a troop
        another Hero already veiled or linked, and Parry, the duel, Giant's Rage, Mana Shield and Bastion
        wait for theirs to end.
    - Last Stand's no-fall-back is the `holdGround` status read at the top of `_fallBackTo`. When #50's
      retreat policy lands it moves into that policy.
    - Giant's Rage grows the body 1.3× from the feet; the tiers don't scale sprites (the design assumed they
      did), so the scale is its own, in `Board._unit`. A duel and Shared Wounds draw a thin line between
      the pair; the other effects show through branch 1's marks and rings.
85. **The lives are hearts, two lives a heart** ("untuk bar darah di kiri atas di ganti dengan icon heart
    tapi icon heartnya di bagi 2"; issue #65; ui-hud.md; follows 63):
    - The top-left lives bar becomes a row of the pack's hearts in the same panel and place (beside the
      troop counter, under it on a phone). The pack has a full, a half (left half red) and an empty heart,
      so "di bagi 2" is 2 lives a heart: 10 lives are 5 hearts, an odd count ends in a half heart, lost
      lives are empty hearts. No number, as with the bar.
    - The bar's white blink on a lost life became a small pop of the heart that lost a half (1.3×, 0.35 s),
      the brief's "a small pop".
    - The hearts are as big as the counter's shield (16·(k−1)), so the panel got shorter (160 px wide at
      1266×713, was ~195).
86. **Eight more Hero skills: the shots, throws, chain and fields** (issue #48 branch 2b; the owner's approval of
    the 45 as in 76, "setuju tapi pakai bahasa inggris"; units-and-combat.md "Hero skills" and "Special shots and
    ground objects", ui-hud.md):
    - Built: War Banner (knight), Snipe, Crippling Shot and Piercing Shot (archer), Javelin (lancer), Axe Throw
      (armored_axeman), Chain Lightning and Frost Storm (wizard), with the design's rules and numbers. 43 of the
      45 are now rolled, so a Hero of those types rolls from a bigger pool.
    - They are made of four shared pieces (lib/hero_shots.dart): a special shot with its own damage, speed and
      look (so a lancer can throw), a line shot that hurts everything on its path (and can come back), a chain
      that jumps from foe to foe, and a zone on the ground that acts on whoever stands in it. Later skills
      reuse them.
    - Snipe aims by holding the archer's next shot (its attack cooldown), not by a busy spell like a summoner's,
      so the archer is drawn as it is. A zone's slow or might lingers a quarter second after a unit steps out,
      so it doesn't flicker at the edge.
87. **A battle log, over one typed event stream** ("perlu di tambahkan fitur log dimana user bisa liat hal
    hal penting seperti ada pasukan yang mati, troops pakai skill, monster drop item, monster high level
    appear", issue #60; ui-hud.md, architecture.md):
    - **The events:** `Game` emits a typed event (`GameEvent`, sealed) where each thing happens:
      - a troop falls, with its killer's type and rank;
      - a #10 skill or a Hero skill is cast;
      - each item or relic dropped, with the monster's type and rank;
      - a high elite, mini boss or boss comes onto the field;
      - a Hero is made, a type awakens, a wave is won or lost.
    - **One stream for two readers:** the events go into `Game.log`, a ring buffer of the last 200, and
      to `Game.listeners`. The battle log reads the buffer; the telemetry (#64) will subscribe as a
      listener and send `toJson` (versioned: `eventVersion`). Nothing is saved: a loaded game starts with
      an empty log.
    - **The UI:** a pack button with the speech bubble beside the lives (hearts), with a red unread count. It
      opens a panel under the troop counter: newest on top, an icon and a short Indonesian line each
      (Hero skills keep their English titles), and filter chips (Semua, Gugur, Skill, Loot, Musuh, Lain).
      The wheel or a drag scrolls it.
    - It stays open while playing: presses elsewhere go on to the field, and the panel covers only the
      top left corner. It and the troop counter's list take turns.
    - Monsters have no display names, so the log names them by their ids in words ("Orc Rider"), with an
      Indonesian rank.
88. **The mini boss and the boss get a bar of their own, their HP in layers of 1000** (issue #67,
    "ketika muncul boss dan mini boss perlu dibuatkan bar darah khusus di guinya dan namanya siapa jadi
    user tau mini boss dan boss yang dilawan ... setiap 1000HP akan ada muncul x1 jadi kalau boss/mini
    boss hpnya 13000 maka <bar hp> x 13"; ui-hud.md "Boss bars"):
    - While the wave's mini boss or boss is on the field, a bar at the top of the screen, under the wave
      meter (on a phone at the right, under the top band): its portrait in the pack's frame, its name
      and title, its rank in the rank's colour, its HP and its MP. Two stack, the boss on top.
    - A name makes it someone: the wave's mini boss and boss draw one of 32 names as they come (the
      names' dice, so spawns and loot keep their sequences) and carry a title from their type ("Morgath
      si Pemanggil", "Grimdor si Cakar Gunung").
    - HP in layers of 1000: "×N" is the layers left (hp / 1000 rounded up), the current layer drains
      over the next one's colour, and the colours cycle so every break shows; the last layer is red, so
      red means nearly dead. What is over the whole
      thousands is the top layer, drawn full at full health: a boss at full health never looks hurt.
      Up to 200,000 HP (×200) it stays readable, for #66.
    - A mini boss a necromancer raises gets no bar: from wave 20 they could pile up.
    - The bar breaks away as it dies (a flash, a shake, a drop and a fade over the death's 0.6 s).
    - On a phone two full bars would reach down onto the field, so there both go compact: no portrait, and
      the rank and the name on one line over the bars.
89. **Light melee keep near the heavies; nobody is left behind the fight; a marker for troops out of sight**
    ("para pasukan light armor mele yang ada di depan itu mundur jika terlalu jauh dengan pasukan heavy
    armor", and "para troops bisa saja off cam jika mereka tertinggal dan baru lari cepat ketika wave
    selesai"; issue #56; formation-and-navigation.md, camera-and-field.md, ui-hud.md):
    - Measured first (the auto-player with every type, items, relics, Heroes and skills, waves 1–30, 36
      seeds, 1266×713's view): light melee walking in were more than 3 tiles ahead of the foremost heavy
      walking in 55% of the time; the heavies struck their first blow 31.7 s into a wave, 22 s after the
      light melee; heavies spent 165 troop-seconds a wave more than 1.5 tiles behind the fight. Out of
      sight left of the view (the middle more than half a tile past the edge): 6.7 troop-seconds a wave,
      71% of it healers at the back line; never more than a tile, because the back line followed the view
      and dragged the rear along (#61 changes that).
    - **P** (`paceLimit`): a light melee walking in stops `paceLead` 2.5 tiles ahead of the foremost heavy
      walking in, or steps back to that line facing its foe; not while it or a heavy is in the fight
      (struck or struck at in the last 2 s: a first version that let it wait under a skeleton archer's
      shots cost 20% more fallen, this one 10%), with no heavy walking in, or in the stall march. **C**
      (`speedTo`): a melee more than 1.5 tiles behind the rearmost melee in the fight catches up, as the
      supports already did. The marker: an arrow on the field's left edge with how many are out of sight.
    - A/B (the same 36 seeds, paired over the waves both played), old → P+C: light melee more than 3 tiles
      ahead 55% → 2% of the time; the heavies' first blow 31.7 → 18.8 s (7.4 s after the light melee's);
      heavy stragglers 165 → 21 troop-s a wave; out of sight 6.7 → 5.9 troop-s a wave; wave time 44.1 →
      44.4 s; no stalls; runs lost 2 → 2. Troops fallen +11% (0.61 → 0.68 a wave; 90% interval over the
      seeds −5% to +31%, 21 seeds more and 13 fewer): the heavies now fight sooner and fall more (49 → 76),
      the light melee a little more too (570 → 613). P alone +10%, C alone +11%, each within the noise.
    - Shipped: both on (the owner's asks), `Game.heavyPace` and `Game.meleeCatchUp` switch them for probes
      and tests. If the owner wants the deaths back, those two switches are where to start.
90. **Monsters keep growing after wave 26 and gain defence; no unit attacks faster than 0.3 s, the boss 0.2 s**
    (issue #71; the owner: "monster juga semua attributenya di buff tapi maksimal attack speed hanya boleh 0.3
    ini berlaku ke semua kecuali boss, boss bisa sampai 0.2", then "maksud aku bukan minimal tapi maksimal.
    untuk troops dan monster kecuali boss monster yang bisa 0,2s"; units-and-combat.md "Monsters" and
    "Fighting rules", ui-hud.md):
    - Every monster attribute that made sense grows with the wave. HP and damage already did (#36). Walking
      speed, attacks per second and long reach used to stop at wave 26; they keep growing after it
      (`waveSpeedLate`, `waveRateLate` and `waveRangeLate` 0.005 a wave). Walking tops out at +75% and reach at
      +50%, both at wave 76.
    - Monsters had no defence. From wave 16 they gain `waveDef` 0.05 a wave, taken off each blow like a shield.
    - Regen, splash, shot speed, MP and the kill gold stay. Melee reach stays too, as before.
    - "Maksimal attack speed 0.3" is read as the owner clarified: the fastest a unit may attack is once every
      0.3 s (`minAttackInterval`), for troops and monsters alike. The wave's boss may go down to 0.2 s
      (`bossMinAttackInterval`).
      - `Game.attackEvery` applies it after every multiplier: gloves, awakening, a Hero, War Cry, Amukan,
        hastes and the wave's growth. It covers heals too.
      - The book's troop row shows the rate floored the same way.
    - The numbers are small on purpose, because the floor alone costs the troops more than the growth does.
      - A swordsman with its 3 gloves attacked every 0.256 s, and under Amukan every 0.15 s; the floor makes
        both 0.3 s.
      - An archer with its 3 gloves is at 0.307 s, and awakening takes it under the floor.
      - No monster reaches the floor before wave 80.
    - **The #36 auto-player** probe ran waves 1–60, 6 seeds a row, on main 8ba4993 mirrors:

      | Row | Runs clearing wave 40 | Lost at | Troops lost / wave 6–40 |
      |---|---|---|---|
      | main | 6 | — | 0.88 |
      | the floor only | 3 | 23, 29, 32 | 1.73 |
      | the floor and this growth | 3 | 21, 28, 30 | 1.48 |
      | the floor and twice this growth | 5 | 34 | 1.01 |

      With 6 seeds the three changed rows are within each other's noise. The floor is what this auto-player
      feels. Its lost runs end with the army wiped out on waves 21–32; the last row's one runs out of lives
      on wave 34.
    - **The owner's live save** (wave 32, 48 troops, 3 Heroes; variant B, 6 seeds) ran from wave 33 to 80:

      | Row | Runs surviving wave 80 | Troops lost a wave 33–50 / 51–65 / 66–80 |
      |---|---|---|
      | main | 6 | 0.05 / 0.99 / 1.32 |
      | the floor only | 6 | 0.28 / 0.81 / 1.57 |
      | the floor and this growth | 5 (the sixth falls on wave 80) | 0.39 / 1.13 / 1.97 |
      | the floor and twice this growth | 2 (the others fall on waves 75–79) | 0.37 / 1.11 / 3.33 |

      This growth is the one kept. Twice as much walls this army at waves 75–79, mostly against the werebear
      high elites and mini boss. Every number is a named const, so either way is a one-line change.
91. **Any monster type can hold any rank, and the rank shows on its body** ("semua jenis monster bisa jadi
    tier enemy apapun tapi perlu di filter warnanya biar ada pembeda jenis monsternya"; issue #58;
    units-and-combat.md, ui-hud.md):
    - Normal to high elite already rolled for any type; now the mini boss and boss slots do too. The mini
      boss is the necromancer at 1/3 from wave 8 (as before), else any type of the wave's pool; the boss is
      the necromancer at `necroBossChance` 1/3, else the same. The n-th weakest type is n times as likely as
      the weakest (`slotType`), so the stronger come more often. Only the necromancer raises skeletons. The
      slots have their own dice (`Game.slots`), so the rest of a wave is unchanged.
    - Stats: a flat multiplier can't serve both a slime (30 HP) and a werebear (320 HP), so a boss or mini
      boss of a monster type starts from its slot's reference (`slotBase`): its HP and damage a second are
      raised to at least the reference's, at its own pace, speed and reach. The mini boss's reference is the
      wave's strongest type (then ×6 / ×2.2), so the strongest in its own slot is exactly the old mini boss.
      The boss's is the necromancer boss, times `bossTypeHp` 1 and `bossTypeDmg` 0.65. Raised minions are
      never raised to a slot (`raised`, the same flag #66 adds). #66's rank-based boss buff, when it lands,
      applies on top to every type alike.
    - The numbers, from #66's probe (the #36 auto-player, full economy, waves 1–40, seeds 1–9):
      | | runs to wave 40 | troops lost a boss wave | a non-necromancer boss's late waves (25–40) |
      |---|---|---|---|
      | main (always the necromancer) | 8 / 9 | 0.69 | (necromancer: 1.09) |
      | bossTypeDmg 1.0 | 7 / 9 | 1.43 | 2.73 |
      | bossTypeDmg 0.65 | 8 / 9 | 0.80 | 1.25 (necromancer 1.20) |
      | bossTypeDmg 0.5 | 7 / 9 | 0.88 | 0.91 |
      At the necromancer's full damage a second the other bosses killed twice the troops (they fight the
      whole time; the necromancer mostly casts). At 0.65 they kill about as many as it does. The bosses die
      as fast as before (10–12 s on average).
    - The rank on the body (`tier_look.dart`): the sprite is recoloured part way (0.45–0.55) toward the rank's
      HP bar colour (silver, gold, purple, orange) and outlined 1 px in it, so the rank reads at a glance
      while the type stays recognisable; normal monsters are as drawn. The HP bars keep their colours.
    - Drops and Hantaman's stun go by the rank: the boss of any type drops 2 items and is never stunned.
92. **The back line stays behind the rearmost troop, not the view; a troop bought mid-wave comes from off
