    screen** ("garis pertahanan tetap berada di belakang para troops paling akhir jadi, cam bergeser !=
    garis pertahanan ikut bergeser. dan spawn prajurit selalu datang dari sisi off cam"; issue #61;
    camera-and-field.md, formation-and-navigation.md):
    - Mid-wave `baseX` (the zone start and the life-loss line) moves up to the tile edge `lineRoom` 2 tiles
      or more behind the rearmost troop that has entered, never back, never past a tile behind the leftmost
      monster; it no longer follows the view. The 2 tiles leave room for a healer or a kiting archer to step
      back.
    - A troop bought mid-wave starts 2 tiles left of the view or of the back line, whichever is further
      left, and marches in at the catch-up pace. Before a wave, placing is as it was.
    - Mid-wave a troop with nothing to do holds where it is instead of walking to its spot. The spots move up
      with the line, so walking to them pulled the line on after them: the army crept forward by itself.
    - The old line did a job nobody had written down: following the view, its clamp dragged the rear along.
      Without it, in a 36-seed A/B against #56 (P and C on in both), the rear drifted out of sight and 40%
      more troops fell (90% interval +13% to +76%), lives lost 11 → 30, out of sight 5.6 → 81 troop-seconds
      a wave. So the supports keep up with the view themselves (the orchestrator's pick, option A): a
      healer's rest and a kiting archer never go behind max(baseX, cam) + tile/2, and anyone out of sight
      walking forward goes at the catch-up pace (`Game.keepUpWithView`; false is option B). With those:
      troops fallen +8% against #56 (−9% to +27%, within the noise), runs lost 2 → 2, lives lost 11 → 14,
      out of sight 5.6 → 31 troop-seconds a wave (the off-view marker, 89, shows them), wave time the same.
93. **Resurrection and Slime Hex, the rare two Hero skills** (issue #48 branch 3; decision 76; the owner kept
    both, with the revive "once a wave" and its line "<name> rises again!"; units-and-combat.md "Hero skills",
    ui-hud.md):
    - With them all 45 Hero skills are rolled (2b's eight came first, 86).
    - Resurrection brings back a *new* troop with the fallen one's type, name and drop spot rather than
      waking the dead `Unit`, so nothing of its last moments (effects, cooldowns, a retreat) comes with it.
      It joins through `raised` after the update loop, as raised minions do. It stands where it fell but no
      further forward than a tile ahead of the priest, so it doesn't rise into the monsters that just killed
      it, nor on top of the healer. Once revived always revived (`Unit.revived`, saved), so reloading can't
      buy a second life. Troops have no summon strip, so it rises as its death strip played backwards.
    - The revive is the one Hero skill that speaks, in English like the skills ("<name> rises again!",
      where the Hero news is still Indonesian).
    - Slime Hex swaps the monster's `Stats` for the wave's slime's and keeps its own in the effect (`was`).
      Its gold (`cost`) stays its own; its rank (`tier`) never changed, so its score, loot and bar colour stay.
      Its share of HP carries over both ways. A monster killed as a slime keeps the hex while it dies, so it
      is drawn dying as a slime. Also excluded: the necromancer at any rank (it raises the dead by its type).
94. **A Hero's cast gets a one-second cut-in** ("ketika hero melakukan skill di kasikan hilight atau splash
    screen supaya special gitu", issue #51; ui-hud.md):
    - When a Hero casts its own skill, a dark band with gold edges slides across the screen for 1 s:
      the Hero big (the #47 splash's portrait: burst, rays, crown), the skill's mark and English title
      in gold, and "Hero <name>". The field dims round the Hero, a spotlight.
    - It pauses nothing and takes no press, so it never gets in the way of play.
    - Casts queue one at a time (`CutIns`, pure Dart). At most 3 wait, and a fourth drops the oldest. A
      Hero casting again while its cut-in waits replaces it rather than queueing twice.
    - At 1–2 casts a wave per Hero, that is a few seconds a wave. For anyone who finds it too much it
      can be turned off in Pengaturan ("Sorotan Hero", on by default, kept in settings.json).
95. **Monsters have plates too, and a tap pins any unit's plate** (issue #55, "enemy juga bisa di hover,
    ketika di hover kelihatan type monster dan tiernya. ketika di click maka popover di atas troops dan
    enemy jadi permanen muncul sampai user click lagi di luar atau troop/enemy mati"; ui-hud.md "Unit
    plates"):
    - Pointing at a monster shows a plate like a troop's nameplate:
      - its type's name, given in Indonesian (`monsterTypeNames`; only "Nekromanser Penyembuh" had one);
      - its rank (`tierNames`) in its HP bar's colour;
      - what kind it is (undead, healer, summoner, raised);
      - its HP now/max.
    - A tap on a unit pins its plate: it follows the unit until a tap anywhere else, or the unit dies or
      leaves.
      - A tap on the same unit keeps the pin; one on another unit moves it.
      - A drag is no tap, so moving troops, items and relics works as before.
      - A tap on a button still presses it (the button reacts on the press down) and, being elsewhere,
        unpins.
    - The pinned plate is drawn under the HUD, so it never covers the book or a button. It is hidden while
      its unit is out of the view.
    - The cursor turns to the hand over a unit, since a tap there now does something.
96. **Hurt troops go back in when heals don't come; the rest of #50's rule ships switched off** ("setelah di
    heal para troops yang sudah di atas 50% darahnya langsung attack lagi, … jangan sampai mati konyol karna
    harus mati nyerang mulu padahal nyawanya sedikit, tapi jangan sampai karna nunggu di heal mulu sampai
    tidak nyerang nyerang"; issue #50; formation-and-navigation.md, lib/retreat.dart):
    - Measured first (the auto-player with every troop type, items, relics, Heroes and skills, waves 1–30,
      main 027aeb0, 6 seeds). Nobody goes back in straight after a heal at 50–80%: every healed return was
      at 80% or more. What kills is bursts: with three priests 72 of 79 deaths came while falling back, in
      waves 14–28, from elites, mini-bosses and bosses that take a troop from 20–40% to nothing in about
      1 s, mostly before it reaches the healer. With one healer the other complaint is real: 63% of the
      fall-back time is spent at the healer, two thirds of it without a heal for 1.5 s, up to 16 at once.
    - The owner's addendum: every threshold in one patchable, versioned brain (assets/ai/retreat.json, the
      defaults in code when a number is missing or wrong) and the decision behind `RetreatPolicy`, which
      reads a small feature record, so a trained model can take its place later. No model now. The file is
      read in `main()` before the game starts, not in `TdGame.onLoad`: there it slowed every widget test's
      boot (hud_test 66 → 127 s, one boot past its 60 s), and a test's game keeps the defaults, which are
      the file.
    - The rule, A/B'd whole and part by part (the orchestrator: "parts that don't help shipped switched
      off"): **S**, heals that don't come: after 3 s at the healer's spot without one, the one with the
      most HP there goes back in from 60%; **D**, fall back sooner (below 80%) when the damage it takes
      would fell it within 2 s; **L**, go back in from 60% when fewer than 2 melee still fight, or above
      50% when a monster is within 2 tiles of the back line; **H**, hold fire: falling back, a melee troop
      strikes only when cornered; **Q**, a new wave keeps the after-wave heals still to come, and a healer
      ready to heal gives the next of them before its own heals.
    - A/B on main 70dd9c9 with this branch, 36 seeds, one healer (the free priest) and three priests,
      30 s between waves (Q at 5 s, Auto's countdown, 77). Compared seed by seed over the waves both sides
      played, since the better side lives into harder waves. "Suicide" = died falling back or fighting at
      50% or less; "idle" = troop-seconds at the healer without a heal for 1.5 s.
      - S against the old rule: one healer, fallen −9%, suicide deaths −13%, idle −34%, further on 13 seeds
        and less far on 6 (846 waves played vs 737, runs lost 20 vs 22, damage dealt per wave +9%); three
        priests, fallen −13%, suicide −12%, idle −60%, waves, damage and wave time the same.
      - On top of S: H, fallen +14% / +12% (one healer / three priests), suicide +20% for both; L, fallen
        +1% / +7%, suicide +2% / +11%; D (D+S, not paired) 2.12 vs 1.75 fallen per wave and 28 vs 20 runs
        lost with one healer, 0.84 vs 0.70 with three priests. (On 18 seeds of 965ff54 D and H had looked
        good for three priests and bad for one healer; 36 seeds don't hold the good half up.)
      - Q: three priests finish the after-wave heals within the 5 s, so it changes nothing; one healer,
        fallen +17%, suicide +14%, idle +14%, less far on 9 seeds and further on 5.
      - S against the old rule again on main 770122e (with #56's pace and #61's back line, 89 and 92), the
        same 36 seeds: one healer, fallen −22% (90% interval −44% to +7%), suicide −23%, idle −44%,
        further on 20 seeds and less far on 11; three priests, fallen −18% (−39% to +13%), suicide −13%,
        idle −32%, runs lost 8 → 4.
    - Shipped: S alone (`healWait` 3, `earlyReturnAt` 0.6). D, L, H and Q stay in the brain at 0 / false,
      for a patch of the file or a trained policy. What no part fixed: most suicide deaths are still
      bursts during the fall-back in waves 21–30 (one healer 442 → 417 there).
97. **Bosses and mini bosses hit harder and last longer** (issue #66, "boss dan mini boss stat HP dan MP-nya
    di x5 dan x3 untuk mini boss, serta attacknya juga di x3 dan x2 ... sekarang mini boss dan boss ini terlalu
    mudah di kalahkan apalagi kalau sudah punya hero yang awakening 3 dan heronya x3 attack speed dan speed";
    units-and-combat.md):
    - A wave's boss gets HP ×10, MP ×5 and damage ×3, and its mini boss HP ×6, MP ×3 and damage ×2, on top
      of today's values (`bossHpK`, `bossMpK`, `bossDmgK`, `miniHpK`, `miniMpK`, `miniDmgK`, applied by
      `bossBuff` in `enemyStats`).
    - It goes by the tier, so with #58 (91) it applies to a boss or mini boss of every type, on top of its
      slot's start (`slotBase`, `bossTypeHp` / `bossTypeDmg`) and the tier. Another type's boss in full is
      6000 HP and 39 damage a second before the wave's growth. Only the necromancer has an MP pool to
      multiply.
    - The HP was first ×5 / ×3, as asked; the owner then raised it to ×10 / ×6 (through the orchestrator).
    - It ramps in with the wave (the owner's pick of four options): none on wave 5, all of it from wave 50,
      in a straight line between (`bossBuffFrom`, `bossBuffFull`). In full from wave 1 it ended the #36
      auto-player's runs on wave 5–6: the wave-5 boss (about 6000 HP, 90 damage) wiped out or outlasted the
      6-troop army. The owner's complaint is about the late game, where it is now in full.
    - The ramp first ended at wave 30. The owner moved the end to 50 after the probe below showed what full
      from wave 30 did.
    - Only the wave's own boss and mini boss (the orchestrator's pick of the two options): a necromancer's
      raised mini-boss skeleton keeps its stats, because its MP price is balanced against them and the buff
      would multiply the boss's summons too.
    - The MP pool is multiplied, the regen isn't (the orchestrator's pick): the summoner opens each wave with
      more MP for bigger summons, but earns it no faster over a long fight.
    - What full from wave 30 did, with #70 (probes, 12 seeds each):
      - The #36 auto-player (waves 1–40): 1 run clears wave 40, against 11 on main. The others are wiped out
        or stall between waves 15 and 36, mostly at the wave-25 boss and the mini bosses.
      - The owner's wave-32 save played on: it ends at waves 40 / 46 / 80 (min / median / max), against 80 in
        every seed before. The werebear mini boss does most of the killing, then the boss.
    - Full from wave 50 (what shipped), with #70:
      - The #36 auto-player: 3 runs clear wave 40; the others end between waves 19 and 31. Boss wave 30 is the
        worst (19 troops lost, 145 s).
      - The owner's save: it ends at waves 43 / 51.5 / 80. It is still the werebear mini boss (542 troops
        fallen over the seeds), then the boss (160).
98. **More healing necromancers after wave 5** (issue #70, "enemy healer lebih sering lagi di spawn di atas wave
    5"; units-and-combat.md):
    - Two from wave 6 (was 10), then one more every 5 waves: 3 from wave 11, 4 from 16, 5 from 21, and no more
      than 5 (`twoNecroHealersFrom`, `necroHealerEvery`, `necroHealersMax`; the orchestrator's numbers). The
      first still joins on wave 4.
    - They keep their places: after the first and second third of the wave, more spread evenly, and on a boss
      wave the last one behind the boss.
99. **The store, "Toko"** ("tambahkan fitur untuk beli di dalam store dengan menggunakan gold yang didapat
    dalam permainan … ada beberapa artefak yang hanya bisa dibeli lewat store dan itu harganya sangat mahal dan
    efeknya juga sangat overpower", "harga item di dalam store itu sangat mahal dan user juga bisa jual item
    yang dia dapat dari battle ke store, hanya dibuka ketika player sudah melewati wave 15"; issue #63;
    loot-items-relics.md "The store", ui-hud.md):
    - Phase 1 measured the economy the store has to fit (the #41 full-economy auto-player, waves 1–50, 3 seeds):
      about 1.1k gold a wave at wave 15 and 2–2.7k after wave 30. Spending on troops and capacity stops
      growing at about wave 35–40, so the bank piles up: 18k by wave 40, 41k by wave 50. The owner's own saves
      agree (17k banked at wave 32, 38k at wave 43, with 20 staffs, 12 potions and 11 bows in the bag but no
      gloves). The bag also fills with about 90 items no type can take by wave 50.
    - So the store is a gold sink that turns that idle gold into power, and turns the bag's surplus into the
      kinds that are short.
    - The owner's answers to the design's questions (each is one constant or switch in `lib/store.dart`):
      - **Between waves only** (`storeMidWave` false): during a wave its buttons grey out ("Hanya di antara
        gelombang"). The page still holds the auto start while it is open between waves, so the 5 s countdown
        never races the shopping.
      - **Twice the design's prices:** items 2,000 +200 a purchase (`itemPrice`), dropped relics 8,000 +1,600
        (`relicPrice`), artefacts 24–40k (`artefactPrice`) ×1.5 a further copy (`artefactRise`). Prices rise
        per kind for the game and selling never lowers them.
      - **Selling pays half the base price** (`sellShare` 0.5; the design had 20%), from the bag only. Items
        given to a type stay unsellable: selling one would un-awaken the type, a feature of its own (which
        type gives it back, what happens to the awakening), not a switch.
      - **English names** like the Hero skills (`relicNames`): Dragon Heart, Dawn Star, God's Thunder, Grail
        of Immortality and Void Eye; the four dropped relics keep theirs, and the lines stay Indonesian like
        the rest of the book. Effects as designed, one `<name>K` record each. No Midas purse.
      - **Icons:** ui_icons.png's own 16 px icons drawn doubled (`_artefactIcons`); the Raven pack isn't on
        this Mac.
    - What the doubled prices mean, against the measured bank:
      - An item costs about two waves' income at wave 16 (1.1k a wave), and about one wave's late on, against
        5–9 that drop a wave: drops stay the main source.
      - By banking alone the first artefact (the Grail, 24k) comes around wave 36 at the owner's pace (17k at
        wave 32, +1.95k a wave) and wave 43 in the probe (18k at wave 40, 29k at wave 45). At the design's
        12k it came around waves 30–36. The owner's 38k at wave 43 now buys one artefact, not two. All five
        (170k before any second copy) are out of reach of a 50-wave game's whole income (the probe earns 66k).
      - Selling at half makes the surplus real income: every drop no type can take is 1,000 gold. The owner's
        wave-43 bag (53 such items) sells for 53k, which with the 38k bank buys three artefacts. A player who
        sells gets the first artefact well before one who only banks.
    - The artefacts are `Relic` values with `store` set, so the one-relic-per-troop rule, the drag onto a
      troop, the fallen holder's return to the bag and the save all carry over unchanged. Drops pick from
      `droppedRelics` only, with the same dice as before (still 4 kinds).
    - Changes from the design:
      - "Jual semua" is a second button, not a long press: a long press already shows the tooltip.
      - The locked tab is the coin stack greyed, not the black coin, since the black coin became Void Eye's
        icon.
      - No tab that lights up until first visited. The win popup's "Toko terbuka!" line says it once.
100. **The troop skills (#10) have English names** (issue #73; the owner, answering #59: "opsi 1 dan trops skill
     juga di rename ke bahasa inggris"; units-and-combat.md "Troop skills", ui-hud.md):
     - Like the Hero skills (#48) and the monster skills to come (#59), the nine names that pop over a caster are
       English now:

       | Troop | Was | Now |
       |---|---|---|
       | soldier | Bertahan | Hold Fast |
       | knight | Tebasan Melingkar | Circle Slash |
       | swordsman | Amukan | Rampage |
       | archer | Hujan Panah | Arrow Rain |
       | lancer | Tusukan Tembus | Piercing Thrust |
       | priest | Doa Pemulihan | Healing Prayer |
       | armored_axeman | Hantaman | Crushing Blow |
       | wizard | Ledakan Sihir | Arcane Blast |
       | knight_templar | Perisai Suci | Holy Shield |

     - Each name translates the Indonesian one, and none is also a Hero skill's.
     - A troop skill's name shows in two places: the pop, and the battle log's cast line (#60, `SkillCast`),
       which reads the same `Skill.name`. The book and the tooltips show a Hero's own skill. Nothing is saved
       by name, since a troop's skill comes from its type, so old saves load unchanged. An event's `skill`
       field carries the new name from now on.
     - The code, tests and docs call them by the new names. The earlier entries here keep the names of their
       day.
101. **A balancing log: a summary per wave plus the rare events, to a local file always and to a server only
     when the player says so** ("kita perlu buat fitur log yang dapat dikirim ke server di mana lognya itu
     mencatat semua kejadian yang terjadi dalam game supaya kita punya data untuk balancing gamenya ke
     depan"; issue #64; telemetry.md):
     - It listens to #60's event stream (`Game.listeners`) rather than hooking the rules again. What only
       the telemetry needs (a wave's start with its army, every monster spawned, buys, items and relics
       given, the stall march, the store's deals) is a sealed `TraceEvent` family the listeners get and `Game.log` never keeps,
       so the battle log and its chips are untouched.
     - "Every monster spawned" goes in as counts (type → rank, raised minions apart) in one `wave` record,
       with what fell, gold in and out, loot, casts, time and lives. One record a spawn would be hundreds a
       late wave; the file has to stay small (256 KiB, two rotated copies). The rarer events (falls, drops,
       buys, Heroes made, awakenings, items and relics given) also go out one by one.
     - Adapters as for the scoreboard: a JSONL file (always), a no-op, and an HTTP stub (batched POSTs,
       backoff) that sends nothing until a build sets `TELEMETRY_SERVER` and the player turns "Kirim data
       permainan" on.
     - The toggle is off by default, as the orchestrator's brief said; the issue said "default ON in dev
       builds". With no server built in, the default changes nothing yet; flip it when a server exists if
       the owner wants dev builds to send.
     - Anonymous: a random install id in settings.json, a random session id; no scoreboard name, no troop
       names, no device data but the OS.
102. **Monsters of high elite rank and up cast skills: the core and seven signature skills** (issue #59 phase 2,
     branch 1; the owner: "setiap monster high elite, mini boss dan boss punya skill unique juga selayaknya para
     troops" and "boss dan mini boss semua punya MP dan punya skill yang bisa merepotkan user"; the owner's
     answers to the design: English names, high elite and up, the half-HP move for the boss only, stuns on
     troops with limits, nothing struck; units-and-combat.md "Monster skills", ui-hud.md, architecture.md):
     - A wave's high elite, mini boss or boss casts its type's signature skill (`monsterSkillOf`). Raised
       minions and types without one yet don't. This branch builds seven:
       - War Shout (orc);
       - Volley (skeleton archer);
       - Shield Up (armored skeleton);
       - Brutal Swing (elite orc);
       - Bulwark (armored orc);
       - Blade Dance (greatsword skeleton);
       - Mass Mend (the healing necromancer).
       A mini boss or boss casts the same skill stronger. The jumps, the mini-boss skills and the boss moments
       come in later branches. The monster-to-troop effects, moves and looks come from a parallel prep
       branch.
     - **Cooldowns, not MP.** The owner asked for MP on every boss and mini boss. The design they approved
       gives each skill its own cooldown instead (10–18 s), since monsters other than the necromancers have
       no MP, and the necromancers' summon economy (#66) stays as it is. The healing necromancer pays Mass
       Mend from its MP as well. The first cast comes 2–5 s after a monster comes on, staggered by its place
       in the queue, with no dice (the game's `rng` also builds the next queues).
     - **A wind-up warns the troops.** The caster stands for 0.3–0.6 s: a red ring tightens at its feet, and
       its title pops over it in red. A stun, a shove, Slime Hex or a march in that time cancels the cast,
       and the cooldown still runs. That gives Crushing Blow and the Hero holds a job against monsters. A
       hexed monster is a slime and casts nothing.
     - **No one-shots.** A skill's blow takes at most 35% of a troop's max HP, and 25% of a Hero's
       (`monsterSkillCap`, applied after defence). Every number is a named `<skill>K` const.
     - **Taunt works on troops too.** Bulwark's taunt turns troops as well (`_nearestFoe`).
     - **The battle log gets a cast line.** A monster's cast is a line in the battle log (`MonsterSkillCast`,
       the foes chip). The telemetry (#64) sums them in each `wave` record (`monsterCasts`: skill → rank →
       casts). It never passes them on one by one, since a late wave casts dozens.
     - **The stall watchdog (#39) stays in charge.** Nothing casts during a march, and the only heal is a
       burst on an 18 s cooldown.
     - `Game.monsterSkills` (default true) turns them all off, for tests and probes.
103. **The battle log names monsters as their plates do** (the orchestrator, after the docs audit, 2026-09-28:
     one wording in the game; ui-hud.md "Battle log"):
     - The log named a monster by its id in words ("Orc Rider", decision 87) and its rank as "Mini Boss" /
       "Boss", while the plates (decision 95) and the boss bars (decision 88) say `monsterTypeNames` ("Orc Penunggang") and `tierNames`
       ("Mini Bos", "Bos"). The log now uses those two tables too; a normal monster still has no rank word in it.
     - Only the words change: the events and their JSON keep the ids, so the telemetry is untouched.
104. **The HUD pieces keep clear of each other** (issue #74, the orchestrator's integration QA after batches
     1–2b; ui-hud.md). Busy scenes shot at 1266×713, 915×412 and 412×860 (a boss wave with the log open, a
     pinned plate, a cut-in and a troop out of view; the store mid-wave and between waves; wave 15 won) showed
     four small clashes and a bug, now fixed:
     - A unit in the top rows had its plate (pinned or pointed at) above it, up over the wave meter and Auto
       on phones, and behind the boss bars on the Mac. A plate now stays under the top band and the boss bars
       (`_plateTop`); such a unit gets it beside it.
     - On a phone the open battle log covered the boss bars (the second one whole). It now starts under them
       and keeps its 220 px.
     - The off-view marker hid under the open battle log (at the field's left edge, where the panel is). It
       now goes beside the panel, or under it on a phone.
     - The boss bars and the off-view marker now cover the field for pointing and pins (`_covered`), as the
       other panels do: a tap on the marker could pin the troop behind it.
     - A found bug: the field's hit bursts, cast names and gold pops run on the game's clock, so after
       another game came in (Ulang, a save) the last one's stayed up, frozen, until the new clock caught up
       (minutes, after a long game). They are dropped with the cut-ins when the game changes.
     The bigger one, a book opened mid-wave covering the boss bars in landscape, went to the orchestrator
     with options rather than a pick (its answer: 107).
105. **#59's groundwork: #48's effects, moves and looks work monster on troop** (issue #59, the PREP branch beside
     enemy-healer's core; the design and the owner's answers in the #59 report; units-and-combat.md "Hero
     skills", "Special shots and ground objects" and "Forced movement", ui-hud.md):
     - Built generic, with no change for today's callers (the #48 tests still pass as they were): `weaken`
       already counted any attacker; `vulnerable` now counts a blow from the other side, not only a troop's.
       The core's cap on a skill's blow (35%, a Hero 25%) comes after both, so a cursed troop still takes at
       most the cap.
     - `knockBack`, `leap`, `charge` and `drag` take any unit. A charge meets the charger's foes and gains
       `onPass`, for a skill's own capped blow or a stun (`hit` 0 lands no plain blow).
     - **A Hero takes half a monster's shove** (`heroShoveShare` 0.5). The design gives no shove limit for a
       Hero; halving it matches the stun rule (the orchestrator's call). A troop is never shoved or dragged
       behind the back line, and one holding its ground (carried, braced, `noShove`) isn't moved at all.
     - **A troop's stun** (`stunTroop`): the owner allowed stuns on troops with the design's limits, at most
       0.8 s, a Hero half, then 4 s immune (`troopStunK`). It stops only what the troop would start: blows
       its skill already queued with `later` still land. Enemy-healer and I agreed on that: the stun is 0.4 s
       at most on a Hero, and stopping them would mean touching every Hero skill's closures. A monster's Blade
       Dance, the other way, stops when stunned.
     - The looks: a slime's glob (drawn as a green blob, not the design's ice arrow tinted green: a slime has
       no arrow, and a green arrow reads as an archer's), a slime puddle, arrows falling on a zone, a green
       draining beam that can follow its two units (`Beam.between`), and rings bursting out (`Game.rings`)
       in nine `RingLook` colours, which also tint a monster's guard ring (`Unit.guardLook`). A troop shows
       the rings of what monsters leave on it, where it has no icon for it, and a taunted troop a line to its
       taunter.
     - Nothing new is saved: moves, rings and the stun immunity all live within a wave.
106. **Monsters that jump, gallop and spit: Sticky Glob, Swoop, Pounce and Trample** (issue #59 branch 2a, split
     from branch 2 so it goes faster; the design and the owner's answers in the #59 report; units-and-combat.md
     "Monster skills", "Branch 2a"):
     - The four high-elite signatures that ride #59's groundwork (105), with the design's numbers and its
       stronger mini-boss casts: a slime's glob slows a back-line troop's steps and attacks by 30% for 3 s (40%
       for 4 s); a bat leaps over the front and bites a back-line troop 1.5× (2×), healing half of the bite; a
       werewolf leaps onto the weakest troop below half its HP (a Hero below a quarter), 1.5× (2×) and a bleed
       of 0.3× a second 4 times; an orc rider gallops through the troops ahead to the first back-line one, 1×
       each and half a tile aside (1.5× and a 0.5 s stun).
     - Where the design left it open: Swoop needs its troop out of the bat's reach (one in reach it just
       fights); Pounce picks the troop with the least of its HP left; Trample needs a troop 2–5 tiles ahead
       and runs at the nearest back-line troop that far, else the farthest troop there, and stops there
       without a blow of its own (it fights on). Each picks its target again when the wind-up is over.
     - A stunned charger stops its charge where it is, a monster's Trample and a troop's Cavalry Charge alike
       (agreed with enemy-healer; like Blade Dance, a stunned monster stops its skill). A leap in the air
       can't be stopped.
     - The glob's attack slow is a haste above 1, which the effect store treats as the stronger of its kind
       against War Cry's 0.8: it replaces it (one of a kind per unit). A haste that slows shows no gloves over
       the troop; its slow's ring tells it.
     - The three #59 branches (2a here, enemy-healer's 2b, troop-counter's 3) each keep their skills in a
       part file of their own, with one delegating arm per switch and their enum values in a block after the
       core's, so they merge with keep-both conflicts only.
     - Balance (the #36 auto-player, waves 1–60, 12 seeds a row, on the branch after PREP and #50 merged in):
       the runs that clear wave 25 / 30 are 12 / 8 with the skills off, 9 / 3 with the core alone and 8 / 2
       with the core and these four (the median run ends at wave 31, 28.5 and 29). Against the core alone
       the four add nothing the probe can tell (wave 30: 3 against 2 of 12), and neither softer numbers
       (Pounce and Swoop 1.2× / 1.6×, Pounce's bleed 0.2× below 40%, Trample 0.8× / 1.2×) nor Pounce off
       moved it, so they keep the design's numbers. Troops lost per wave played (6–40) can't tell the rows
       apart (2.69 off, 3.13 the core, 2.69 with the four): a run that ends sooner plays fewer of the hard
       late waves.
107. **A book opened mid-wave puts the boss bars compact at the left; its tabs run Pasukan, Tas, Toko,
     Pengaturan** (ui-hud.md "Boss bars" and "Bookmarks"):
     - #74's open question A, the orchestrator's pick, option (b). In landscape the book's room starts right
       under the wave meter's band (so the meter never moves for it), which is where the boss bars hang, and
       its tabs and top edge covered their HP and MP. Of (a) the book starting under the bars (it would
       shrink and jump as a boss came or died), (b) the bars compact out of its way while it shows, and (c)
       the bars over the book (hiding its tabs), (b): no jump for the book. There is no room between the band
       and the tabs even for compact bars, so they go to the left column under the top band (under the open
       log or troop list), where the field shows beside the book at 1266×713 and 915×412 (a long name cut
       with ".." to fit); the full bars come back when it shuts.
     - The owner, 2026-09-28: "posisi tab store dan setting di switch dan posisinya". The Toko tab takes the
       third place (book x 64) and Pengaturan the fourth (x 86), so the pages the game is played through come
       first and the settings last. The Toko tab's lock (the grey icon, "Terbuka setelah gelombang 15") and
       its hover lift go with it; no key turns the pages, so no shortcut order changes. `_Page` lists the
       pages in the same order.
108. **Mini bosses hit ×1.5, not ×2** (issue #75; the owner's pick after the combined #66 probe, "Soften mini boss
     damage"; units-and-combat.md "The boss buff"):
     - `miniDmgK` goes 2 → 1.5; bosses, and the mini boss's HP and MP, are unchanged. In full, a mini boss
       deals ×3.3 its type's damage instead of ×4.4, and the necromancer as mini boss 27 instead of 36.
     - Why: with #66 on #71 and #58 (decision 97's batch-2 probe), the owner's wave-32 army fell at waves
       52–60 in all 6 runs, against 3 of 6 reaching wave 80 before. The mini bosses of every type did most of
       the killing, with their plain blows.
     - The probe (the #76 load, on 4a492d0 against the same with ×1.5; the snapshot of the owner's wave-32 save,
       9 seeds a row, and the auto-player, 6 seeds a row to wave 60): the save's runs end at 58.9 on average
       (median 58, 1 of 9 past 65) with ×2 and 67.9 (median 66, 7 of 9 at 65 or later, 1 to wave 80) with
       ×1.5. Troops lost a wave at 51–65 go 4.1 → 2.4, and the army at wave 50 is 43 of 48 on average against
       36. The auto-player ends at 24.5 against 32.7 (one run to wave 60). The mini bosses still kill most,
       with the necromancer boss now first.
109. **A Pounce is one cast under one cap: its bleed gets what the bite left** (issue #59, the orchestrator's
     call on the cap, 2026-09-28: A, per cast per troop; units-and-combat.md "Branch 2a"):
     - The cap (`monsterSkillCapOf`: 35% of a troop's max HP, 25% of a Hero's) held per blow, and Pounce's
       bleed ticks were capped one by one, so a bite with its 4 ticks could take the cap and more. Now the
       cast reads what the bite took and the bleed shares the rest of the cap over its ticks (at most its
       0.3× a second as before).
     - A tick takes at least `minHit` (`hitTaken`), so a rest under `minHit` a tick gives no bleed at all;
       four ticks of that least would pass the cap.
     - A vulnerable troop's ticks can still pass it a little: a tick is a blow of its own with no cap, and
       Vulnerable adds after defence.
     - Sticky Glob, Swoop and Trample hit a troop once a cast and were already inside it. The core's
       multi-hit skills (Blade Dance, Volley) take the same rule in their own branch.
110. **The last three signatures (Reassemble, Maul, Curse of Frailty), and one cast under one cap** (issue #59
     branch 2b; the design the owner approved with "nothing struck", decision 102; units-and-combat.md "Branch
     2b", ui-hud.md):
     - The first blow that would kill a skeleton of high elite rank or more drops it into a heap of bones for
       2 s instead, at 1 HP, so it is no kill yet. Then it stands at 30% of its max HP; a mini boss or boss
       stands at 50%. Once a life, every number in `reassembleK`.
     - While it lies, only holy damage touches it, and any holy blow ends it for good. The troops' own attacks
       pass it by and go for the next monster, so a heap never soaks up the army's blows.
     - Holy damage is a flag on the blow (`_holyHurt`), not a new damage type: a troop healer's light on the
       undead, Holy Nova and Judgement. A troop healer with nobody to heal already goes for the weakest undead
       in range, which a heap is, so healers are the plain answer (the design's §4).
     - **One cast, one cap** (the orchestrator's call, option A, 2026-09-28): the cap on a skill's blow (35% of a
       troop's max HP, a Hero's 25%, decision 102) held per blow, so a mini boss's Blade Dance (4 cuts on every
       troop within 1.5 tiles) or Volley (3 of its 5 arrows on one troop when only 2 are in range) could take
       105–140% of a troop's HP in 1.5 s once #66's damage reached the cap. Now a cast's hits on one troop share
       it: a cut takes at most the cap ÷ the cuts, an arrow the cap ÷ that troop's arrows. Pounce's bite and
       bleed got the same rule in 109; every other skill strikes a troop once a cast.
     - **Maul** (werebear), with the design's numbers: a troop in reach, a long 0.8 s wind-up as the tell, then
       one blow at the nearest for 2.5× its damage (a mini boss or boss 3×; the cap holds) that knocks it back
       a tile through 105's `knockBack` (a Hero half, a troop holding its ground not at all). Every 12 s.
     - **Curse of Frailty** (necromancer: in practice the boss and mini boss, since #58 rolls no necromancer
       high elite): 3+ troops within 3 tiles all take 1.15× from monsters for 5 s (a mini boss or boss 1.2×),
       105's `vulnerable` monster on troop. Every 18 s, beside its summons (it pays no MP for it).
     - The two looks promised with the prep branch: Bulwark's guard ring in the taunt's orange
       (`Unit.guardLook`), and War Shout's red ring bursting out to its reach (`Game.rings`).
     - With these every monster type has its signature; the mini-boss skills and the boss's moments are
       branch 3's (111). Its `CastBlows` came after this cap and takes it as the blows come; Blade Dance and
       Volley split it evenly up front, so every cut and arrow still lands.
     - Branch 2b's skills live in their own part file, handed over by one arm in each of the core's switches,
       like branches 2a and 3 (agreed with scoreboard-2 and troop-counter).
     - Balance is weighed after the merge (the owner's fast lane, 2026-09-29): a QA cycle (129) replays main's
       saved waves (the owner's save from wave 33, the auto-player's from wave 10) on main and on this branch.
111. **A mini boss casts a second skill, and a boss a moment at half its HP** (issue #59 phase 2, branch 3; the
     owner's answers to the design: English names, the half-HP move for the boss only, stuns on troops with
     limits; units-and-combat.md "Mini bosses and the boss", architecture.md, testing.md):
     - A mini boss casts its type's signature, stronger, and its type's mini-boss skill. A boss casts both,
       and its moment once, when its HP first drops to half. Each has its own clock (`skillAt`,
       `bossSkillAt`, `momentDone`), and the order is moment, mini-boss skill, signature.
     - **A gap between a mini boss's two.** A recurring skill waits `bossSkillGap` 3 s after the monster
       began any, so the two never come back to back. The mini-boss skill's first cast also comes 3 s after
       the signature's.
     - **The moment always comes, once.** A stun during its wind-up cancels it, and it winds up again 1.5 s
       later (`bossMomentK.retry`). So a well-timed stun buys time but never erases it, and it still never
       casts during a march.
     - **What a skill brings in is a raised minion**, like the necromancer's skeletons (Split, Swarm, Grave
       Call): no gold, no score, no skills, and the stall watchdog doesn't count it. The orchestrator asked
       for that rule to be pinned by a test.
     - **Grave Call raises the wave's own dead.** It takes skeleton kinds that fell this wave (`Game.graves`),
       never the necromancer's raised skeletons, at their own rank and 25% HP, their bodies gone.
     - **Three statuses of their own**, so they never undo a troop's or a Hero skill's: `swift` (a monster's
       speed-up), `daze` (a troop's slower attacks) and `soulRend` (MP taken per blow). A monster's line shot
       is a skill's blow, capped like the rest.
     - All 28 are built, eight of them on the PREP branch's troop stun, troop knockback, rings, drain beam
       and zones: Headbutt, Bone Bash, Soul Drain, Slime Tide, Bone Rain, Iron March, Skull Crusher,
       Earthshaker. Iron March's "nothing slows it" is a status of its own, `steadfast`; a boss is never
       stunned or shoved anyway.
     - **The cap is per cast per troop** (the orchestrator's rule): Barbed Arrow's arrow and bleed, Soul
       Drain's three drains and Bone Rain's arrows on one troop share its 35% (a Hero's 25%), through
       `CastBlows`. As in Pounce's (109), a bleed whose share is under `minHit` a tick isn't laid.
     - **Areas are sized by the design's guard rail**, "1.5–3 tiles across": Slime Tide's "3-tile puddle" is 1.5
       tiles round the boss, Bone Rain's "2-tile zone" a tile round its spot. "Within N tiles" stays a radius.
     - **Balance: the design's numbers stay.** The probe was run with all 28 on and off (the same code,
       seeded loads per 112), and a kill attribution put each troop's death down to the cast behind it.
       - On the owner's save (3 seeds), no branch-3 cast killed a troop. In the #36 auto-player (6 seeds),
         one did (a Barbed Arrow).
       - Where branch 3 cost troops, the mini boss had stopped to cast and stayed in the fight, where off it
         walked through for a life. Its #66 blows (`miniDmgK` 2) did the killing.
       - With #75's `miniDmgK` 1.5, the save's runs end at 70 / 60 / 60 on against 67 / 61 / 61 off. Troops
         lost per mini-boss wave are 2.67 against 3.31, and no mini-boss wave costs 10+ where off costs fewer.
       - Split, Unholy Ward, Slime Tide and Last Rites never came up: no slime or necro healer rolled as a
         mini boss or boss.
112. **A probe run of one seed is the same run every time: `Game.fromJson` takes the dice it rolls a loaded Hero's
     picks with** (issue #76; troop-counter found two live-save probe runs of one seed far apart; testing.md
     "Throwaway probes", test/determinism_test.dart):
     - The cause: the owner's save snapshot has three Heroes from before the Hero skills (#48) and #69
       (attack rate among their attributes, no skill). `Game.fromJson` rolls their missing picks in the
       constructor with the `heroes` die, while the probes set `..heroes = Random(seed + 300)` by a cascade,
       which runs after it. So those rolls used the unseeded default: two runs of seed 3 gave the knight
       Guardian Leap in one and War Banner in the other, and differed from the first wave played (33).
     - The fix: `Game.fromJson(j, [rng, names, heroes])` takes the die it rolls with, and probes pass it there.
       The app passes none, so a player's load rolls unseeded as before: play doesn't change. `Game()` rolls
       nothing in its constructor, and `loot` and `slots` are never rolled at load, so a cascade stays right
       for those.
     - Nothing else feeds play. With the Heroes' picks equal (the snapshot re-saved), two games stepped in
       lockstep matched field by field on every tick from wave 33 until the army fell at wave 58 (seed 3).
       With the fix, the snapshot loaded as a probe does now matched the same way to its end at wave 52, and
       two separate queue jobs of that gave the same hash of the whole state every wave. The ruled-out
       candidates: no clock or unseeded `Random` in the rules (the `identityHashCode` dice, `Stopwatch` and
       `DateTime.now` are in drawing, sound, ids and dates only); Sets and Maps are Dart's insertion-ordered
       defaults; the sorts have no dice; `Unit.id` only breaks ties; the probes tick a fixed 1/30 s.
     - determinism_test.dart keeps it so: two runs from the same seeds, a new game and an old save, are
       compared wave by wave.
113. **The heavies fight 20% stronger** (issue #57, the owner's pick "Buff heavy ~20–25%": the axeman and the
     templar lag behind the light melee and die first, "jadi mereka seperti last hope"; units-and-combat.md
     "The heavies' buff"):
     - `heavyTypes` (the axeman and the templar) fight with `heavyBuff` 0.2 more HP, attack and defence (their
       shields'), on top of items and awakening (`statsOf`): a fresh templar has 336 HP, not its table's 280.
       The table and the prices stay; what reads a share of max HP (Bastion's cap, Dragon Heart) grows with it.
     - The probe: rows base / +20% / +25% on paired seeds, the #36 auto-player on 18 seeds to wave 40 and the
       owner's live save (wave 33) on 6 seeds to wave 60. "Stalled" is a wave still on after 300 s, which ends
       the run. On main 29a2902 (with #56 and #66's boss buff):

       | row | runs lost | stalled | mean end wave | troops fell a wave | heavies fell a heavy-wave | heavies' share dealt / taken |
       |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
       | auto base | 11 of 18 | 3 | 33.3 | 2.10 | 0.076 | 4.4% / 28.7% |
       | auto +20% | 9 | 3 | 32.7 | 1.79 | 0.064 | 6.7% / 36.0% |
       | auto +25% | 10 | 4 | 28.8 | 1.96 | 0.071 | 7.1% / 35.0% |
       | live base | 4 of 6 | 0 | 55.3 | 2.73 | 0.060 | 34.9% / 43.9% |
       | live +20% | 4 | 1 | 58.5 | 2.62 | 0.043 | 42.0% / 44.8% |
       | live +25% | 1 | 3 | 58.7 | 2.54 | 0.035 | 41.4% / 44.5% |

       An earlier round on 770122e (#56 alone) agreed on the auto-player: 5 / 3 / 7 runs lost of 18, 0.90 /
       0.86 / 1.15 troops and 0.033 / 0.021 / 0.028 heavies fell a wave; the live save won all 6 on every row.
     - 20% is the best auto row in both rounds (fewest runs lost, fewest troops and heavies fallen). On the
       live save 25% loses fewer runs (1 against 4) but 3 of its 6 stall, so it is not clearly better; 25% is
       one number away if the owner wants it.
     - The buffed heavies deal more of the army's damage and, on the auto-player, take more of it too: they
       hold the front longer rather than falling first.
     - Both rounds ran before #59's monster skills (105, 106, 109) came to main; the buff is not re-probed with
       them.
114. **Healing necromancers' heals don't stack** (issue #78; the owner lost at wave 19 with 4 healers a wave all
     mending the same front monsters, wave 18 taking 104 s, and chose "Keep 4, heals don't stack";
     units-and-combat.md "The healer"):
     - A monster a healing necromancer heals (a heal, or Mass Mend) takes no other healer's heal for
       `healWindow` 1× that healer's heal interval (`Unit.healedUntil`, `healedBy`). The others skip it for the
       next most hurt they can safely reach; Mass Mend neither counts nor heals such a monster, and opens a
       window on each one it heals. The one that healed it may heal it again (its next heal comes as the
       window ends). How many healers a wave brings is unchanged.
     - Not a healer's heal, so untouched: troop healers (two priests still stack on one knight), a monster's
       regen and lifesteal, and the boss moments' heals (branch 3's Second Wind, Last Rites). Branch 3's
       Unholy Ward is an absorb shield, not a heal, and already skips a warded monster.
     - Probe, the #36 auto-player, 12 seeds a side, main 57468de against the branch: before, 22% of the
       healers' heals in waves 15–25 landed inside another healer's window (13% in waves 4–14; counted on 6
       seeds); now none, and the healers heal 20% less (27.0 → 21.6 heals a wave: the skipped heal often finds
       nobody else hurt in safe reach). The waves 15–25 didn't get shorter (+0.8 s ± 0.5 a wave, paired over
       97), troops lost a wave went 2.69 → 2.27, and as many runs reached wave 25 (9 of 12; 8 before). The
       owner's save snapshot at wave 32 (12 seeds on to 50, with #76's seeded load) played the same waves to
       within a second (−0.2 s ± 0.2): there the healers seldom find a safe spot to heal from.
     - So the rule spreads the heals as asked, but the healers' heals weren't what made those waves long.
       If long waves stay the complaint, the lever is elsewhere (how many healers, how much they heal, or the
       monsters' own HP).
115. **3 hearts, and the back line moves up only after a win** ("garis belakang di kurangin jadi 3 heart
     saja, tapi garis belakang di majukan setiap selesai wave saja"; issue #79; camera-and-field.md "Back
     line", ui-hud.md, formation-and-navigation.md):
     - `startLives` 10 → 6: 3 hearts of two halves, a leak still half a heart. A save with more lives comes
       back with 6 (no older save keeps 5 hearts).
     - Mid-wave the line stays put: #61's `_followRear` (the line `lineRoom` 2 tiles behind the rearmost
       troop, 92) is gone, and `lineRoom` with it. A win still moves it up as before: to the rearmost troop's
       tile edge, never back (the brief asked for 2 tiles behind it "as the win rule already does"; the rule
       had none, and since the spots are counted from the line the 2 tiles would only have made the army
       walk back 2 tiles more after every win, so the orchestrator kept the rule as it was).
     - Kept from #61: troops clamped to baseX + `clearOfLine`, the rest in place mid-wave (`_rest`), and
       `keepUpWithView` (measured below: still needed).
     - Changed from #61: a troop bought mid-wave starts 2 tiles left of the view, no longer from behind the
       line when that is further left. The line now ends a wave on the owner's save some 230 tiles behind
       the view (below); from there even the fastest melee (28 px/s) would walk for about 130 s, more than a
       wave lasts. Past the line, it counts as entered and heads for the fight at the catch-up pace.
     - The probe (paired seeds, every die seeded as #76 asks, `slots` too): the #36 auto-player on 18 seeds,
       waves 1–40, and the owner's snapshot (wave 32, 48 troops, 10 lives) on 6 seeds to wave 60. Main is
       main 4a492d0 with #61's line and 10 lives; the new line is this branch, the same with 6 or 10 lives.

       | row | runs lost (on lives + wiped out) | stalled | mean end wave | troops fell a wave | lives lost (a wave) | out of sight (troop-s a wave) | line behind the view (tiles, wave's most: mean / max) |
       |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
       | auto main | 1 + 13 of 18 | 3 | 26.1 | 2.28 | 60 (0.128) | 65 | 4.6 / 64 |
       | auto new line | 0 + 14 | 0 | 28.1 | 2.01 | 12 (0.024) | 141 | 49 / 220 |
       | auto new, keep-up off | 0 + 15 | 2 | 24.4 | 2.17 | 15 (0.034) | 179 | 38 / 300 |
       | live main | 1 + 2 of 6 | 1 | 57.3 | 2.49 | 34 (0.224) | 754 | 38 / 100 |
       | live new line | 0 + 4 | 2 | 55.3 | 3.12 | 0 | 723 | 232 / 355 |
       | live new, keep-up off | 1 + 5 | 0 | 53.3 | 3.42 | 14 (0.109) | 993 | 212 / 328 |

     - 6 lives or 10 made no difference: no run with the new line lost more than 5, so the two rows played
       alike, seed for seed. With the line so far back, a monster that slips past the army is almost always
       caught before it gets there: lives lost fell by 80% on the auto-player and to none on the owner's
       save, and no run was lost on lives. The 3 hearts seldom come into play.
     - The flip side: a monster that slips past used to leave the fight (a life lost, and gone); now it stays
       in it. On the auto-player fewer troops fell (−12%) and runs went as far or a little further (paired:
       9 later, 6 sooner, 3 the same). On the owner's big army more fell (+25%) and 3 of 6 runs ended sooner
       (none later).
     - Keep-up stays on: with it off the rear fell out of sight more, more troops fell, and runs ended
       sooner (the owner's save sooner than main on all 6 seeds).
     - The line far back is what #80's minimap is for: its strip runs from the line to the view's right edge.
116. **The HUD re-laid out: the numbers and buttons at the top left, the wave meter with its minimap at the
     top right, the battle log at the bottom right** (issue #80 and the owner's requests on it, 2026-09-28;
     ui-hud.md "Layouts", "Wave meter", "Minimap", "The top left row", "Battle log"):
     - The owner: "map pindah ke kanan atas dan dia itu dropdown dari meter wave", "gold, x2 dan pause di
       pindah ke kiri. wave level di pindahkan ke dalam wave meter", "log di pindah ke kanan bawah". With #79
       the back line stays put during a wave, so the fight can be far from it: "kita perlu buatkan map untuk

     - The top left row: the counter, the hearts, the gold, x2, pause, and in a wave in landscape the book

     - The wave meter at the top right with the wave's number in it, always (the orchestrator: between waves
