117. **Every troop skill shows a look of its own when it is cast** (issue #81, the owner: "setiap kali troops pakai
     skill tambahkan effect yang berbeda untuk setiap skill mereka"; units-and-combat.md "Troop skills", ui-hud.md
     "Skills"):
     - Before, every cast popped its name, and that was mostly all: Hold Fast, Rampage and Holy Shield showed the
       same `upgrade` burst (the items' sword-and-plus) on the caster; Circle Slash, Piercing Thrust, Crushing Blow
       and Healing Prayer only the hit or heal bursts their normal blows show; Arrow Rain two ordinary arrows;
       Arcane Blast its orb and hit 1.4× as big. Hold Fast's and Holy Shield's guard rings were the same pale blue.
     - Now each has a shape and a colour of its own that says what it does: Hold Fast a steel-blue brace (rings
       closing in, a shield flashing) and a steel-blue guard ring; Circle Slash a blade arc sweeping round the
       knight; Rampage an ember burst, then an ember aura for as long as it lasts; Arrow Rain the archer's arrows
       falling on its targets; Piercing Thrust a teal spear streak through its line; Healing Prayer a mint ring
       over its reach and a column of light on each troop it heals; Crushing Blow cracks and dust; Arcane Blast a
       violet orb and a violet blast; Holy Shield a white ring, a white dome over each troop it shields and white
       guard rings.
     - Built on the skill objects the Hero and monster skills already use, not a system of its own: each cast
       leaves a `Ring` (new `RingLook`s; `Ring.over` a unit follows it), a `Beam` (`BeamLook.thrust`) or a zone
       that only shows (`ZoneLook.volley`) in the game, where the tests reach it, and the UI draws them in the same
       loops. What lasts reads the unit's state: the guard ring's `guardLook`, Rampage's `frenzyUntil`.
     - None uses the Hero skills' gold or the monsters' red, and the `upgrade` burst no longer shows on a troop's
       cast, so a Hero's gold burst stays its own.
     - Cheap with 40+ units: short (0.3–0.8 s), drawn in code with a few ovals, arcs, rects and paths (no
       `saveLayer`, no blur, no new image); only the guard rings and Rampage's aura last, as long as the effect.
     - Play is unchanged: the looks touch no rule and roll no game die (the cracks' jitter is a drawing-only die
       seeded by the ring).
118. **Two troops whose ways cross: the one that goes first walks straight, the other steers round behind it; after a
     win a rank trades spots whose walks cross** (issue #82, the owner: "ini path movementnya masi bug, dimana kalau
     tA dan tB sama sama mau lewat", with a sketch: troop A from the top to a target low on the right, troop B from
     the bottom to one high on the right; formation-and-navigation.md "Paths that cross" and "Walking without
     shoving", units-and-combat.md "Fighting rules"):
     - The cases found, each a test in path_cross_test.dart (on main 5fb76bd 6 of the first 9 fail, the stall
       detector's with its fields left out; the other three pin which side the one giving way takes and that in
       battle main's rule stays; the tenth needs the stall detector, which main hasn't):
       - The walk home after a win. A walking troop bent round another only once it stood right in front, and one
         coming through from behind (heading right, more ahead than beside) went first. The one pushed back came
         through from behind next and took the way, so two back-rank troops (archers, priests, a wizard and a
         priest, two archers swapping spots up and down) swapped it for good and never got home (the probe's
         scenes: none in 30 s); two soldiers got home 0.3–1.8 s late. Remembering who gave way, tried on the way,
         made rings in packed zones (0 waits for 21, 21 for 10, 10 for 8, 8 for 0).
       - Spots after a win: the first placed keeps a doubled cell and a later one moves to the nearest free cell,
         so two troops of a rank could be sent across each other, or two swapping spots along a row.
       - Idle healers' lanes, and the healing necromancers': by placement order, two whose lanes crossed pushed
         against each other and one froze there for good.
       - A kiting archer backing off at the view's left edge was clamped along it and slid sideways into its
         neighbours: most of the long stalls (a second or more) left on the auto-player.
       - A jam of allies that hold their ground (healers mid-cast) held a troop walking home for good.
       - Found by the probe on the way (auto-player, seed 1, wave 14): a wizard walking up the back rank through
         the spot of an archer that kept stepping back onto it was shoved back down, round and round every 10 s.
     - Fixed at both levels, as the brief asked:
       - Assignment: `_uncrossSpots` after `_claimSpots`: two troops of a rank trade spots when their walks cross
         (not when they stand together, closer than `_personalSpace`), or when the other way round is half a tile
         shorter. Pairwise, each trade shortens the whole walk, so it never trades back. `_claimSpots` breaks a tie
         between two free cells by where the troop stands. Healer and necromancer lanes go top to bottom as they
         stand (`_topDown`): the one change to monsters, since the same bug hit them.
       - Local, between waves: who goes first is a fixed order (`_passes`: on the move, then further forward, then
         the lower id), so it never changes while two meet and makes no rings. The other steers (`_steer`): it looks
         a second ahead at the walking allies that go first and takes the first step of a fixed list (straight,
         bent 20/40/60°, slower, waiting, aside) that keeps a body's room. Side: behind one crossing its way;
         head-on, on its goal's side of the other's goal, so the one whose goal is lower passes below (the brief's
         example). `_makeWay` pushes only troops not walking, and clears the way only as far as the mover still
         goes. The stall detector (`_watchStuck`, between waves and in battle): 1.5 s without getting on, then 1 s
         walking through its allies (monsters still block). Between waves getting on is coming a quarter step
         nearer its spot than yet on this walk (`Unit.closest`): the wizard above got on now and then, so a
         tick-by-tick count never reached the limit.
       - Local, in battle: main's rules stay (one coming through from behind goes first, the others only bend round
         it at full pace, `_bendRound`, and walking troops in its corridor step aside). With the between-wave rules
         in battle too, the owner's waves ran 3.0 ± 1.0 s longer than main (6 seeds, 72 waves); with the old kite
         too, 3.7 ± 1.5 s, and the long stalls came back (7 → 72 troop-s a wave). Ablations (dice as then, the boss
         types unseeded) put it on the walking rules: main's back in battle alone brought it to +0.2 ± 0.6 s.
         Crossings in battle are rarer and shorter (nearest picks don't cross, the melee take spots, nobody keeps a
         spot), and main got through them (the probe's head-on retreat: 0.07 s late).
       - A kiting archer's step back isn't steered, and at the view's left edge it backs straight up to it and holds
         there, shooting.
     - Not changed: attack targets are never swapped. The nearest picks can't cross pairwise (if A→M1 and B→M2
       crossed, |AM2| + |BM1| < |AM1| + |BM2|, so one isn't the nearest), and where melee stand to fight is #84's
       spots (spot mates don't steer round or push each other; decision 120). Troops given a post before a wave, or
       marching in, still walk through each other (`arriving`). Monsters walk as before.
     - Measured (the probe, every die seeded (#76), paired seeds, main 5fb76bd against the branch merged with it):

       | Paired, 6 seeds each | wave time | troops fell a wave | stall a wave (troop-s) | of it in stalls of 1 s+ | from the win until all stand on their spots | waves not home in 40 s |
       |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
       | auto-player, waves 1–40 (240 waves): main | 65.0 s | 1.45 | 432 | 60 | 33.8 s | 194 |
       | branch | 64.3 s (−0.7 ± 0.3) | 1.30 | 250 | 7 | 12.9 s | 1 |
       | owner's save, waves 33–44 (72 waves): main | 95.5 s | 2.94 | 344 | 34 | 40 s (the cap) | 72 |
       | branch | 94.6 s (−0.9 ± 0.6) | 2.61 | 293 | 3 | 24.4 s | 1 |

       Main's waits home are capped at 40 s, so its figure is a floor. The one wave left each way is a longer walk
       than the cap (35 s and 43 s walked straight), not a jam. All home, on average, 1.0 s after the farthest one's
       straight walk on the auto-player, 0.5 s on the owner's save.
     - What it does worse: the one giving way between waves waits or slows for the one going first, up to 0.9 s past
       walking straight in the scenes, and on the owner's save the walk home counts more stalling (3 → 15 troop-s a
       wave), which is that waiting (on main they stood jammed off their spots, which the probe doesn't count). A
       troop the stall detector sends through walks over its allies for a second, overlapping them. In battle the
       crossing rules are main's, so two crossing there may still trade the way back and forth for a moment; the
       stall detector ends that after 1.5 s.
119. **Kill gold by rank ×1 / 1.5 / 2 / 3 / 4, growing 5% a wave, compounding, floored once** (issue #83; the
     owner: "bonus wave drop coin high elite/bos/mini boss x2/x4/x3 dari monster biasa, dan setiap wave coin
     drop naik 30% yang hasil akhirnya di flooring ... konstanta 30% ini nanti bisa di adjust", with a sketch
     of compound interest, P × (1 + r)^n; units-and-combat.md "Kill gold"):
     - A kill pays `killGold` = floor(type's base `cost` × `Tier.reward` × (1 + `killGoldGrowth`)^(wave − 1)),
       floored once at the end. The ranks were ×1 / 2 / 3 / 5 / 10 and the gold never grew with the wave.
     - After seeing what 30% does (×146 at wave 20, ×27,900 at wave 40) the owner chose `killGoldGrowth` 5% to
       start (one named constant, to be tuned) and the elite ×1.5 (high elite 2, mini boss 3, boss 4 as asked).
     - The win's bonus (`waveBonus` 20 + 10n) and the score read no `Tier.reward`, so they are unchanged.
     - Measured (issue #83's probes, main c2f9273 against the branch). What a wave's whole spawn queue pays if
       every monster is killed, mean of 100 seeds a wave (no fight involved, so it reaches wave 50):

       | Kill gold a wave | w5 | w10 | w15 | w20 | w30 | w40 | w50 |
       |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
       | main (×1/2/3/5/10, flat) | 210 | 433 | 780 | 971 | 1,567 | 1,783 | 2,166 |
       | new ranks, r = 0 | 122 | 273 | 508 | 691 | 1,119 | 1,314 | 1,607 |
       | r = 3% | 132 | 343 | 759 | 1,198 | 2,614 | 4,152 | 6,825 |
       | **r = 5% (chosen)** | 143 | 410 | 984 | 1,730 | 4,589 | 8,815 | 17,575 |
       | r = 10% | 174 | 641 | 1,924 | 4,220 | 17,785 | 54,294 | 172,217 |

       From wave 5 the new ranks alone pay 26–42% less (the necromancer boss 400 → 160 before growth). At 5% the kills pay
       less than before up to about wave 10 (w5 ×0.68, w10 ×0.95), then more: ×1.26 at 15, ×1.78 at 20, ×2.9 at
       30, ×4.9 at 40, ×8.1 at 50.
     - The #41 full-economy auto-player (6 seeds, waves 1–50, every die seeded; its runs end where the army
       falls, main's at waves 20–31):

       | | Army full (48) at wave | The Grail's 24,000 banked after wave | Runs to wave 50 | Mean last wave |
       |---|---|---|---|---|
       | main | 20, 23 (4 runs fell first) | never (no run passed 31) | 0 of 6 | 26.5 |
       | r = 3% | 20–25 (4 of 6) | 35, 44 (2 of 6) | 1 of 6 | 33.7 |
       | **r = 5%** | 18–22 (5 of 6) | 28, 29, 33 (3 of 6) | 2 of 6 | 37.0 |
       | r = 10% | 16–20 (6 of 6) | 22–25 (6 of 6) | 1 of 6 | 35.5 |

       More gold kept more runs going, but the seeds are far apart (one r = 3% run fell at 15), so only the gold
       figures are firm, not the waves reached.
120. **Melee troops take one of eight spots round a monster; a monster fights the troop in its way** (issue #84, the
     owner: "ai enemy aku liat milih menerobos troops dari pada hit ini tidak expected sih. harusnya para enemy
     memukul mundur troops. serta para troops harus mencari posisi supaya mereka dapat melakukan hit enemy ...";
     then, through the orchestrator: eight spots like a compass, sized to the monster and the reach, the front ones
     filled first; formation-and-navigation.md "Where melee stand to fight", units-and-combat.md "Fighting rules"):
     - Why monsters went through (a probe on main c2f9273 that traced every monster's moves): not the stall march
       (none in the owner's 79 logged waves), and seldom past the whole melee line (0.17 a wave on the auto-player,
       mostly Swoop). What the owner saw is monsters getting past single troops: 40 a wave on the auto-player, 200
       on the owner's 48-troop save. About 90% were the monster's own walk: it went for its nearest troop, often a
       heavy walking up behind the line, and walked past a knight that stood fighting 12–16 px from its way, just
       out of its 12 px reach. The rest: shoves by other monsters and by troops, and the skills (Swoop, Pounce,
       Trample). And a bug: a monster walked at its troop's centre, so every step went into the troop's body; the
       separation pushed the troop back, and a hair out of reach the monster stepped in again. It drove troops back
       without a blow (a knight 29 px in 5 s in a test).
     - Monsters now: go for the first troop their way runs into (less than a body off it), not one behind it; walk
       only to the edge of their reach; and one walking up behind a monster that stands takes the whole push and
       slides round it. A troop in reach (`reaches`) counts within 0.01 px: the separation parts bodies to exactly 12,
       a melee unit's reach. So monsters drive troops back only by fighting (a hurt troop falls back, a fallen one
       leaves a gap). Skills (Trample, Swoop, Pounce, the knockbacks) and the stall march still pass through.
     - Melee troops now take a spot (`spotCount` 8, `spotFill`: the front, then front-top/bottom, top/bottom,
       back-top/bottom, the back), at their reach from the monster; if its spots are all taken, the nearest monster
       with a free one; if none, they wait 1.5 tiles behind the front spot. They go round the monster a body outside
       their reach and step in lined up with the spot; spot mates don't shove, step aside for or steer round each
       other. Long range, healers and hurt troops keep their rules; the catch-up and the light melee's pace too.
     - Measured, paired seeds, every die seeded (#76), main c2f9273 against the branch (engage-ai's probes):

       | | runs lost (lives + wiped) / capped | end wave: later / sooner / same | troops fell a wave | lives lost a wave | wave time | monsters past a troop a wave |
       |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
       | auto-player, 12 seeds, waves 1–40: main | 2 + 9 / 0 | | 1.22 | 0.018 | 47.1 s | 39 |
       | branch | 1 + 5 / 2 | 6 / 3 / 3 | 0.99 (−19%) | 0 | 48.3 s (+3%) | 20 (−49%) |
       | owner's save, 6 seeds, waves 33–60: main | 1 + 4 / 1 | | 2.33 | 0 | 110 s | 205 |
       | branch | 1 + 2 / 1 | 3 / 0 / 3 | 2.18 (−6%) | 0 | 115 s (+4%) | 96 (−53%) |

       Per wave figures are over the waves both runs won. Mean end wave: auto-player 25.2 → 32.3 (4 runs reach wave
       40, main 1), owner's save 56.0 → 57.8. Monsters behind the whole melee line stay rare (0.15 → 0.16, 0.03 →
       0.01 a wave): those are the skills.
     - The two capped auto-player runs (the probe stops a wave at 300 s) are wave 30, which main lost outright on
       those seeds: every melee troop fell, the archers kited the boss and the mini boss while five healing
       necromancers healed them from beyond the view, and the stall march (#39) began at 240 s, with the back line
       far behind (#79). The rules behind that are older than this change.
     - What it does worse: troops fill the nearest monster's spots before another's, so in a fight on two monsters
       most may stand round one. When the few on the other fall back, that monster has no fresh troop near and
       follows them to the healer, hitting them as they go (a monster with nobody else near did that before too).
       In a test fight of 8 melee on two elites that nobody could kill, both sides struck the same blows for the
       same damage and every melee troop fell by 18 s on main and on the branch; but the first fell at 7.6 s, not
       10.4 s, since on main each monster's next blow found a fresh troop in the crowd in front of it.
121. **A popup over the troop instead of rings, and loot stays in hand** (issue #86; the owner: "ketika assign item
     ganti yellow ring dengan popup ketika user hover troops", then "begitu juga red ring", and "ketika item punya
     lebih dari 1 user bisa assign berkali kali tanpa harus klik item lagi terus klik troops lagi"; ui-hud.md "Loot
     in hand and the drop popup", loot-items-relics.md):
     - Before, a dragged item ringed every troop of the type it would go to (amber, red when it couldn't take it)
       and a dragged relic the troop under it (yellow): it said which, not what. Now nothing is drawn on the troops;
       one popup in the tooltip frame over the troop under the pointer says what the drop would do. An item: "Semua
       <type> (<n>)" (it goes to every troop of the type), each stat before → after, the kind's taken/cap, and the
       awakening it counts toward. A relic: that troop's name and type and the relic's effect. Or, in red, why not
       (the book's `refusalNames`; "Sudah memegang <relic>"), with no before → after.
     - Its words are `Game.assignPreview` (with `StatKind`, `statName`), written once for both this popup and the
       book's troop lists of #87 (the book-assign worker's commit, shared by cherry-pick), so the two never disagree.
     - Loot stays in hand: picked with a tap on its slot (relics too now), or kept after a drop, the next copy goes
       with each tap (or drop) on a troop until the bag runs out; a refusal keeps it. Esc, a right click, a tap on
       bare ground or its slot put it back. The brief's list of ends also had "the target refuses"; the orchestrator
       settled that a refused drop keeps it (its own message). "x<n>" at the pointer counts what the bag holds.
     - Placement: like a unit's plate, but pointing at the troop and the loot at the pointer together, so it never
       covers the pointer (with a finger both sit 28 px above it); above, left, right or below, centred or lined up
       with an edge, whichever overlaps #74's HUD least. It may reach up to the top rows, not only to a plate's
       floor under the map and the boss bars: on a phone that floor is where the open log starts. The pinned plate
       hides while loot is held (the pin stays), so the two never stack.
     - Two small rule changes the orchestrator agreed to: a drop or tap over the HUD (the book, a button, the log,
       the boss bars) no longer reaches a troop hidden under it, since no popup can show there; and a refusal on the
       field no longer opens the message window over the popup that already says why.
     - Found on the way: Flame 1.38's drag updates put the pointer one move ahead (`localEndPosition` adds the
       update's delta to the new position again), so a drop landed where the pointer was heading. Drags now sum the
       deltas (`Board._dragPos`), which moving a troop and the battle log's drag-scroll share.
122. **A picked relic or item lists who takes it, under a sticky troop filter** (issue #87, the owner: "ketika user
     klik artefak di ui book sebelah kanan langsung berisi list para troops dan di bagian atasnya ada filter
     troopsnya yang tidak tereset otomatis jika item lain di pilih"; ui-hud.md "Tas", loot-items-relics.md "What a
     gift would do"):
     - Before, a relic could only be dragged onto a troop on the field (a tap only said "Seret ke pasukan di
       medan"), and the item list closed after one use. Now a tap on a relic picks it like an item, and the right
       page lists every living troop, with its name, type, level, the relic it holds and its HP. A troop holding
       one is greyed: "Sudah memegang <relic>", one relic each (decision 34). An item lists every type, with its
       count, the stat before ▸ after, the price, its taken/cap and the awakening's progress.
     - The pick stays after each gift while the bag holds more, so several troops take it one tap each: the
       owner's multi-assign (#86).
     - The filter is multi-select (the orchestrator's choice of the options): "Semua" plus a chip per type with
       its sprite, several at once, none meaning all. So "archers and wizards" is two taps, and a single type is
       still one.
     - It is sticky as the owner asked: another pick doesn't reset it, and neither do a turned page, the book
       shutting and opening, or a new game. Only the player's own taps change it. It isn't saved.
     - One preview for both sides (`Game.assignPreview`): the book's rows and the field's popup (#86, drag-popup)
       say the same things in the same words. It was agreed between the two workers and cherry-picked by both.
     - The rows give on tap UP, so a drag on the list scrolls it (like the battle log) without giving.
     - On phones the book is still two pages, so the list stays on the right page. It gets four lines a row and two
       rows of chips there (the brief assumed a one-column book; the orchestrator keeps the right page until the
       owner says otherwise).
123. **The view's centre is the battle point: where the troops and the monsters meet** (issue #85, the owner:
     "center cam adalah battle field. battle field adalah titik pertemuan antara troops dengan enemy"; before that,
     "the battle must always be mid-screen"; camera-and-field.md "Camera", ui-hud.md, formation-and-navigation.md):
     - Supersedes the camera part of decision 11, and amends 65 (the clamp is unchanged, but the view it clamps to
       now sits on the fight), 92 and 115 (the keep-up floors follow a view centred on the fight).
     - Before: the view centred (front troop x + leftmost *entered* monster x)/2 while both sides had someone on
       screen, else the rest view. One troop running ahead, a bat that swooped behind the line or a monster that
       slipped past dragged it; every lull flipped it ~9 tiles to the rest view and back; and a monster waiting off
       screen never entered, because `rightLimit` settled on the troops.
     - Now (lib/battle_focus.dart, from a design workflow: a camera map, three designs, two judges, a synthesis;
       the spec's base is the contact centroid): every unit whose nearest foe is within its reach + half a tile
       marks the midpoint of the pair (a shooter half weight, a rank's monster more); melee points 3+ tiles apart
       are separate fights, a shooter joins its target's; the heaviest fight is centred, and another takes over
       only when 1.5× as heavy for 0.75 s. Without a fight the view holds (1 s after a contact, with no monster
       alive, with no troop entered), slides with the troop front toward the next meeting, or follows the pursuit.
       It glides at most 6 tiles/s, ignoring moves under half a tile; after a win it holds through the cheer, then
       glides back once. The camera never reads `entered`, so monsters enter before they meet the troops.
     - The owner's two open choices take their defaults, each one const away: before the sides touch the view
       slides with our front, a tile left of centre (`approachFollowsFront`; false = jump to the predicted meeting
       point); with two fights the bigger one (`fightPick`; `FightPick.frontMost` = always the front-most).
     - A troop bought mid-wave is `joining` until it fights or reaches the others' front, so a mass buy 2 tiles
       left of the view doesn't drag the front back. Monsters spawn at least 4 tiles ahead of the foremost troop
       (`spawnClear`). The minimap's gold line is the fight shown (`fightX`).
     - Three deviations from the spec, each forced by the probe:
       1. **`reachPull`.** The spec took an archer's point to pull the centre a tile at most, but bows stack ×1.2
          each with no cap for shooters, and a late army's archers shoot from 15–20 tiles. In a trace (the
          auto-player, seed 6, wave 36: 48 troops, 20 archers ~300 px behind the melee) their midpoints pulled the
          view 5–7 tiles back off the melee line, which then sat on the right limit, and new monsters entered late.
          So a contact point is never more than `reachPull` 2.5 tiles from its foe; a base archer's or wizard's
          point is still the plain midpoint.
       2. **The healer's back-off keeps to the right limit.** On main 5fb76bd, 3 of 12 auto-player runs stalled at
          wave 30 (main: 1). The healing necromancers waited right of `rightLimit`, not yet entered, so the #42
          clamp never held them; a late archer reached into their margin, and their back-off walked them right with
          no end. The mini boss they kept healing followed the archer, and the whole fight drifted off the right of
          the screen until the probe's 300 s cap. Main hid it: its view followed the foremost troop, and
          `rightLimit` with it. The back-off now keeps to max(`rightLimit`, where it stands), the cap a knock-back
          puts on monsters; their rest spot already kept to it (formation-and-navigation.md).
       3. **`spawnLead` and `keepUpInset`.** The spec left the rules the view bounds as they were (the spawn point,
          #61's keep-up floor and catch-up trigger), taking the old view to be centred on the fight too ("the same
          as today in a centred fight"). It wasn't: its centre was halfway between the *foremost* troop and the
          nearest monster, and the foremost troop leads the clash by about 3 tiles, so it sat about 1.5 tiles ahead
          of the fight. Centred on the fight, monsters spawned 1.7 tiles nearer the troops and the supports could
          hang 2 tiles further back, and more troops fell: the auto-player lost 10 of 18 runs (main 7 + 1 stall),
          2.58 troops a wave (main 2.09). So a monster now spawns `spawnLead` 2 tiles further past the right edge,
          and once the wave has shown a fight the keep-up floor and the catch-up trigger sit `keepUpInset` 2 tiles
          inside the left edge (`keepUpShift`). Before the first fight the floor stays at the edge: the old view was
          then the rest view, further back than the approach's, as the spec's analysis of the approach has it.
          #82's kiting hold (decision 118) holds at that floor, so it moves in with it too.
          The right limit stays 2 tiles inside the right edge: moved alone it changed nothing, and a monster held
          at the very edge would be half off screen.
     - How that was weighed. Whole runs are too chaotic for it: one purchase apart they part ways, and a variant
       that read main's old view for every view-bound rule (the same fighting as main, to a replay) still ended
       differently. So the probe saved main's army before every wave of the auto-player (17 seeds; seed 14 is out
       at wave 8) and played each saved wave on every variant from the same save with the same dice, 1–6 dice a
       wave. Troops fell a wave, each variant against main, dice averaged per saved wave (SE over the waves):

       | waves (saves × dice), view | main | branch before the fix | every view-bound rule on main's view (1 die) | main's spawn only (1 die) | main's keep-up only (1 die) | main's right limit only (1 die) | 1.5 tiles (1 die) | **2 tiles (this)** |
       |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
       | 14–27 (238 × 3), Mac | 1.76 | +0.28 (0.06) | +0.03 (0.05) | +0.15 (0.11) | +0.14 (0.10) | +0.28 (0.12) | +0.21 (0.15) | **+0.04 (0.06)** |
       | 14–27 (125 × 2), phone | 3.68 | +0.41 (0.20) | | | | | | **−0.23 (0.24)** |
       | 3–13 (193 × 3), Mac | 0.21 | | | | | | | **−0.04 (0.02)** |
       | 28–36 (137 × 6), Mac | 5.49 | | | | | | | **−0.01 (0.15)** |

       The fix plays each saved wave like main. On the Mac rows (14–27, 3–13, 28–36) it lost 0 / 15 / 30 lives
       against main's 0 / 19 / 43, was wiped 1 / 5 / 31 times against 0 / 3 / 28, and hit the 300 s cap 0 / 0 / 3
       times against 0 / 0 / 2.
     - The spec's probe (paired seeds, every die seeded as #76 asks, `slots` too; before = main 5fb76bd, after =
       this branch; the meter is the same code on both: the heaviest fight by the contact points, after every tick;
       the Mac window 341 px wide, the phone 208):

       | | auto-player, 36 seeds, waves 1–40: main | branch | owner's save, 6 seeds, 33–60: main | branch | auto-player on a phone, 6 seeds: main | branch |
       |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
       | fight in the view's middle third | 93.0% | **96.1%** | 87.6% | 88.4% | 90.8% | **97.1%** |
       | fight within a tile of the centre | 31.8% | **75.0%** | 42.3% | 46.6% | 64.9% | **87.4%** |

       | "lull-lock" ticks (all runs) | 42811 | 17595 | 39395 | 13889 | 9473 | 2956 |
       | runs lost (lives + wiped) / capped | 1 + 16 / 2 | 2 + 20 / 3 | 0 + 1 / 0 | 0 + 0 / 1 | 1 + 5 / 0 | 0 + 6 / 0 |
       | end wave: mean; branch later / sooner / same | 32.4 | 30.9; 9 / 14 / 13 | 60.0 | 60.0; 0 / 0 / 6 | 20.0 | 21.5; 2 / 1 / 3 |

       | battle point's mode (share of the wave) | | contact 88%, approach 7%, hold 4% | | contact 97%, hold 3% | | contact 86%, approach 8%, hold 6% |

     - Against the spec's bar: the centring, the 1 s move, the swings and reversals, and out of sight pass on the
       auto-player and the phone. On the owner's save the view moves far less (swings −39%, reversals −67%) but is
       no more often centred (88%): that army clears a clash in a moment and the next contact forms several tiles
       on, where the view, at its 6 tiles/s, is still gliding (80–85% in waves 33–39, 88–94% from wave 50).
       `focusSpeed` is the lever if the owner wants it to keep up rather than glide. "Lull-lock" (a monster not
       yet on screen while the foremost troop is within a tile of the right limit) is down 60–70% but not 0: with
       the view on the fight a troop that chases on reaches the right limit. More monsters stand at the right
       limit, which sits nearer the fight than on the old view (that led it); the clamp moves one less often on
       the auto-player and the phone, far more often on the owner's save, where the knockbacks of a late army
       push against it. Monsters come on 0.9 s later, the 2 tiles of `spawnLead`.
     - Balance: the auto-player's runs end 1.5 waves sooner with 5 more lost of 36, past the spec's bar (1 of 18,
       ±1 wave), but the replays play every saved wave as main does, and the runs split 14 / 9 (13 the same), which
       36 chaotic runs can't tell from chance (the same probe put the branch *before* the fix at 9 / 2). The
       owner's save loses none (main 1); its wave-60 cap is a 400-tile chase main finished at 539 s of 600.
124. **Awakened troops learn a skill of their type, and it costs MP** (issue #88, the owner: "ketika troops awekening
     troops juga dapat skill baru"; the design is the #88 phase 1 report; units-and-combat.md "Awakening skills",
     loot-items-relics.md "Awakening", ui-hud.md "Skills"):
     - The owner's answers (2026-09-29): one skill per type that grows, not a new skill each level. Bangkit 1
       unlocks it, and Bangkit 2 and 3 make it stronger ("Disarm", "Disarm II", "Disarm III"). The nine names are
       the design's. A type that awakens mid-wave has its skill ready at once, its troops 0–3 s apart. And the
       skills **use MP**, where the design had 0 MP and a cooldown only.
     - **The cost** is 40% of the type's MP pool at its level (`awakenCost`), after awakening's +25% a level. It is
       10 / 12 / 14 MP for the 25-MP types and 40 / 48 / 56 for the wizard. Every type gets 5% of its pool back a
       second, so a cast is 8 s of regen for every type at every level: no type's skill is cheaper by the accident
       of its pool. A full pool (a wave's start) pays for the #10 skill and the awakening skill once each (the #10
       skills cost 60% of the pool or less at L1).
     - **Who gets the MP.** Each tick the order is the Hero skill, then the #10 skill, then the awakening skill,
       one cast a tick. When the MP pays for only one of the last two, the awakening skill has first claim: the #10
       skill waits while the awakening skill is ready and wanted and the rest wouldn't pay for it
       (`_savingForAwaken`), as a Hero saves for its Hero skill (`_savingUp`). Without that rule the soldier,
       knight, lancer and axeman would never cast theirs in a long fight. Their #10 skill (15 of 25 MP) already
       uses all their regen, so the pool never refills past the #10 cost. With it, each gets its awakening skill
       about once a cooldown and the #10 skill the rest. The priest and the wizard pay for both from spare regen.
       When the MP pays for both, the #10 skill casts first and the awakening skill on the next tick, as the
       design had it. The order is deterministic, with no dice (#76).
     - **The cooldowns** are the design's minus 2 s, 22 / 20 / 18 s for Disarm and Unbroken and 22 s for
       Consecration. The MP now spaces the casts too, and in a long fight a low-MP type waits for its 8 s of MP
       after the cooldown anyway. A cooldown equal to the design's would have cast less often than the design
       weighed.
     - **The other MP rules** stay as they are, reading the one pool:
       - `_savingUp` now also holds the awakening skill, so a Hero saving for its Hero skill spends on neither.
       - Gift of Mana counts a troop short of MP when it lacks the dearer of its two skills (`mpWanted`).
       - Soul Rend and Mana Shield take their MP from the pool both skills share.
       - A troop Resurrection brings back has 0 MP, so its awakening skill, ready at once, waits for MP like the
         #10 skill.
     - **The stagger:** at a wave's start and at the awakening moment, the i-th living troop of the type is ready
       after (i % 4) × 1 s, so a type never fires on one tick. A troop placed later is ready at once.
     - **Branch 1 (this one)** built the plumbing and three skills with the design's numbers:
       - Disarm (soldier: a 1.5–2.5× blow on the strongest foe in reach, whose damage then drops to 0.9–0.8, a
         boss's to 0.95–0.9, for 6 s);
       - Unbroken (knight: below 55% HP when just hit, or below 85% under a monster's hindrance, it heals 25–35%
         of its HP and throws the hindrances off, and its neighbours heal 10–15%);
       - Consecration (templar: holy ground of 1.5–2 tiles for 4–5 s, 0.15–0.25× its damage a second to each foe
         on it, 1.25× on an undead one).
       Branches 2 and 3 plug their skills into the same switches.
     - **Consecration's blows are holy**, like Judgement's and Holy Nova's: #59 branch 2b's Reassemble reached main
       during this branch. A skeleton Consecration kills never reassembles, and a heap of bones lying on the holy
       ground ends there. As plain blows they would have passed a heap by, on ground named holy.
     - **Curse of Weakness** now skips a foe only when it is already weakened as strongly as the curse would do
       (`effectK`). Before, it skipped any weakened foe, so a disarmed foe would never have been cursed. Only
       curses weakened monsters before, so with the switch off nothing changes.
     - **Cost to the frame:** `awakenLevel` is now cached per type while its item list is the same list at the
       same length, since every troop asks it every tick. The book's try-ons (`priceWith`, `assignPreview`) add an
       item and take it back, so they change the length and read a new level. A ready skill whose rule says no is
       not asked again for 0.25 s. The ground zones now skip an invisible zone before its layer, and Consecration
       draws with no layer at all (decision 117's cost).
     - **With `Game.awakenSkills` off**, a game plays as main did (checked against main's copy of the replay probe,
       below).
     - **Balance** is weighed after the merge (the owner's fast lane, 2026-09-29). The replay probe is in the
       awaken-core report's probe plan for qa-loop: main's saved between-wave states, replayed with the skills on and
       off and the same dice, per army, per type and level, and every type at Bangkit 3. A first cut, before the fast
       lane, ran 75 states of seeds 1–3 (the soldier and the knight awakened, as main's auto-player plays them):
       - troops lost per wave fell from 2.29 to 1.57 (−31% ± 15%);
       - the soldiers and knights themselves fell about half as often;
       - a soldier cast Disarm about 3 times a wave and a knight Unbroken 0.4 times.
       That is at the Hero skills' 30% cap, where the design wanted well under it, so qa-loop's full run decides
       whether Disarm needs trimming.
       - With the switch off, seed 1's 23 saved waves replay exactly as on main: who fell, lives, time and flag
         alike.
125. **The wake script also wakes agents stopped by an unavailable auto-mode check** (the orchestrator's brief,
     after it found two workers idle about 22 h on 2026-09-29; dev-workflow.md "Waking agents after a usage limit"):
     - When auto mode's safety check gives no verdict 10 times in a row, Claude Code ends the turn with "Auto mode
       is unavailable: … Wait for the user's next message", and a background session then sits `done` until
       somebody writes to it. The script's third kind, *classifier*, finds that result at the end of the last turn
       and resumes the session like a limited one, with its own prompt: carry on, retry once, then tell the
       orchestrator and wait.
     - Back-off: 15 min after the stop, and at most once an hour per worker. The hour counts over the worker's
       chain, because each wake is a new session and, while the check stays down, each new one stops again on its
       first tool call.
     - Left alone: a session listed `stopped` that the script never tried (someone ran `claude stop` on purpose),
       and, for every kind, one whose stopped turn said `DONE`.
     - Resumes made by hand are recognised, for every kind: a later session that has the stop's entry (its uuid)
       as one of its own is the resume, and is recorded in the state (`"by": "hand"`). Without it the old
       generation of a worker the orchestrator resumed by hand still looks stopped, and would have been woken a
       second time next to its successor. With an empty state on the live listing it found the 15 resumes the
       state holds, each with the same successor. Only a real entry counts: a first version took this worker's
       own session for a resume, because it had printed that uuid while looking into the stuck one.
126. **The necromancer mini boss has the HP of any mini boss** (issue #89; the owner asked on 2026-09-29 why the
     wave-48 mini boss showed only ×19 on its bar when earlier mini bosses had far more; it was the necromancer. Of
     keep / the same HP as any mini boss / half, they picked "same HP as any other mini boss"; units-and-combat.md
     "Stats", the slots and the boss buff):
     - `enemyStats`: as the mini boss the necromancer's HP is the slot's reference (the wave's strongest type,
       `enemyTypes[poolOf(wave).last]`, not its own 600) × `Tier.miniBoss.hp` 6, then the boss buff and the wave
       as before: exactly what a mini boss of the wave's strongest type has. `necroMiniHp` (0.4 of its own 600,
       240 on every wave) is gone.
     - Base HP (before buff and wave): 240 on waves 8–9 (the skeleton archer's 40, as before), 900 on 12, 1,320
       on 21, 1,920 from 22 (the werebear's). On wave 48: 144,213 (×145 on its bar) instead of 18,027 (×19).
     - Unchanged: its damage (`necroMiniDmg` 0.6 of its own, not the tier's ×2.2), its MP (120, × `miniMpK`),
       summons, gold, relic chance, and the boss necromancer.
     - A necromancer below the mini boss (only tests make one) keeps its own 600 × its tier.
     - Balance: under the owner's fast lane (2026-09-29) it merged on its tests; the paired replay (main's saved
       mini boss waves with the necromancer forced into the slot, main vs this) is the qa-loop's to run after the
       merge (reports/necro-mini-hp.md, "PROBE PLAN").
127. **From wave 50 every mini boss and boss comes with an escort: 3 healing necromancers and a high-elite
     necromancer** (issue #90; the owner, 2026-09-29: "wave 50+ miniboss dan bossnya di backup 3 necromencer
     penyembuh biar ada perlawanan dan 1 necromencer pemanggil level high elite"; units-and-combat.md "Waves" and
     "The necromancers", formation-and-navigation.md "The healing necromancer"):
     - From `escortFrom` 50, each mini boss and boss is followed in the queue by `escortHealers` 3 healing
       necromancers and `escortSummoners` 1 necromancer of rank high elite. A wave with both (60, 75, 90…) gets
       two escorts. They come on top of the wave's own healers. The "last healer right behind the boss" rule
       stays; that healer now comes after the boss's escort. The orchestrator chose these defaults, and they are
       constants the owner may change.
     - The escort's healers keep the usual random rank. It is drawn from the slots' dice after the slots' own
       rolls, so the rest of the wave is what it was.
     - The escort's healers heal their boss first when it is hurt and they may. #78's no-stack window still
       holds: one of the three heals it per heal interval, and the others heal the next most hurt. With nobody
       to heal they wait a tile behind their boss rather than behind the rearmost monster.
     - They are brave for their own boss (the orchestrator's option B; the owner may veto). For its heal spot,
       their rest spot behind it and backing off, only the melee troops' reach + `necroSafety` counts
       (`escortMeleeOnly`). They stand up to `escortReach` 64 (their heal range) behind it, never past it, and
       take arrows and spells meanwhile. For any other monster the whole rule holds.
       - Why: the brief first kept _mend's whole rule. The first behaviour probe (the owner's live army of 48
         troops, waves 50/51/60, the queue cut to the slots and escorts, 2 seeds) showed the escort's healers
         150–240 px behind their boss and inside some troop's reach 76–100% of the time. They healed their boss
         0–1 times a slot, because the long-range troops cover the field.
       - A heal is small at wave 50 (43–73 HP, about one per 1.2 s under the no-stack window, against an 81,600
         HP boss). So this is about how the escort plays and looks: the healers stay with their boss and give
         the troops something to kill.
     - The link: the escort-shaped monsters (up to 4) that come on right after a mini boss or boss are its
       escort (`Unit.escortOf`). The queue keeps its `(type, Tier)` shape, which dozens of tests fill by hand.
     - The high-elite necromancer is new: before, the necromancer was only the mini boss or the boss.
       - HP: #89's mini boss reference (the wave's strongest type) × the tier's 3, a high-elite werebear's
         (13,056 at wave 50).
       - Damage: the mini boss's share 0.6 × 1.7 / 2.2 ≈ 0.46 of its own (74 at wave 50).
       - No boss buff.
       - MP 60 (+2/s), half the mini boss's 120 (+4). It raises up to elites: one tier below its own under the
         existing ceiling rule; `maxMinions` 6 unchanged.
       - Gold, score and relic chance as any high elite: 873 gold at wave 50, 50 points, 5%.
       - No name and no boss bar; the log says "Elit Tinggi muncul: Nekromanser".
       - It is still never stunned or hexed: those rules go by the necromancer's type.
     - Balance was not measured here (the owner's fast lane, 2026-09-29). A behaviour probe checked that the
       escort comes on, follows its boss and heals it. It used the owner's army at waves 50, 51 and 60, 2 seeds,
       8 slots. Every slot came with its escort. Under B the healers healed their boss 3–7 times in 5 of the 8
       slots, and stayed 32–117 px behind it. The other 3 had no boss heals; they include both fast orc_rider
       bosses, which outran their healers (102–218 px behind). The waves 50–60 comparison with main is the
       qa-loop's (reports/boss-escort.md, "PROBE PLAN").
128. **Relics come off between waves, and a Hero holds two** (issue #91, the owner: "tambahkan feature untuk lepas
     artefak dari troops dan buat hero bisa pegang 2 artefak"; loot-items-relics.md "Relics", ui-hud.md "Tas",
     "Unit plates", "Loot in hand and the drop popup"). "Artefak" here is every relic a troop holds, the 4 dropped
     ones and the 5 store artefacts. It ends decision 34's "no way to take a relic off":
     - **Taking one off** ("Lepas", `Game.takeOff`) puts it back in the bag, from where it is given again or sold
       like any other. Between waves only (the orchestrator's default, `takeOffMidWave` false, like the store's
       `storeMidWave`): no swaps mid-fight, so a Grail that saved its holder this wave can't be handed on for a
       second save. During a wave the Lepas buttons show greyed with "Hanya di antara gelombang"; a tap says it.
       Giving a relic stays allowed mid-wave, as before.
     - **Where:** on the Tas page's troop rows, a tap on a held relic's slot picks it out and the row's last line
       becomes "Lepas" and the relic's name (a two-step, so a tap meant for the row's gift can't take one off);
       and the pinned plate on the field (a tap on a troop) lists its relics, each with a Lepas button. The Tas
       list only showed while a relic was picked, so with an empty bag nothing reached a held relic: with nothing
       picked the facing page now lists the troops that hold relics ("Relik dipakai").
     - **A Hero holds two** (`heroRelicSlots` 2; every other troop one): two different kinds, the store's
       artefacts included (the orchestrator's default: no doubling one kind). A Hero holding that kind says
       "Sudah memegang <relic>", one with both slots taken "Slot relik penuh"; a troop with its one slot taken
       still names what it holds. Every relic hook reads both (`Unit.holds`), so Dragon Heart and Dawn Star
       together give HP ×3 and damage ×2, and guard with fang both work. The Grail's once-a-wave is still per
       holder (`grailUsed`), which is safe because taking off waits for the wave's end.
     - `Unit.relic` became `Unit.relics` (in the order given); the save writes `relics` (a list), and a save from
       before still loads its one `relic`. A fallen Hero gives both back to the bag.
     - Taking one off is a telemetry event (`RelicTakenOff`, counted per wave as `relicsTakenOff`), not a battle
       log line, like giving one (`RelicUsed`).
     - No balance probe: a Hero's second relic only adds power when the player owns two kinds, and relics are
       rare (about 12.7 a game from drops, decision 52's numbers); the store's prices are unchanged.
129. **Features merge on their tests, QA cycles check the merges after, and the whole lifecycle lives in one file**
     (the owner, 2026-09-29: "pengerjaan feature yang lama di keluarkan dari development flow dan di kerjakan di 1
     agent loop sendiri jadi feature bisa lebih cepat di deliver ke user, dan kalau ternyata dari agent loop tadi
     menemukan bug maka bisa jadi improvement tersendiri", then "qa-loop selalu agent baru setiap ada loop baru, 1
     loop bisa ngecek langsung lebih dari 1 report jadi bisa lebih cepat lagi untuk menemukan masalahnya tanpa harus
     menunggu antrian", and "sdlc ini di simpan dalam 1 file jadi next pindah mesin atau developer tidak perlu
     setting ulang lagi"; sdlc.md, testing.md "Weighing balance: paired replays"):
     - Why the fast lane: on 2026-09-27..29 probes took 687 queue jobs, 31.6 lane-hours, 83% of the runners' time,
       while a full suite has a median of 61 s, analyze 6 s and targeted tests 51 s. A feature's own checks took
       minutes, and it waited hours behind the probes.
     - Before READY a feature worker now runs only its tests, the full suite, analyze and at most 2 short behaviour
       probes (≤ 3 min each). What would weigh balance goes in its report as a PROBE PLAN.
     - After each merge the orchestrator queues it in `qa-loop/pending.txt`. A QA cycle is a fresh agent `qa-<n>`
       (`spawn-qa-cycle.sh`) that checks every merge since the last cycle in one batch: one combined paired replay
       of the range, attributed per merge only when something moved, the plans' own checks, and the owner's
       telemetry. It reports BALANCE and FINDING, then DONE, and `finish-qa-cycle.sh` advances the range. A finding
       becomes a new issue for a fresh worker. The queue's runner 2 is the QA lane (`qa-` ids first), runner 1
       the features' fast lane. A first design had one standing qa-loop agent; the owner replaced it with cycles
       before it ran a check.
     - sdlc.md replaces agent-workflow.md: the roles, the lifecycle, the rules that lived only in the orchestrator's
       memory, and every infra file of `<agents>/` embedded whole, with a bootstrap that installs them on
       a new machine, `--check` for drift and `--export` to refresh the doc after an infra change. Machine values
       (HOME, the repo, the sockets) are `@@…@@` in the blocks. Any infra change updates sdlc.md in the same change.
     - The decisions log merges entry by entry (`scripts/merge-decisions.py`, `.gitattributes`): the log was the
       conflicting file in 105 of 116 real merge conflicts. `merge=union` was replayed on the 149 past merges where
       the log conflicted. It moved an entry's last line into another branch's entry 3 times, broke numeric order
       46 times, and would have landed 123 numbers taken twice without a conflict. The driver merged 26 of them
       cleanly and correctly and stopped on the 123 real collisions, which handed-out numbers now avoid.
130. **No pause panel: the field dims under "Pause" and the game can be played while it waits; the book pauses a
     wave; the game runs on while the window is hidden** (issue #93; the owner, 2026-09-29: "butuh pause dan bisa buka
     tas untuk melakukan upgrade/ spawn pasukan jadi user bisa berfikir", then "jadi popup jeda itu di remove aja di
     buat hover layar baru di atasnya ada tulisan "Pause" atau ketika buka tas maka otomatis game jadi ke pause,
     kalau window tidak focus juga game tetap berjalan"; ui-hud.md "Pause"):
     - The Jeda panel (the crate with Lanjut, Pengaturan, Menu Utama) is gone. Paused, the field is dimmed with
       "Pause" (the owner's word) in the score screens' gold title at its top centre, under the HUD. The old panel
       blocked the HUD so the game could be thought over but not played; now the book, the buttons, the tooltips
       and the drags all work while paused: troops are bought and placed, items and relics given by tap and drag.
       The pause button, Esc and P pause and resume; a tap on the field no longer resumes (the player may be placing
       troops). Pengaturan is only the book's tab, and Menu Utama stays on its page.
     - The book pauses a wave, one rule (`_bookPauses`). The brief said "opening the book pauses (any tab, mid-wave
       or between waves)", but between waves the book is always open in landscape (it floats in after the cheer)
       and a phone's is never shut, so taken literally the game would stay paused. The orchestrator's pick (A + B
       + a phone rule): in landscape, the book opened by hand mid-wave pauses, and shutting it resumes if it
       paused the game (paused first by the player, it stays paused); on a phone, turning the book to Tas mid-wave
       (the owner's "buka tas") pauses, and back on Pasukan resumes; between waves the auto start's countdown
       waits while the book shows Tas, Toko or Pengaturan (Toko did already, #63). Two small follow-ons: on a
       phone Mulai turns the book back to Pasukan, so a wave started from Tas doesn't pause at once; and Menu
       Utama during a wave leaves a pause of the player's, so "Lanjutkan" always comes back paused.
     - Defaults kept (the orchestrator's): the store still deals between waves only and taking a relic off stays
       between waves (#91), paused or not; the music ducks while paused, as it did under the panel.
     - The window: losing the focus never paused (inactive), and hiding no longer does. But hidden (minimized,
       covered, another Space) Flutter draws no frames (SchedulerBinding turns them off for hidden and paused; macOS
       reports hidden from FlutterEngine.mm's occlusion handler), and Flame's loop runs on frames, so the game would
       stand still anyway. The owner said yes to option (b): a 30 Hz timer runs the game's update while hidden, by
       the real time (the periodic timer's tick count), and the frames' updates are dropped meanwhile. When frames
       come back it stops and Flame's loop starts over, so no time counts twice; Flame's own pause on hiding is
       off. The music and sounds play on. `NSAppSleepDisabled` in Info.plist keeps App Nap from delaying the
       timer (the orchestrator's catch: muted music would let App Nap in).
131. **The movers: Phantom Rush, Skyfall and Lifeline** (issue #88 branch 2 of 3; the owner's answers in decision 124;
     the design is the #88 phase 1 report §3; units-and-combat.md "Awakening skills" and "Forced movement", ui-hud.md
     "Skills"):
     - Built with the design's rules and numbers, and with decision 124's MP (40% of the type's pool at its level) and
       cooldowns (the design's minus 2 s: Phantom Rush 18 s, Skyfall 22 s, Lifeline 22 / 20 / 18 s):
       - Phantom Rush (swordsman): 3 / 3 / 4 dashes of 0.2 s round the most wounded foes within 2.5 tiles, a cut of
         1.2× / 1.3× / 1.5× at each, one more while Rampage lasts and one more for a kill, then home in 0.15 s;
       - Skyfall (axeman): a 0.5 s leap from behind the front onto 3+ foes beside a troop that fights there, never
         past it; 1× / 1.25× / 1.5× its damage within 1.25 / 1.5 / 1.5 tiles as it lands, and a 15–25% guard 3 s;
       - Lifeline (priest): the 1 / 1 / 2 most hurt troops below 30% HP still fighting are lifted 0.45 s to its
         side, healed 1.5× / 2× / 2.5× its heal and counted as come to their healer.
     - All three move only troops, so they cast during a stalled wave's march too. Each move is a `Carry` (forced
       movement): a carried troop does nothing else, nobody shoves it, and its attack pause waits, as the design
       wanted for the rush. `Carry.look` and `Carry.radius` are new, for the drawing only.
     - Where the design left room:
       - Phantom Rush's round leaves out a heap of bones (Reassemble reached main after the design): a cut on one
         would do nothing. A dash whose foe died on the way still counts as one of its cuts, so a rush never runs
         longer than its cuts (at most 6 × 0.2 s + 0.15 s at Bangkit 3).
       - Skyfall holds its spot back to the front-most of the troops that fought near it when several did, and
         counts its 3 foes at the spot after that. "Ahead" and "nearest" are from the axeman.
       - Lifeline's petals show only with the heal: a troop set down after its priest fell lands plain, unhealed.
     - **Crushing Blow now stuns through `_stunFor`**, as the design asked with Skyfall: a mini boss stands 0.5 s, not
       1 s. The docs already said half; the code stunned it the whole second. This one change reaches games with
       `Game.awakenSkills` off too (any axeman's Crushing Blow on a mini boss).
     - **Balance** is weighed after the merge (the owner's fast lane, decision 129): the awaken-b2 report's probe
       plan, the replay probe of decision 124 with the three types forced to each level.
132. **Android release builds are signed with our own release signing key, kept outside the repo** (the owner,
     2026-10-01, after the itch page work found release APKs signed with the debug key: "ini coba di buat saja dulu
     dan nanti read parse keynya dari sini the signing password's file dan nanti buat keynya di
     dalam the signing key's folder"; dev-workflow.md "Android release signing"):
     - The key is the release keystore (JKS, alias `upload`, RSA 4096, valid to 2054). The
       orchestrator named it the release signing key: for the APKs sold on itch.io it signs every update (Android
       installs an update only over the same key), and on Google Play it would be the upload key.
     - The password stays in the owner's file and is copied nowhere: keytool got it with `-storepass:file` /
       `-keypass:file`, `key.properties` names the file (`storePasswordFile`), and Gradle reads its first line at
       build time. No agent has seen the value.
     - Gradle finds `key.properties` through `ANDROID_KEY_PROPERTIES` (by default the owner's signing
       `key.properties`; since 315 `android/key.properties`, and release-build.sh sets the variable from
       `git config poh.androidKeyProperties`).
       Without one (CI, other machines) the release build falls back to the debug key with a warning, so nobody's
       build breaks. With one that doesn't work, release packaging fails instead of quietly signing with the debug key,
       because an APK published with the wrong key can't be updated by the right one.
     - Losing the key means no installed APK can ever be updated: the owner backs up the signing key's folder and the
       password file in two offline places. CI will get them as encrypted secrets.
133. **The app's id is `cloud.brata.poh`, and phones keep the game's files in the app's own files dir** (the
     owner, 2026-10-01, on the release plan's J4: "id app android maksudmu? kalau iya di arahkan ke
     cloud.brata.poh"; the orchestrator gave the other platforms the same identity, which the owner may veto;
     dev-workflow.md "App identity"):
     - Android: `applicationId` and `namespace` `cloud.brata.poh`, `MainActivity` moved to that package, label
       "Path of Hero". Linux: `APPLICATION_ID` `cloud.brata.poh`. Windows: `CompanyName` "brata.cloud" (and the
       copyright), `ProductName`/`FileDescription` "Path of Hero". macOS: bundle id `cloud.brata.poh` (tests
       `cloud.brata.poh.RunnerTests`). This lifts 37's "the bundle id keeps tower_defense": the ids had to be final
       before the first public build, since Android installs no update over another id.
     - The binaries keep `tower_defense`, macOS's `PRODUCT_NAME` included (the orchestrator's call, 2026-10-01): the
       agents check the game runs with `pgrep -x tower_defense`, a name with spaces needs quoting everywhere and
       couldn't be test-built here, and the player already sees "Path of Hero" (CFBundleName/CFBundleDisplayName;
       the release's folder is renamed to `Path of Hero.app` when packed, itch-page.md). The Dart package and the
       save folder stay `tower_defense` too.
     - The version starts at `0.1.0+1` (pubspec, the single source; Android's versionName/versionCode come from it).
     - macOS: the new id means a new sandbox container, so the first new build shows a fresh game. No migration
       code: a sandboxed app can't read another app's container (the plan's review, R5), and only the owner's own
       save existed. The owner (or the orchestrator, with a backup) copies the old container's `tower_defense`
       folder once, after the new build's first launch (dev-workflow.md "The save's move to the new container").
     - Android sets no HOME, so every path (save, settings, scores, telemetry) pointed under `/` and nothing could
       be saved (R4). `dataDirFor`/`initDataDir` (lib/save.dart) give one folder per platform: desktop unchanged (no
       desktop save moves), Android and iOS `getApplicationSupportDirectory()` from path_provider (Android's
       `Context.getFilesDir()`). path_provider was chosen over a MethodChannel in MainActivity because it was
       already in pubspec.lock through flutter_soloud: no new download, nothing native of our own.
     - Writes never crash: `saveGame`, `saveSettings`, `clearSave` and the telemetry's file log I/O errors
       (`debugPrint`) and go on.
     - Android may end a backgrounded app without a word, so going to the background (hidden/paused) between waves
       saves the game. Not mid-wave: a save holds no wave in progress, and loading one would skip that wave, so the
       last won wave's save stands as before.
134. **Awakening skills, branch 3: Impale, Spellbreaker and Singularity, the three that act on the monsters' own
     rules** (issue #88; the design is the #88 phase 1 report, its "Changed after review" rows winning; the owner's
     answers of 2026-09-29 as in 124: one skill per type that grows, MP, the design's names, ready at once mid-wave;
     units-and-combat.md "Awakening skills", ui-hud.md "Skills"):
     - **Impale** (lancer): a lunge out to its reach + a tile for 1.5× / 2× / 2.5× its damage. First it breaks a
       monster's wind-up (its cooldown, begun with the wind-up, runs on; a 0.3 s stagger through `_stunFor`, a mini
       boss 0.15 s); else it pins a strong foe to 0.1× walking (the boss rank 0.55×) for 2 / 2.5 / 3 s
       (`Status.impaled`, apart from `slow`). While a monster it could break stands within 5 tiles it waits for the
       break, 3 s at most after its skill is ready. One monster is broken at most once in 25 s (`Unit.interruptedAt`).
     - **Spellbreaker** (archer): a silver arrow at the foe with the most monster buffs and guards, the highest ranked
       first, for 1.5× / 2× / 2.5×; landing, it strips them off it (and at Bangkit 2 / 3 off every foe within 1 / 1.5
       tiles). A mini boss, the boss rank, and a buff the boss rank gave lose half of what is left, once. No
       interrupt and no silence, as the review asked.
     - **Singularity** (wizard): a well on the foe with the most pullable foes round it (4+) for 2 / 2.5 / 3 s,
       drifting them inward at 24 / 28 / 32 a second × their shove share, then a burst of 1× / 1.25× / 1.5× within
       1.25 tiles of its centre.
     - **Cooldowns and MP** are the plumbing's (124): the design's minus 2 s (Impale 18 s, Spellbreaker 18 / 16 / 14,
       Singularity 24 / 22 / 20), and 40% of the type's pool a cast.
     - **Where this branch went past the design's words:**
       - Impale never breaks a once-only skill (Frenzy, Thick Hide: infinite cooldowns). The wind-up starts the
         cooldown, so a broken once-only skill would never come again: the very lockout the review took out of
         Spellbreaker. Those foes are pinned instead.
       - "Not the necromancer" is by type: the escort's high-elite necromancer (#90) is never broken either, though
         it may be pinned. The escort's healing necromancers' Mass Mend may be broken.
       - "Buffs a boss's moment gave" is read as any buff the boss rank gave (its `Effect.by`): Rally and Howl, and its
         War Shout too. Iron March and Second Wind are on the boss itself, which is halved anyway. A buff that names
         no giver (Frenzy, Bloodrage, Unholy Ward, Bulwark's reflect) counts as a monster's, so on a normal monster
         Spellbreaker strips an escort healer's Unholy Ward, and on the escorted boss halves it.
       - Spellbreaker's "no arrow at it in the last 1 s" is "no silver arrow flying at it": the arrow is in the air
         under 1 s at every range, and a foe whose buffs are all halved has nothing left to count.
       - A break pins nothing and a pin staggers nothing: the stagger comes only with a break, as the review had it.
       - The well's "never closer than baseX + 1 tile" needs no clamp: its x part only moves a monster away from the
         base.
     - **With `Game.awakenSkills` off** nothing changes: the pin's ×1 and the halved flag are never set.
     - **Balance** is weighed after the merge (the fast lane, 129): reports/awaken-b3.md "PROBE PLAN" (the on/off
       replays per type and level, Impale's breaks per mini boss, Singularity's leaks, the frame time).
135. **The app icon is the Hero knight, drawn from the game's own sprite on a background of our own** (the owner,
     2026-10-01: "icon game ambil dari sprite knight heronya saja terus di kasi kan background di belakangnya";
     release job J2; assets.md "The app icon", itch-page.md Licences):
     - `tool/make_app_icon.py` builds every platform's file (macOS AppIcon, Windows .ico, the Linux window icon,
       Android's legacy and adaptive launcher icons, the web icons and favicon), so no Flutter logo is left. It only
       reads `assets/images/`.
     - The figure is the knight's idle frame 0 at a whole-number nearest-neighbour scale, in a Hero's look: the
       splash's white halo and the pack's gold crown above the helmet, so it reads as "the Hero", not any knight.
       Where not one whole pixel fits (16-32 px) it is area-averaged into a sharp silhouette with a dark edge, which
       stayed readable at 16 px where a plain average was a smudge.
     - The background is drawn in the tool (a sunrise gradient in the crown's golds, the splash's 10 rays, a soft
       ground shadow, a dark rim), not the LudicArts valley, whose licence is still unconfirmed.
     - The knight and crown make the icon a derivative of Zerie's and Kenmi's packs. Both allow commercial games, so
       it ships in the builds; it stays out of a future public code repo, which needs an icon of its own.
     - Linux: the window icon (`data/app_icon.png`, set in `my_application.cc`) rather than a `.desktop` file, since
       a bundle run straight from its folder has no installed `.desktop` file. GNOME on Wayland shows only a
       `.desktop` file's icon: that comes with an installer.
     - Android also gets a monochrome layer, so Android 13's themed icons show the knight (outline solid, the rest
       half see-through) instead of falling back to the full-colour icon.
