137. **The code is source-available under the Path of Hero License; CREDITS.md, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt and an
     in-game Lisensi page carry the credits and every licence** (release job J5; the owner, 2026-10-01: "open source
     like jeansh, only the builds are paid", then "game ini bukan beli tapi donasi" and "arahkan ke githubnya saja kan
     ini di opensource"; the release plan's D1 (a), the orchestrator's default, which the owner may still change to
     MIT or GPL; README.md "Licence", ui-hud.md "Lisensi page", assets.md "Licence files"):
     - `LICENSE` is the owner's Jeansh licence adapted, same Licensor (Trias BYM). Official builds are the ones on
       itch.io (or a channel the Licensor names), "free, or offered for a donation or a price that the player
       chooses". Kept as they are: build it yourself for your own use (§2), the contribution grant (§3), no
       distribution, with the fork note (§4), termination, no warranty, liability (§7–9). §5 reserves the name, the
       icon and the logo. §6: the packs (Zerie, Kenmi, unTied Games, BDragon1727, LudicArts) are licensed to the
       Licensor only, not in the public repo, and the licence grants nothing in them; packages keep their own
       licences; the owner's own art and audio are all rights reserved.
       - Past the brief's words: §6c lets a §2 build use the owner's own art and audio, since a build made under §2
         needs them and "all rights reserved" alone would forbid it. The owner may strike it.
       - The licence's opening keeps Jeansh's "is not open source software". Nothing else calls the game open
         source: the README and the game say "source-available" (the plan's §2, OSD #1), and a test checks README,
         CREDITS.md and the in-game text.
       - Changing the licence later (MIT, GPL) is LICENSE, the README's paragraph and `licenceSummary` in
         lib/licences.dart.
     - `CREDITS.md`: every pack with its author, link and terms (from itch-page.md's audit; unTied Games' credit is
       required), what was made for the game, and the software. `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt`, written by
       `tool/third_party_notices.py`: part 1 the 46 Dart packages pubspec.yaml pulls in (path_provider's family
       included) with their LICENSE files, part 2 the native libraries flutter_soloud compiles in (SoLoud and the
       code inside it, miniaudio, dr_libs, pffft, Signalsmith's headers, libogg, libvorbis, libopus, libFLAC). No
       package's LICENSE carries part 2, so Flutter's NOTICES misses it: `registerLicences` (lib/licences.dart, from
       main()) adds it to the LicenseRegistry, and the file's part 2 is made from the same Dart texts (a test checks
       they match). The Xiph texts came from the prebuilt libraries' headers and copies on this Mac (Homebrew's opus
       COPYING, an Android NOTICE's libogg); libvorbis's year line ("2002-2020") is from memory, to check against
       its COPYING when there is network.
     - The game has no MaterialApp, so Flutter's `showLicensePage` can't open. The Lisensi page draws the same in the
       book, in the game's style: the licence in short and the credits on the left page, the packages on the right
       one, a tap on one shows its licences. Reached from a button on Pengaturan (no fifth tab), whose tab stays the
       open one. ICU alone has over 500 licences, so a column lays out what shows and then a slice a frame.
     - `cupertino_icons` is gone from pubspec.yaml: nothing used it (`pub get --offline`).
     - CREDITS.md and the in-game credits name the app icon (135): Zerie's knight with Kenmi's crown on our own
       background, which §6c names as the owner's.
     - Not done here: the public repo (J14, with the owner's final OK) and the itch page's source link.
     - The orchestrator took the defaults on 2026-10-02: §6c's carve-out stays, and so does "not open source
       software"; the owner may still change either, or D1.
138. **The five artefacts are Pusaka: bound to a troop TYPE, with stars, moved between waves; the probes get their
     knobs** (the owner, 2026-10-01: "sekarang user bener bener nga ada ngerasa apapun dari penggunaan artefaknya",
     and the roguelike element is to come from the artefacts; the design "Pusaka Jenis + Peti Bos",
     <agents>/reports/artefact-roguelike-design.md, parts P0 and P1a, built on its defaults: (1a) on a
     type, (4a) a Pusaka only from the chest later, (6a) the small relics stay on troops; loot-items-relics.md
     "Pusaka", units-and-combat.md, telemetry.md, testing.md "The Pusaka", sdlc.md's probes):
     - Why: an artefact on one troop of 48 was 2% of the army and died with its holder, in silence. In the owner's
       run all five went on templars at w67; two were back in the bag after the w70 boss and sat there 16 waves;
       95% of relic gifts came back through a death. Items already work per type and survive deaths; so now do the
       artefacts.
     - A Pusaka (lib/pusaka.dart) is bound to a troop type and works on every living troop of it, its Heroes and the
       ones bought later included; never lost when they fall (with none alive it sleeps). A type holds one; the rest
       wait in the Gudang. ★1 to ★3: Dragon Heart HP ×1.6/2.2/3.0 and 1% regen; Dawn Star power ×1.3/1.45/1.6 (the
       dead pause cut gone); God's Thunder 2/3/4 leaps at 40%, at most 12 drawn a second; the Grail once a wave per
       troop at 30/40/50% HP, 2 s untouchable; Void Eye ×1.25/1.35/1.45 (boss ×1.15/1.2/1.25) as its own
       `Status.voidMark`, so it stacks with Hunter's Mark. Dragon Heart and Dawn Star are in `statsOf`, so the book
       and the field agree. Every number is one constant in pusaka.dart.
       - Void Eye's mark is read in `_afterDefence`, beside `vulnerable` (the design said `_beforeDefence`):
         `vulnerable` is an after-defence multiplier, and the two must multiply the same blow the same way.
     - Binding, unbinding and Pindah happen between waves only (`bindMidWave`). The first binding of each is free,
       unbinding is free, a later binding costs `rerollPrice(wave)` (the chest's reroll, P3: 600 × 1.05^(wave−1),
       2.5k at w30, 38k at w86) × `pindahShare` 1.0.
     - The store sells one of each: a copy of one owned is refused ("Dimiliki"), since a purchase that does nothing is
       a trap; one in the Gudang sells back at half its base, a bound one doesn't ("Terpasang: lepas dulu"). The
       shelf itself closes with the chest (P3).
     - A save from before them migrates in `fromJson`: every artefact in its bag or worn is counted (the first ★1,
       each copy +★ up to ★3, past it paid back at 50% of base) and bound by default (a preference list per Pusaka,
       first living type with none), the HP coming with it. The owner's w86 save: templar ← Dragon Heart, axeman ←
       Grail, wizard ← God's Thunder, priest ← Dawn Star, archer ← Void Eye, each ★1. A one-time message with Batal
       waits for P1b's Tas page (`Game.notes`, `pusakaNoteDue`, `undoDefaultBinding`, `dismissPusakaNote`). New save
       keys `pusaka` and `notes`; an older build would drop `pusaka`, so the save is copied before the first launch.
     - Each wave counts what each Pusaka did (H3c): the Grail's saves kept, Dragon Heart's blows lived through that
       would have killed at base HP, Dawn Star's extra damage and healing landed, God's Thunder's leap damage, Void
       Eye's bonus. The telemetry carries them (`telemetryVersion` 2, `eventVersion` 2): `WaveStarted.pusaka`, the
       wave record's `pusaka` and `gold.pusakaSpent`, `PusakaBound` / `PusakaMoved`, and `TroopFell.relics`.
     - With the owner's limits (141): Lepas jenis sends the released type's Pusaka to the Gudang, free (a later
       binding is a Pindah, as after an unbind); the one-time notes are one set, `Game.notes` ("pusaka", "army",
       "types"), saved only when any.
     - Amends 34 and 128: one relic per troop, Lepas and a Hero's two slots are the four small relics' rules now;
       and 99: the store's artefacts are Pusaka. (52, the boss's relic roll, and 54, the army cap, are P3's and
       P4's.)
     - P0, the probes (sdlc.md's embedded probes, `probe_knobs.dart`): `u.relics.isEmpty` (the probes still asked
       for #91's `u.relic`), and the knobs SKIP_REFUSED, REBUY=owner, CUT, PUSAKA, ARMY, TYPES and OFFERS, each off by
       default, so a probe without them plays as before. What a ref may lack is reached through `dynamic`: the
       Pusaka's hooks (`givePusaka`, `bindByDefault`) are Game instance members for it, and P3's and P4's knobs
       (`armyMax`, `typeLimit`, `offers`, `draftPolicy`) must be too.
     - Not here: the Tas page (P1b: until it lands no screen binds a Pusaka, and the book's artefact slots read the
       bag, so they show none), the chest (P3), the cap and the type limit (P4). Balance is weighed in the QA cycle
       (129): reports/pusaka-rules.md "PROBE PLAN", A1 "Pusaka worth at 48", where Dragon Heart ★1 is tuned between
       ×1.6 and ×1.75.
139. **The wake script starts woken agents fresh, not by `--resume`; only the orchestrator is resumed** (the owner,
     2026-10-01: "pastikan jika reuse agent untuk di mulai dari new saja contextnya", the orchestrator's brief;
     dev-workflow.md "Waking agents after a usage limit", sdlc.md section 8):
     - A resume copies the whole conversation, so a worker woken after a limit carried its old, fat context on, the
       opposite of the one-job, small-context rule (decisions-log 129). Its state lives in files anyway: the
       worktree and branch, its report, its queue requests.
     - The script decides what the stopped session is: a worker or QA cycle (its cwd is a worktree that still exists,
       with `reports/task-<name>` or `qa-loop/job-qa-<n>.md`), a test runner (by name), or the orchestrator (by name).
       A worker gets the preamble + its job + a handoff, a test runner its role brief + a handoff, the same brief
       `prompts/respawn-worker.sh` builds by hand. The script builds it itself, in Python, so that its selftest can
       check it and a dry run can name it; the two must change together.
     - The handoff says why and when the old session stopped, quotes its last message (trimmed to about 1500
       characters: the first two thirds and the end, which hold what it did and what came next) and says what to
       read first.
     - The orchestrator keeps `--resume`: its state is its conversation (merges in flight, the owner's questions,
       what it told whom). The owner may veto that later.
     - Other projects' agents keep the old wake, unchanged (a resume with the kind's prompt, the same back-offs and
       records). The cron job serves the owner's whole machine, and the agents of their other projects (other cwds,
       e.g. `~/dev/edot/…`) relied on it; the fresh-context rule is this project's (the orchestrator, at review).
       "Outside" is a cwd outside this repo's main checkout, which the script finds from its own checkout's git
       common dir (`WAKE_REPO` overrides).
     - An unknown session in this repo (no job file, no known role) is no longer woken. It is logged once, for the
       orchestrator to decide, rather than every 15 min.
     - A fresh respawn made by hand copies no uuid, so inside this repo "taken over by hand" also counts a session
       started after the stop in the same cwd under the same name. Otherwise the script would start a second worker
       in a worktree the orchestrator had already respawned. For other projects only a resume counts, as before.
     - The detection, DONE, the back-offs, the state's chain records (`"fresh": true` added) and the reaping are as
       before.
140. **The necromancer is never both the mini boss and the boss of one wave** (qa-2's FINDING, 2026-10-01; the
     orchestrator's default, qa-2's option 1; the owner may still pick another; units-and-combat.md "Waves" and
     "The summoner"):
     - Why: #89 (126) gave the necromancer mini boss any mini boss's HP, and a wave with a necromancer mini boss and a
       necromancer boss became a near-wipe. qa-2 forced the pair on states at waves 15/30/45/75/90 (ee6a43d vs
       9ae979c): from wave 61, 24.0 troops fell a wave instead of 12.0 (+11.96 ± 4.41), 0.42 more lives were lost a
       wave and waves ran 40% longer; the necromancer mini boss lived 146 s instead of 22 and leaked in 3 of 24 plays.
       At wave 90 on the owner's save 37–46 troops fell a play instead of 15–19, with 1–4 lives lost in 4 of 12. A
       necromancer mini boss alone stayed fine (still the gentlest mini boss): only the pair was broken, on ~11% of
       the waves with both. qa-2 measured before #90 (127), whose escorts from wave 50 likely make it heavier still.
     - What: `Game.necroPairAllowed` (false). The dice keep their order: the mini boss rolls for the necromancer on
       `rng`, then the boss rolls on `slots`. When the boss draws the necromancer and the mini boss had drawn it too,
       the mini boss becomes `slotType(pool, roll / necroMiniChance)`: its own necromancer roll (under 1/3) scaled
       back to 0–1.
     - Why that way: rolling the boss first would change the boss of many waves with both against main, and an extra
       draw would shift the escorts' ranks and every later slot. The scaled roll draws nothing new, so only that mini
       boss's type changes (~1/9 of the waves with both); determinism tests and saved-wave replays stay comparable.
       It is uniform on 0–1, so the moved mini boss has any mini boss's odds (#58, the stronger likelier) rather than
       always one type.
     - Unchanged: the necromancer mini boss at 1/3 from wave 8 on every other wave, and on a wave with both whose
       boss is another type; its HP from #89; the boss's roll; the escorts (#90), which follow whichever mini boss
       comes.
     - `necroPairAllowed` is a `Game` field, like `monsterSkills`: a probe or test turns it on to play main's waves.
     - Balance: the fast lane (129); the QA cycle runs the PROBE PLAN in reports/necro-pair.md (natural waves with
       both, fixed vs main, and an escort wave at 90).
141. **At most 32 troops alive and 4 troop types a run, with Lepas jenis, and Auto holds for a gutted army** (the
     owner, 2026-10-01: "jumlah maksimal pasukan juga di turunkan jumlahnya jadi cuma 32 saja? dan ada batasan jumlah
     jenis troops yang bisa di spawn"; the artefact redesign's part P4, <agents>/reports/artefact-roguelike-design.md
     §3.1, §3.2, §4; qa-1's finding 2; units-and-combat.md "The owner's limits", ui-hud.md, camera-and-field.md):
     - The owner hasn't answered the design's decisions 2 and 3, so these are their defaults: 4 types per run as a
       roster, a type keeps its slot when it dies out, Lepas jenis frees one between waves, the free priest counts;
       and the owner's 48-troop, 5-type save keeps everyone (buys resume at 31 or fewer alive, the roster reads 5/4
       so only a 6th type is refused, Lepas jenis any time between waves).
     - Both limits are switches the board turns on (`Game.boardRules`: `armyMax` 32, `typeLimit` 4), off in a plain
       `Game()`, so the tests and the probes keep today's rules. The numbers are named constants: `armyMaxBoard` 32,
       `typeLimitBoard` 4, `autoHoldShare` 0.75, `releaseRefund` 0.5.
     - The cap amends decision 54: `armyCap` = min(capacity, 32) gates buys and Resurrection, and capacity stops at
       32. Nobody is cut (the critique's C1: a shrink step gave capacity away and missed the owner's point): an army
       of 48 keeps its troops until they fall, shown "48/32" in red.
     - A roster, not a limit on the types alive (C2): with the latter, a front line wiped by a boss could never be
       bought back. A type joins on its first buy and keeps its place; only Lepas jenis takes it out. A save from
       before it has the types alive.
     - One gate: `buyRefusal(type)` inside `place()`, which `autoPlace` and #92's "Ganti yang gugur" (wt/tide, agreed
       with its worker) call, so every buy meets the cap and the roster.
     - Lepas jenis sends the type's living troops home for half their price, their relics to the bag, between waves
       only, and never while a Hero of the type lives (too rare to lose to a tap). Two taps, like #91's Lepas: a
       chip on the roster row arms it, and a red button over the row ("Lepas Templar?", "13 pulang, +12k emas")
       releases it. The type's Pusaka goes to the Gudang there once P1a (lib/pusaka.dart) lands.
     - The Auto hold (qa-1: Auto began w86 5 s after a wave that left 20 of 48; the owner bought 66 troops mid-wave):
       with the cap on, Auto's countdown holds while fewer than 75% of the cap are alive, and the start button says
       "Pasukan 20/32 - Auto ditahan"; buying back to 75% or Mulai goes on.
     - The owner's save gets two one-time notes (the saved `notes`): the cap is 32 and the troops stay; the limit is
       4 and the 5 types stay. Saved keys: `runTypes`, `notes`.
     - (Amended by 161.) With the tide, the 48 kept made a cliff: they shrink to 32 as they fall and can't be bought
       back, and meet the tide at 32 only when it is past what 32 holds. The game now warns while the army is full at
       the cap with the tide on, and the tide's HP grows 1% a wave.
     - (Amended by 162.) The troops kept over the cap now pay in tide: each one alive over it counts the wave's tide
       from 2 waves earlier, ramped in over 5 waves ("Beban").
     - (Amended by 201.) The owner meant a limit on how many of one type can be bought, not on the types in the army:
       the roster of 4 types is gone, and each type has a cap of its own alive (priest 5, archer and wizard 8, the
       melee 10). Lepas jenis stays.
142. **From wave 35 the tide ("Pasang") grows the crowd every wave, and the fallen can be bought back in one press**
     (issue #92 part 1; the owner, 2026-09-30: "late game too easy" and "iya bener duitnya itu aku bingung di buat untuk
     apa karna tanpa artefak shop juga lawan masi bisa di atasi dengan mudah", the gold has no use and the enemies are
     easy even without the artefact shop; the design is reports/late-game-design.md §2 part 1, its proposal B, which
     scored highest; units-and-combat.md "The tide" and "Ganti yang gugur", ui-hud.md, telemetry.md):
     - The owner hasn't answered the design's decisions 1-4, so the defaults are built, each a named constant:
       - 1b, the strength: HP +1.5% (`tideHp`), damage +0.5% (`tideDmg`) and the spawn gap 0.5% shorter (`tidePace`,
         never under `tideGapMin` 0.5 s) a wave, compounding: wave 72 had HP ×1.73 (amended by 161: `tideHp` is 0.01,
         wave 72 HP ×1.45);
       - 2b, the start: wave 35 (`tideFrom`), where the issue says the game gets too easy;
       - 3b, an old save: it catches up halfway, its tide counted from 20 waves back (`tideCatchUp`), never before 35.
         The owner's wave-72 save counts from 52: HP ×1.37 on wave 73 instead of ×1.76 at once;
       - 4a, the slots: the wave's boss and mini boss get no tide. They already killed 3-11 troops at waves 69-70,
         while the crowd killed almost nobody after wave 26.
     - Everything else that fights for the monsters gets it: the healing necromancers (their heal), #90's escorts and
       its high-elite summoner, and every raised minion. Kill gold, score, drops, speed, reach, defence and MP don't
       change, so the tide adds no income.
     - "Ganti yang gugur" turns the tide's falls into a use for gold: one press buys back the last won wave's fallen
       (not the Heroes), the cheapest first, each to its old spot. It buys through `place()`, the one buy gate
       (`buyRefusal`), so the army cap and the 4-type roster (decisions-log 141) apply to it with no code of its own;
       the two branches agreed that gate's name and order (the army and the roster, then the gold).
     - The button is on the book's Pasukan page, not in the "MENANG!" popup as the design drew it: the popup lasts
       2.4 s and fades, too short to press, and troops are bought on that page.
     - The feedback: the wave meter's "+56%" with its tooltip, a line in the "MENANG!" popup on the win before the
       tide's first wave, a message when an old save comes in with it on, and `start.tide` in the telemetry.
     - Weighing it (1-3 falls a wave, 0-1 lives, 30-70% of the gold spent) is the QA cycle's, after the merge (the fast
       lane, decisions-log 129); `tideHp` is the first knob.
143. **Bangkit 4-5 (Kebangkitan Emas): gold buys two more awakening levels for a type at Bangkit 3, in the Toko's
     Bangkit section** (#92 part 2; the owner, 2026-09-30: "iya bener duitnya itu aku bingung di buat untuk apa karna
     tanpa artefak shop juga lawan masi bisa di atasi dengan mudah"; late-game-design.md §2 part 2; loot-items-relics.md
     "Bangkit 4-5", ui-hud.md "Toko page"):
     - The owner hasn't answered the design's questions, so the orchestrator built the defaults: decision 5 c (the
       replace button of part 1, this, and Hero recall later) and 6 b, 100,000 / 250,000 per type. Every number is a
       named constant: `maxAscend` 2, `ascendPower` 1.25, `ascendTroopPrice` 1.0, `ascendSkillCd` 0.85, `ascendPrice`.
     - `awakenLevel` is the items' level (`itemLevel`) plus, at Bangkit 3, the levels bought (`ascended`, saved), so
       every reader (the stats, the nine awakening skills, the looks, the telemetry's `levels`) sees 4 and 5 with no
       second level to pass round. The item rules (`capOf`, `whyNot`, the progress) already stop at `maxAwaken`, so
       nothing more fits. HP and MP keep +25% of the base a level; damage (a heal) ×1.25 a level; the price doesn't
       rise; the awakening skill keeps Bangkit 3's numbers and MP and its cooldown is ×0.85 a level (#88's nine, as the
       brief says).
     - "(Maks)" moved from Bangkit 3 to Bangkit 5 (`awakenName`): at 3 the book now says "Bangkit 4: beli di Toko".
     - The section is the Toko's facing page while nothing is picked, not a fifth tab and not on the left page beside
       the goods (which pusaka-rules' shelf is changing): the store opens on it, the nine rows fit, and its code is its
       own file. The help lines that page held shrank to two small ones under it; what they said is on each card.
     - The colours: Bangkit 4 violet #8E44FF and Bangkit 5 white #F2F6FF, as designed, on all that is round the troop.
       Checked against skills.dart's colours, white would clash on the shots (Spellbreaker's silver arrow, the healers'
       white smite that only the heal's colour tells from a heal) and violet with Arcane Blast's orb, so a troop's
       shots, orbs and hit bursts stay Bangkit 3's gold past it (`_fxColor`); the awakening's own burst takes the new
       colour.
     - The unused bag (the owner's w68-71 save: 1-3 items short of Bangkit 3 with 29-48 of each in the bag): a row
       below Bangkit 3 whose next awakening the bag holds says "Bisa Bangkit n dari tas" and turns to the Tas page, and
       the Tas tab has a dot while a fielded type could awaken from the bag. Counts only, so two types may count the
       same items.
     - Its balance is not weighed here (FAST LANE): the QA cycle with the tide replays it (the worker's PROBE PLAN).
144. **Each test file keeps the game's files in a temp dir of its own** (an improvement reported by necro-pair,
     2026-10-02: hud_test's start-button test sometimes read its Auto toggle back off; testing.md "Where the tests'
     files go"):
     - The cause: `flutter test` runs test files at once, each in a process of its own, and they all shared the queue
       job's one HOME (the runner's fixed HOME per project dir). Eleven files boot a `TdGame`, and booting saves
       settings.json (the telemetry's install id), as does any toggle a test presses; a file that had loaded the
       settings before hud_test pressed Auto then saved them back over it. Two of four suites on the same code failed
       on `(b.autoStart.on, loadSettings().autoStart)` = `(true, false)`.
     - The fix: `test/flutter_test_config.dart`, which Flutter runs around every test file's `main()`, sets
       `testDataDir` (lib/save.dart) to a fresh `$TMPDIR/td_data_XXXXXX` and deletes it after the file's last test.
       `dataFile` takes it before `dataDirFor`, so save.json, settings.json, the scores and the telemetry of one test
       file can't race with another's, and no test ever writes HOME's folder, whoever runs it.
     - The hook is one `@visibleForTesting` variable, null in the app: the app's paths (decision 133) don't change.
       A test that reads those paths (save_test's `initDataDir`) turns it off for itself and back on after.
     - The queue's own HOME stays as a second fence. The tests that already pass their own temp file (the settings,
       the scores, the telemetry's sinks) keep it: they test the `file` parameter, and nothing there juggled HOME.
145. **The macOS and Android builds come from `scripts/release-build.sh`, the Windows and Linux ones from a release
     workflow, and the owner pushes them all with butler** (release job J10 without its push script, plus J11's
     workflow as a file only; the orchestrator's brief, 2026-10-02; itch-page.md "Build checklist" and "Pushing
     builds", dev-workflow.md "Release build"):
     - Why the owner pushes: the agents' permission check refused an earlier `scripts/itch-push.sh` as public
       publishing (2026-10-01). So the script stages the builds and prints the owner's butler commands (`butler push
       --dry-run`, `butler push … --userversion <X.Y.Z+N> --if-changed`, `butler status triasbrata/path-of-hero`),
       and runs none. butler takes the key from `BUTLER_API_KEY`, set by the owner; the script reads no key or
       password file.
     - Why the owner builds: a build needs the network (flutter_soloud's build hook downloads the Xiph libraries,
       Gradle its plugins), which agent shells lack. Agents run only `--dry-run`, which runs no flutter, ditto,
       lipo, codesign or apksigner and writes nothing, and `check`.
     - The version is pubspec.yaml's: the folders are `dist/PathOfHero-<platform>-X.Y.Z/`, butler's `--userversion`
       is `X.Y.Z+N`. `dist/` is gitignored.
     - A release ships only what an allowlist names (itch-page.md "What a build ships"; `ALLOWED_ASSETS` in the
       script, and its test checks the two agree). It is checked on `assets/` before building and on what the build
       bundled after. floors.png and the 10 free Raven icons are refused by name and by their bytes (sha256 from git
       history), because our own icons took the Raven names (136).
     - Android: a missing `key.properties` fails before anything is built, Gradle's debug-key warning fails the
       build, and every signer of the APK must be our release key's SHA-256. So a debug-signed APK is never staged
       (132). The APK is staged alone in a folder: itch serves a one-file build as the file itself (a phone needs the
       .apk, not a zip), and pushing the folder keeps butler, which unpacks a pushed zip, from unpacking the APK. Its
       notices are in the game (Lisensi).
     - macOS: every binary must hold arm64 and x86_64 (the page promises Intel too), `ditto` keeps the frameworks'
       symlinks, and `codesign --verify --deep --strict` checks the staged app. The folder is pushed, not zipped
       (release plan §4.1).
     - Flutter must be 3.47.5, the version CI pins (release plan R7). The script's test caught a universal check that
       refused `x86_64 arm64` before any real build ran it.
     - The workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) builds, stages with the notices, checks the bundled assets and
       uploads the staged builds as artifacts kept 1 day. It has no butler step and no secrets, each job is guarded to
       `triasbrata/tower-defense`, every action is pinned by its commit SHA, and it may only read the repo (release
       plan R2, R10).
       - Linux's artifact is a tar, which keeps the executable bit that an artifact's zip drops.
       - Windows gets the VC++ runtime's three DLLs from Visual Studio's redist folder (app-local deployment).
       - It needs the owner to push the repo and enable Actions; agents never push.
     - Not done here: pinning flutter_soloud's prebuilt tag (release plan R6), a `.itch.toml`, and the smoke tests on
       each OS (J12).
146. **On a phone the game pauses when it goes to the background, and stays paused when the player comes back**
     (app-identity's finding under decisions-log 133; the orchestrator's default, 2026-10-02, which the owner was told
     and didn't object to; ui-hud.md "A phone in the background pauses", dev-workflow.md "App identity"):
     - #93 (decision 130) keeps the game running while the window is hidden or unfocused, with a 30 Hz timer and
       Flame's `pauseWhenBackgrounded` off. The owner asked that for the desktop ("kalau window tidak focus juga game
       tetap berjalan", "keep running while minimized"), but the same timer ran on Android and iOS: a backgrounded
       phone game fought on, and Auto could start waves, until Android ended it. That drains the battery, and the
       player loses troops while away.
     - Android and iOS (`hidden` or `paused`): the game pauses as the player's own pause (as by the pause button, not
       "by the book"), mid-wave or between waves, where the auto start's countdown then waits; Flame's own
       `pauseWhenBackgrounded` is on, so its loop stops and no timer runs. Back, it stays paused under "Pause" until
       the player resumes it, even when the book had paused the wave: coming back to a running fight unseen would
       cost what the pause saved. `inactive` alone (the notification shade, a call's banner) pauses nothing.
     - The desktop and the web are unchanged, as the job asked: #93's timer runs the hidden game. The check
       excludes the web by name, since a phone's browser reports android as its platform.
     - One platform check (`_pausesInBackground`, main.dart: `defaultTargetPlatform` android or iOS, not `kIsWeb`)
       and a named switch, `pauseInBackgroundOnMobile = true`; off, a phone runs in the background as the desktop.
     - The between-waves save on going to the background (133) stays, on every platform.
     - `flutter test` reports android unless a test sets the platform, so the desktop's lifecycle tests now run as
       macOS (`TargetPlatformVariant`), and the phone's as Android and iOS.
147. **On a phone the background silences the game's music and effects; back, they go on, the music where it was**
     (android-bg's follow-up under decision 146; the orchestrator's default, 2026-10-02, told to the owner; ui-hud.md
     "A phone in the background is silent"):
     - After 146 a backgrounded phone game paused, but flutter_soloud was never told: the music looped on after the
       player had left, a bug players notice at once. With Flame's loop stopped even the paused game's 40% duck
       wasn't applied.
     - Android and iOS (`hidden`, `paused`, and `detached`): every sound holds where it is, on the welcome screen and
       after a game over too. Back (`inactive`, `resumed`) the sound goes on, though the game stays paused (146), at
       the player's own volumes: a volume set to 0 on Pengaturan stays silent. `inactive` alone holds nothing.
     - Desktop and web are unchanged: #93 keeps a hidden window's game, and so its sound, running on purpose.
     - The same platform check as 146 (`_onPhone`, main.dart) and its own switch, `muteInBackgroundOnMobile = true`.
     - How: flutter_soloud 5.1.2 has no pause for everything (`stopAudioDevice` stops the device but leaves the
       voices playing, and a play, an unpause or the end of an OS interruption, like a call, can start it again
       with them). So the hold pauses the loops that play, which keep their place (their fades wait too), and sets the
       global volume to 0 for an effect still sounding; with nothing playing SoLoud stops the device by itself after
       500 ms, so the phone keeps no audio running. No effect starts meanwhile, nor a cross-fade's loop. Nothing is
       stopped or reloaded.
     - Testable: `Sounds` now plays through `Sounds.output`, a `SoundOutput` that names the effects and loops
       (`SoLoudOutput` in the game). Tests can't load SoLoud's native library, so pause_test.dart puts a fake there
       and checks what would be heard through the real lifecycle messages.
148. **flutter_soloud's Xiph prebuilds are pinned to release v1.0.2, and every desktop build carries an `.itch.toml`**
     (the orchestrator's job release-pin, 2026-10-02: release plan R6 and the two items decision 145 left undone;
     itch-page.md "Pinned binaries", "The itch app's launch manifest" and "Build checklist", dev-workflow.md "Release
     build"):
     - flutter_soloud 5.1.2's build hook downloaded libogg, libvorbis, libopus and libFLAC from
       `alnitak/flutter_soloud_prebuilds`'s `latest` release, so two builds of one commit could link different
       third-party binaries into a build people may pay for. pubspec.yaml now sets `hooks: user_defines:
       flutter_soloud: prebuild_tag: v1.0.2`, which the hook reads (`input.userDefines['prebuild_tag']`).
     - v1.0.2 was found offline, not guessed: the hook's own records in the pub cache copy
       (`.dart_tool/flutter_soloud/xiph/prebuild/{,include/,macos/}flutter_soloud_prebuild_version.txt`, written
       2026-09-27 10:06 from the `latest` redirect) all say v1.0.2, and the repo's hook runs linked that folder. With
       the pin and that cache the hook downloads nothing; macOS's libraries are universal.
     - The tag must carry its `v`: the hook deletes a cached folder whose record differs from the tag, and `1.0.2`
       never matches the record `v1.0.2`. So `scripts/release-build.sh` (and `check`, which the workflow runs) refuses
       a pubspec without a `vX.Y.Z` pin, and a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt (`tool/third_party_notices.py` writes the tag
       from pubspec.yaml) or CREDITS.md that doesn't name it. After each build, and in the workflow with `check
       --xiph <os>`, the hook's records for that platform must say the pin: on a fresh runner a hook that ignored it
       would have recorded what `latest` was.
     - The release checks R6 asked for: macOS's universal check now finds each framework's binary by its Info.plist
       and fails on a declared one that's missing (the frameworks under `Contents/Frameworks` were already covered,
       native assets' `flutter_soloud_plugin` and `objective_c` included, as long as the binary bears the
       framework's name). Android: `zipalign -c -P 16 -v 4` (build-tools 35+; this Mac has 36.0.0) and every 64-bit
       library's ELF LOAD segments aligned to 16 KB. Linux (the workflow): each ELF file's newest `GLIBC_` and
       `GLIBCXX_` and the two floors, information only; the old line read `lib/*.so` and so missed the Xiph libraries,
       which the hook bundles by their SONAME (`libFLAC.so.14`).
     - `.itch.toml` (repo root): one `play` action each for `osx` (`Path of Hero.app`), `windows`
       (`tower_defense.exe`) and `linux` (`tower_defense`), copied to the root of the mac, windows and linux builds,
       not into Android's (the APK stays alone). The Windows artifact sets `include-hidden-files: true`, since
       upload-artifact drops dotfiles by default.
     - A tag names a release, not its bytes: hashing the archives would need a hook of our own. Not done.
149. **The Pusaka are seen in battle: a ring and an icon on every troop of a bound type, the Grail's cut-in once a
     wave, the saves and the returns in the log, one line on "MENANG!", and build names** (the owner, 2026-10-01:
     "sekarang user bener bener nga ada ngerasa apapun dari penggunaan artefaknya"; the design "Pusaka Jenis + Peti
     Bos", <agents>/reports/artefact-roguelike-design.md, part P2 "Bukti", §3.8 and the critique's M4;
     ui-hud.md "The Pusaka in battle", loot-items-relics.md "Pusaka"):
     - Why: P1a (138) made the Pusaka strong and type-wide, but on the field nothing told a bound type from any other,
       a Grail save looked like a holy burst among many, and a relic sent back to the bag by a fall was silent. P2 shows
       that strength.
     - On the field: a 1 px ring in the Pusaka's colour under the feet of every living troop of a bound type, and the
       Pusaka's icon left of its HP bar, past the small relics it holds. The colours keep off the awakening's blue,
       crimson, gold, violet (Bangkit 4) and white (Bangkit 5) and off the grass's green: Dragon Heart ember orange,
       Dawn Star pink, God's Thunder lemon (its leaps' yellow), the Grail cyan, Void Eye all but black. They are a first
       pass for the owner to tune. Both are drawn for 32+ troops every frame without a Paint per troop: the type →
       Pusaka map is made once a frame and the five ring paints once.
     - The Grail's cut-in, on the wave's first save only ("Grail menyelamatkan Kael Drake!"): a slim plate under the
       top rows for 1.6 s. It pauses nothing and takes no press. Later saves get a log line each but no cut-in, so a
       boss wave with six saves doesn't flash six times. It is not behind "Sorotan Hero", which is the Heroes'.
     - The battle log, under its own chip "Pusaka": a line for each Grail save (`GrailSaved`); a second row under a
       fall for the small relics it sent back ("Amarah kembali ke tas", from 138's `TroopFell.relics`); and at a won
       wave the full report (`PusakaReport`, right before the win's line), a row for each bound Pusaka with its
       counter and one for the relics back. Neither new event is passed on to the telemetry, whose wave record has the
       same counts, so `eventVersion` and `telemetryVersion` stay.
     - "MENANG!" gets one line, because the popup lasts `victoryTime` 2.4 s (M4): the best counter and the relics back,
       "Pusaka: Grail 6 selamat - Kembali ke tas: Amarah ×2". The best counter is troops kept alive first (the Grail's
       kept saves or Dragon Heart's blows lived through), since a life saved is what the player can see; else the most
       damage or healing added. The line fits 361 px, shrinking from 18 px to 12 px before it is cut. It uses " - ":
       the HUD's font has "×" but no "·", "★" or "→".
     - Build names, the type's name and the Pusaka's epithet, on the type's Pasukan row (its top band, clear of the Lepas
       chip and P1b's badge in the price column) and on its troops' plates: "Templar Undying" (Grail), "Templar
       Raksasa" (Dragon Heart) and "Penyihir Badai" (God's Thunder), as the design named them, plus "Pendeta Fajar"
       (Dawn Star) and "Pemanah Hampa" (Void Eye). The table (`buildEpithets`) is in pusaka.dart beside the Pusaka list;
       P3's Langka add theirs.
     - Not here: the chest popup's header (P3 reads `Game.lastPusaka`), and any balance change. QA cycle's probe plan:
       reports/pusaka-bukti.md "PROBE PLAN" (UI shots only).
150. **Hero Gugur: a fallen Hero is kept, and the Toko calls it back between waves for about one wave's income**
     (#92 part 3; the owner, 2026-09-30: "iya bener duitnya itu aku bingung di buat untuk apa karna tanpa artefak shop
     juga lawan masi bisa di atasi dengan mudah", and Heroes falling at wave 66 was a loss the owner cared about;
     late-game-design.md §2 part 3; units-and-combat.md "Hero Gugur", ui-hud.md "Toko page"):
     - The owner hasn't answered the design's decision 5, so the orchestrator built its default c: the replace button
       (142), Bangkit 4-5 (143) and this. Every number is a named constant in lib/recall.dart: the price is
       `heroRecallK` 2500 × (1 + `killGoldGrowth`)^(wave − 1), to `heroRecallRound` 1,000 (57k at wave 65, 80k at 72,
       313k at 100), so it grows with the kill gold and stays about one wave's income.
     - A Hero that falls is kept (`fallenHeroes`, saved) with its name, type, rolled attributes and own skill, and the
       recall brings that same Hero back: nothing rolled, no dice drawn, so a run's later Heroes and names stay as
       they were. Its stats are its type's as they are now (the items, Bangkit 4-5, the type's Pusaka); its 2 relic
       slots are empty, since its relics went back to the bag when it fell ("Relik tidak ikut (ada di tas)").
     - The design said a Resurrection removes the entry, but Resurrection never raises a Hero (`_revivable`, "not a
       Hero"), so the only way back is the recall, and only it takes an entry out (a test pins that Resurrection leaves
       a fallen Hero alone).
     - One gate: the refusals go through army-cap's and the tide's `buyRefusal` (it gained an optional `price` and a
       `hero` check), after the store's own (`_closed` first, as the design orders it): the roster ("Jenis penuh 4/4:
       lepas satu jenis dulu", which a type released since its Hero fell meets), the army ("Pasukan penuh 32/32",
       "Kapasitas penuh"), "Hero sudah 5", then "Emas kurang" against the recall's price, not the troop's. A recalled
       Hero counts in `heroMax`, so the 10th waves' crowning still stops at 5.
     - It goes where `autoPlace` would send a troop (its cell search and line-up are shared helpers now), but it isn't
       a troop bought: no `Bought`, its own `HeroRecalled` event and `gold.recallSpent`, as Bangkit's `Ascended` and
       `ascendSpent`. The new Hero's splash says "<nama> kembali!".
     - Where: the Toko's facing page, which bangkit45 gave the 9 Bangkit rows, now has two tabs across its top,
       "Bangkit 4-5" (first) and "Hero Gugur (n)". The design asked for a section beside Bangkit's; under the 9 rows a
       phone's page had no room, and the left page is the goods (whose artefact shelf peti-bos is closing). Rows past
       what fits go on pages ("<" n/m ">"), since every 10th wave can crown one and a long run can lose many.
     - Its balance is not weighed here (FAST LANE): the worker's PROBE PLAN gives the QA cycle's Bangkit probe a recall
       arm.
151. **The Tas page binds the Pusaka: their slots with stars, a Gudang strip, and on the facing page a row for each
     troop type with Pasang or Pindah, the type's Pusaka now and what the binding would change** (the design "Pusaka
     Jenis + Peti Bos", <agents>/reports/artefact-roguelike-design.md, part P1b, with the critique's H1 and
     M6; ui-hud.md "Tas", loot-items-relics.md "Pusaka" and "What a Tas row previews"):
     - Why: P1a (138) made the artefacts type-wide Pusaka, but only `bindPusaka` could bind one; the book had no way
       to. P1b is that way, between waves only, in two taps: the Pusaka's slot, then a type's row.
     - The left page: a slot for each Pusaka ("★2", or "-" and a ghost while not owned; the Toko's shelf only while
       it is open or one is owned), a "Gudang" strip under them with the unbound ones, and a line for the one picked
       (where it is, and for a Gudang one "Jual +15k", armed "Yakin? +15k" on the first tap: P1a's sale at half the
       base price). The facing page lists every troop type: its Pusaka now, the stars, the action ("Pasang" when its
       binding is free, "Pindah" with the coin and "38k" at wave 86, "Lepas ke Gudang" on its own type), the stat it changes with the
       type's total ("HP 580 → 927 ×13 Templar (+4.511)") and, when the HP changes, the next boss's blows it lives
       through ("Tahan pukulan bos (gel. 90): 0 → 1", H1). A refusal greys the row and says why in red, mid-wave
       too.
     - The numbers are the field's: `statsOf` times the Hero's aura (×1.15 while a Hero lives), what a troop's plate
       shows, so the owner's 580 reads 580. The design's "580 → 928 (+4.524)" was 580 × 1.6; the game rounds the
       book's 504 × 1.6 to 806 and then adds the aura, 927 (+4.511 for 13). The Pasukan row still shows the book's
       stats, as before.
     - Every Pasukan row of a bound type gets the Pusaka's icon and stars, bottom right in its price column (clear of
       pusaka-bukti's build name in the top band and army-cap's Lepas chip at the top right), faded while none of the
       type lives ("tidur"). Its hover shows the Pusaka's tooltip, which now leads with the type-wide total, "13
       Templar: +4.511 HP, +121 HP/detik" (M6: the sum, not one troop's factor), as the Toko's card does. The Toko
       says "Dimiliki ★2" on an owned one's Beli.
     - The one-time message for an old save's suggested bindings is shown once, when the game comes in, beside the
       limit notes (8 s), and marked shown like them, so a game reopened says nothing twice. Batal and OK stay on the
       Tas page while the suggestion stands, and a wave begun keeps it. The design put Batal and OK in the message,
       but the message window closes on any press.
     - The HUD's font has "×" but no "★", "·" or "→", so the board's text draws "★" as the pack's star icon
       (ui_icons.png), sized to the line; the design's "·" is the coin icon before the price and its "→" the drawn

153. **A wave whose monsters drift away from the base, or that runs on 180 s after its last spawn or life lost, marches;
     the kite hold that would stop the drift is a switch, off** (qa-3's FINDING, 2026-10-02, "a near-wiped wave never
     ends"; the orchestrator chose the switch off after the repro; units-and-combat.md "Stalled waves" and "Long range
     kite", camera-and-field.md, telemetry.md):
     - The stall: after a near-wipe (47 of 48 fallen by ~300 s) a lone wizard stood 104 px right of a skeleton archer
       mini boss. Its kite step backs off along (troop − foe), limited only on the left (`_rearEdge`), so it backed off
       right and the boss followed to its own shorter reach: both went right 2,160 px every 120 s with the view in
       tow, 0 lives lost, the wave still on at the 600 s cap. `_watchStall`'s "what is left" (HP + way to the base)
       fell with every blow (the boss lost ~10% of its HP every 2 min), so it never stalled. About 1 play in 230–450
       of the late replays (w48–100), always after a near-wipe, on ee6a43d, 145cc65 and 14437d0 (so before #90,
       whose escort makes near-wipes more common); also an archer led a greatsword skeleton boss off the same way.
     - The stall watch, two more ways to stall (both named constants): while the front (the least way to the base of
       any of the wave's own monsters) stands more than `stallDrift` 10 tiles past its low since the last spawn,
       death or leak, a new low of "what is left" is no progress, so `stallTime` later they march (10 tiles: twice
       Death Leap's reach, ten 1-tile shoves); and `stallOvertime` 180 s after the last spawn or the last life lost
       they march whatever else. None of the owner's 149 waves of telemetry (w1–86, none marched) went on much over
       110 s after its last spawn, by its spawn count. `Marched.why` (`MarchCause`: `stalled`, `drifting`,
       `overtime`) says which, for the listeners; the wave record keeps only the time, as before.
     - The kite hold (`Game.holdPastFoe`): on, a troop past its foe keeps its x and only steps aside. The brief asked
       for it; the repro said no. #85's way, a limit at `rightLimit`, doesn't bind here, because the view follows the
       fight and the limit with it. The hold binds, and where it does, after a near-wipe, it takes away the last
       troops' only defence. The repro states on 14437d0 with this change, the same dice (k = seed·1000 + wave·10 + rep),
       secs into the wave:

       | state | 14437d0 (qa-3) | hold on | hold off (the default) |
       |---|---|---|---|
       | live86 s3-w90-r2 | STALL at 600 s, 47 fell | LOST at 308 s, all 48 fell | won at 428 s, overtime march, 46 fell, 1 life |
       | live86 s2-w90-r3 | (stalled on ee6a43d, 145cc65) | won at 373 s, overtime march, 43 fell, 1 life | won at 368 s, the same |
       | live86 s3-w99-r3 | (stalled on 145cc65) | LOST at 350 s, all 48 fell | won at 331 s, no march, 36 fell |

       The last troop falling ends the run (`wipedOut`), so the hold turned two stalls into game overs where the stall
       watch alone wins them. One play each, and a replay diverges as soon as one tick differs, so the QA cycle
       weighs it; if its numbers don't argue for the hold, a later job deletes it.
     - Ordinary waves don't change: 17 replayed waves (live86 w87–99 near full armies, auto2 w12–28) played the same
       to the tick with the hold on and off, the hold binding 0 troop-ticks, and none marched. On this branch's own
       base the repro dice no longer near-wipe (s2-w90-r3 is won at 258 s, 5 fell), so the repro ran on 14437d0.
     - Tests: test/kite_stall_test.dart (the drift ended by a march within `stallDrift` + `stallTime`'s walk, the hold
       on standing its ground and stepping only aside, a drift stalling while HP falls, a slow fight with knockbacks
       not stalling before `stallOvertime`, a life lost starting the overtime afresh, the old stall unchanged).
       FAST LANE: no balance probe before the merge; reports/kite-stall.md "PROBE PLAN" (main vs branch, and the
       branch with the hold on vs off).

155. **The three Legenda Pusaka change a rule: Dragon Crown caps every blow its type takes at 60% of the max HP, Oath
     of One cuts the roster to 2 for x1.5, Alliance opens it to 6 for +5% a type** (the artefact redesign's P5;
     reports/artefact-roguelike-design.md §3.4, §3.5, §3.10, §6 P5, §8 M3; loot-items-relics.md "Legenda", ui-hud.md
     "Tas" and "Peti Bos"):
     - Owner decision 7 is unanswered, so its default (a) is built: the Legenda come from the boss's chest from wave
       `legendFrom` 20, ★1 only (`legendStars`, `maxStars`), each at most once a run, at most one oath. This **amends
       152**'s (7): from wave 20 a Legenda roll deals a Legenda; before it, or once all three are found, it steps down
       to an Epik as before.
     - **Dragon Crown** (bound to a type): its own check at the end of `_hurt`, after every other cut, never a
       `Status.cap` (critique M3: a cap effect ends with its wave, a Grail save's would replace it, and Bastion fires
       only while no cap is on). A Grail save's untouchable and Bastion's 8% still go under it, and Bastion still fires.
       It caps a blow, it saves no life: from under 60% the next blow still kills. `crownCap` 0.6.
     - **The oaths** (Sumpah, `RelicScope.army`): the whole army's at once, on no type, never in the Gudang, never sold,
       never taken off. The roster's limit is read in ONE place, `Game.rosterLimit` (the board's `typeLimit`, or the
       oath's); every reader (the rules, the Pasukan page, the troop counter, the row chips) goes through it. With no
       board limit an oath sets none. Oath of One: the limit 2, and HP and damage x1.5 while the roster holds 2 or
       fewer; above it the oath waits ("Sumpah menunggu: sisakan 2 jenis"): Lepas jenis is the way down, nothing
       is cut. Alliance: the limit 6, +5% HP and damage for each roster type with a troop alive. The multiplier
       (`_oathK`) is applied last in `statsOf`, so the book and the field agree, and every troop is refit when it moves
       (`_oathWatch`, every tick and after each change between waves). The save's roster now loads before the troops'
       stats, so an oath works on load.

       found Legenda is never offered again, even once sold; one oath found keeps the other off the cards, and a chest
       rolled before then shows a Serpihan in its place.

156. **Disarm weakens one monster at most once in 30 s, and Lifeline lifts a troop below half its HP** (qa-3's two
     FINDINGs, 2026-10-02; the owner wants the late game to push back, "biar ada perlawanan"; units-and-combat.md
     "Awakening skills"; reports/disarm-tune.md):
     - **Disarm** was far too strong on the mini boss and boss waves: with only Disarm on, at natural levels, the army
       lost 47% fewer troops (qa-3 on 14437d0: -1.87 ± 0.61 a wave, 87 pairs), where the design's per-type target is
       10-15%. Each soldier re-weakened "the strongest foe not already weakened as strongly", so ten soldiers kept the
       mini boss or the boss under it nearly the whole fight.
     - **The window:** a foe Disarmed can't be Disarmed again, by any soldier, for `disarmK.again` 30 s from the cast
       (`Unit.disarmedAt`, as Impale's `interruptedAt`). A soldier whose strongest foe is inside its window strikes the
       next one, so the casts still come as often; one foe is just weakened at most 6 of every 30 s. The blow, the
       weaken (0.9 / 0.85 / 0.8, the boss rank 0.95 / 0.93 / 0.9, 6 s) and the cooldown are as they were: the window
       takes out the mechanism itself, and the book's numbers still say what a cast does.
     - **Measured** (the natonly set: main's saved states, every mini boss wave 12-39 of auto seeds 1-6 and auto2 seeds
       7-14, natural levels, only Disarm on vs all off, same dice; on main 73c611d + the window): fell 4.53 → 3.74 a
       wave, -0.79 ± 0.53 (**-17.5% ± 11.6%**), 87 pairs, better/worse 30/29 (qa-3's 40/18), lives -0.02 ± 0.02.
       By set: auto -33% ± 18%, auto2 +1% ± 12%. Two wave-30 states (boss and mini boss) give most of it; without
       them it is about -8%. The slots are under Disarm 20% of their time (the window's cap); a wave's Disarms go to
       the mini boss 1.15, the boss 0.30, high elites 5.7, elites 7.5, normals 6.6; 3.2 casts a soldier a wave (3.55
       before).
     - **Unbroken** (qa-3's second step, `unbrokenK.self` 0.25 / 0.3 / 0.35 → 0.2 / 0.25 / 0.3) is unchanged: it was
       to follow only if the nine together stayed above about -20% with Disarm in range, and that is left to the QA
       cycle (at natural levels the nine are Disarm and Unbroken, which was -4% ± 4% alone).
     - **Lifeline** hardly fired: 0.08 casts a priest a wave at Bangkit 3 (qa-3), under awaken-b2's bar of ~0.3.
       Counting how often a troop comes into peril for some priest (rule as it was 1.20 a priest a wave) with one of
       its five conditions loosened at a time: below 40% HP 2.04, below 50% 3.45, hit in the last 2 s, a foe within 2
       tiles, 1+ tile from the priest or 2 tiles more reach 1.20-1.25. Only `below` moves it, so `lifelineK.below` is
       now 0.5 (the book: "Tarik pasukan terluka (< 50% HP) ke sisinya"; "sekarat" no longer fit). At Bangkit 3
       (priest only, auto seeds 1-3 and auto2 8-11, 60 pairs): 0.53 casts a priest a wave, fell 1.22 → 1.25, +2.7% ±
       14.4%, lives unchanged. The asked 1-3 casts are out of one condition's reach: only ~15% of the perils become a
       cast (a priest mid-heal, 0.6 s of each attack, skips its skills; the 0.25 s think; and the priests' heals lift
       most troops out of peril first).
     - FAST LANE: the brief allowed 6 short tuning probes, and these were all of them (each under 2.5 min of queue
       time; the tools are <agents>/probes/disarm-tune/). The QA cycle weighs both against main
       (reports/disarm-tune.md "PROBE PLAN").
157. **Bought packs never go into `raw_assets/`; the public repo gets placeholder art drawn from a manifest of the

     di bilang di websitenya tidak boleh di share ulang assetnya", i.e. a bought pack must not be put in raw_assets/,
     since the stores say its files must not be re-shared; the release plan's J6, rescoped, and J7; assets.md
     "Placeholder art"):

       `assets/` here is the licensed art's only source. The importers stay as the record of how each file was made.

       their bytes, image size, the frame grid the code cuts, the feet and the Soldier's baked shadow, and
       `tool/assets.sha256` their sha256s (hashes can be public). `python3 tool/asset_manifest.py` writes both from

       public `.gitignore` gets `tool/placeholders.gitignore`. It refuses to write over any file git tracks, so it
       never writes into this repo's `assets/`. `python3 tool/test_gen_placeholders.py` tests it in temp dirs.
     - **No placeholder font** (the orchestrator, 2026-10-02): the game's font becomes the open Pixelify Sans (SIL OFL
       1.1, decisions-log 158), committed for real and public as it is. Kenmi's font.ttf stays in the manifest until
       it leaves `assets/`.
     - **`@Tags(['art'])`** (dart_test.yaml) marks the tests that need the real art. A public clone runs `flutter
       test -x art` on its placeholders (testing.md "Placeholder art").
158. **The game's font is Pixelify Sans (SIL OFL 1.1), the itch page's header font; Kenmi's 5×9 is no longer used**
     (the owner, 2026-10-02: "game text sepertinya perlu di ganti ke header itch.io text dari google font": the game's
     text in the itch page's header font, the Google Font; ui-hud.md "The font", assets.md, CREDITS.md "The font"):
     - **All game text**, not only titles: every `TextStyle` in lib/ is `hudStyle` (lib/hud_font.dart), pubspec.yaml's
       family `PixelifySans`. Body text at weight 500, titles at 700 (the itch page's pair; the book's page titles,
       "MENANG!", the welcome title, the score screens' titles and "Pause", the ribbons, the tooltips' and the drop
       popup's titles, the Lisensi page's headings). The font is variable (wght 400-700) and `fontWeight` sets its axis.
     - **The file** is google/fonts' `ofl/pixelifysans/PixelifySans[wght].ttf` at commit 9710da1e (2026-09-30),
       unmodified, as `assets/fonts/PixelifySans.ttf` (sha256 9ba86cd0…89e8a5), with its `OFL.txt` as
       `assets/fonts/OFL-PixelifySans.txt`. `assets/fonts/font.ttf` (Kenmi's, "can not redistribute") is out of
       pubspec.yaml and stays on disk while the owner's game runs from main: removable later (deleted on
       2026-10-02 by drop-old-font).
     - **Why it also helps:** the OFL lets the font ship in the game and sit in the public repository, so the public
       export needs no placeholder font (open-source-release-plan.md §3.4, §3.5 #2 and #3 now allow exactly these two
       files). The licence is bundled (pubspec.yaml assets), on the Lisensi page (`fontLicence`, read from the
       bundled file), in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt part 3 and CREDITS.md; LICENSE §6a no longer names the font, and §6d
       says it stays under the OFL (the owner may reword it). The itch page's credits name it (description.html).
     - **Sizes:** the HUD's sizes stay the old face's; the text draws at 0.8 × them (`hudFontScale`). Pixelify Sans is
       about 1.25× as wide at one size (its lower case 5 font pixels tall, the old one's 3), so at 0.8 it runs about
       as wide and no layout's numbers change.
     - **Crispness:** sizes are not snapped to whole screen pixels per font pixel. The face is not a strict bitmap
       (strokes 1.11-1.4 grid pixels, glyphs half a pixel off the advance grid), so no size has every edge on a pixel,
       and whole-pixel sizes measured no sharper (Flutter at 2× device pixels: 59% of a line's inked pixels
       partly covered at 2.0 device px per font pixel, 54% at 2.25, 46% at both 2.75 and 3.0, at 500). Snapping would move texts in 5.5 px steps on a Retina
       Mac and break the layouts.
     - **Glyphs:** it has a real space (the probes' `spaced` patch and the space notes are gone), "·", "–", "—", "…",
       "#" and accents, but no "★" or "→" (still drawn: the ui_icons star, the drawn arrow). "·" now separates the
       two lines whose " - " stood in for it: "Pasukan 20/32 · Auto ditahan" and the "MENANG!" Pusaka line. Names stay
       ASCII. The cmap tests read the new font (`fontChars`, test/hud_font.dart).
     - (Amended by 179, 2026-10-03.) The game's font is now Poh Sans, this file with 13 glyphs redrawn; Pixelify Sans
       stays the source (`tool/fonts/PixelifySans.ttf`, the same bytes) and is no longer bundled.
159. **One copy of the game at a time on macOS: a later copy quits before Flutter starts** (the owner saw "2 app yang
     jalan"; the orchestrator's `ps`, 2026-10-02 08:14 and 08:17; dev-workflow.md "One copy of the game";
     reports/single-instance.md):
     - **The cause:** `flutter run -d macos` starts the app's executable itself, then `open <bundle>` to bring it to the
       front (flutter_tools' `MacOSDevice.onAttached`, whose own comment admits there is no way to know when `open`
       can find the process). When LaunchServices doesn't know flutter's copy yet, `open` launches a second one, ppid 1,
       about 1 s later. Both load and write the same save, and only flutter's gets hot reload.
     - **The fix is in the game, not the script**, so it holds for every start (dev-macos.sh, the release, Finder, a
       build from another folder with the same bundle id): `SingleInstance` in `macos/Runner/AppDelegate.swift` runs in
       `AppDelegate.main()` before `NSApplicationMain`, takes an exclusive `flock` on `instance.lock` in the container's
       Application Support, and a copy that finds it held logs why, asks the other copy to the front (best effort,
       macOS 14+ may decline) and exits 0. The first copy wins, and flutter's starts first.
     - **A lock rather than LaunchServices's running apps** (`NSRunningApplication`, the brief's first idea): the bug is
       LaunchServices not knowing the first copy, a lock dies with its process (no zombie or crash blocks a start), and
       two copies started together can't both quit. `NSRunningApplication` only finds the copy to bring forward.
     - **dev-macos.sh** stops with exit 1 before the build while a `tower_defense` runs, listing it: that catches a copy
       built before the guard, which holds no lock (the stray of the old bug among them). It never kills one: the
       owner may be playing in it. No watcher that quits strays: with the guard none is left to quit.
     - Checked without building the app: the file typechecks against Flutter 3.47.5's FlutterMacOS (arm64 and x86_64,
       Swift 5 and 6), and the same file built against a stub FlutterMacOS with a test bundle id quit a second copy at
       once and let a new one start after `kill -9` of the first. The owner checks it on the next start (one
       `MacOS/tower_defense`, its parent `flutter run`).
160. **The public repo's export is a script, a dry run that stages, checks and commits locally; nothing is pushed**
     (release plan J8; itch-page.md "The public repo"; reports/export-public.md):
     - **`scripts/export-public.sh <ref> <staging-dir>`** (the work in `scripts/export_public.py`): `git archive`, an

161. **The army cap's warning: while the army is full at 32 and the tide is on, the game says so every 5 waves**
     (qa-4's FINDING, 2026-10-02: on the owner's w63 save, with the cap and the tide together, the army lost nobody
     until it was down at the cap, then went in 2-3 waves (3 of 6 runs over by w78-84); the owner's goals: a cap of 32,
     a late game that pushes back, "biar ada perlawanan", gold that matters; units-and-combat.md "The tide", ui-hud.md
     "Message window", reports/tide-slope.md):
     - **The warning** (qa-4's suggestion c, built whatever the numbers): "Pasukan penuh: batas 32 - Pasang +87%" /
       "Kuatkan jenis di Toko (Bangkit)" in the message window for 8 s, between waves once the "MENANG!" popup is
       over (not before the game's first win since it came in: a loaded save has its notes there), at most once every
       `capWarnEvery` 5 waves, while `Game.capPressed`: the board's cap on and the capacity at it, the army as it
       stood in the wave at the cap or over it (the owner's 48 counts), the coming wave past the tide's first, and a
       fielded type below Bangkit 5 (the advice needs a level left to buy). It waits for the Hero
       splash, a boss chest and another message. The wave meter's tooltip, where the tide's strength already shows,
       ends with "Pasukan penuh (32): kuatkan jenis" while it holds. Not saved (`capWarnedAt`): a loaded game may say
       it once more.
     - Its count is the cap, not "32/32": between waves the fallen are still down, and "Pasukan penuh 29/32" would
       contradict itself; the buy refusal keeps its "Pasukan penuh 32/32".
     - **`tideHp` 0.015 → 0.01** (qa-4's suggestion a; the tide's damage and pace stay): measured on qa-4's repro, the
       owner's w63 save forward to w90 with the board's knobs (ARMY=32 TYPES=4 OFFERS=rarity REBUY=owner
       SKIP_REFUSED=1), 6 seeds, the same dice, no spending but the buy-back: 0.015 lost 3 of 6 runs by w78-84
       (falls a wave 0.0 / 0.4 / 5.5 / 8.2 / 33 by 5-wave band from w64); 0.0125 lost 5 of 6 by w90 (w81-89, 3 by
       w85 as at 0.015); 0.01 lost none by w90, falls 0.1 / 0.4 / 1.8 / 5.0 / 5.9, then 31 on w89-90 (one run lost 3
       lives at w90). The margin is narrow: the QA cycle probes on past w90.
     - **The other two arms at 0.01:** the w86 save cut to 32 (CUT=32, its migrated Pusaka bound, w87-105) lost none
       of 6 (0.015: 1), falls 2.4 / 3.2 / 7.5 / 16.8 (0.015: 2.7 / 5.0 / 14.6 / 27.4), more than half the army on 7 of
       24 boss waves (0.015: 11; army-cap probe C's bar, 1 in 6, still not met past w95). Buying Bangkit 4-5 (keeping
       100k; every type at Bangkit 5 by ~w80) lost 0.03-0.23 a wave to w90 (0.015, to w85: 0.07-0.42).
     - **Not met: the owner's 1-3 a wave with Bangkit.** Bangkit 4-5 makes the w63 army about three times as strong as
       the one that doesn't spend (48 kept at Bangkit 5 against one shrinking to 32 at Bangkit 3), so a tide that leaves
       the second alive at w90 can't make the first lose 1-3. The one shape change tried, Bangkit 5's damage step
       ×1.25 → ×1.0 (a probe knob, not built), still lost only 0.1-0.75 a wave. Left to the owner (reports/tide-slope.md
       lists the choices): Bangkit 4-5 stays the answer to the tide, or it gets weaker, or the tide follows the army
       (a rubber band).
     - The cliff is the owner's 48 from before the cap: the falls above 32 can't be bought back, so the army shrinks to
       32 while the tide rises, and meets the tide at 32 only once it is past what 32 can hold. A new game never holds
       more than 32 and feels the tide from its start (the CUT=32 arm: a rise over ~20 waves).
     - Amends 141 (the cap: an old save's 48 shrink to it, and the warning tells it) and 142 (`tideHp` 0.01, the
       design's first knob, now turned).
     - The whole table: reports/tide-slope.md.
162. **"Beban": an army alive over the cap meets a later wave's tide, 2 waves a troop over, ramped in over 5 waves**
     (J1 of reports/late-economy-design.md, §2.1; the owner's decision 1, default (a) relayed 2026-10-02, tuned by the
     probe below with the orchestrator; amends 141's grandfathered army; units-and-combat.md "The tide", ui-hud.md
     "Wave meter" and "Message window", telemetry.md; reports/beban.md):
     - Why: the owner's run is easy because his 48 troops sit above the cap of 32 and kept every one for free (141);
       the tide never caught them until they had shrunk to 32 (161's cliff). New runs, at most 32, are unchanged.
     - The rule: at each `startWave`, while the board's `armyMax` is on, s = max(0, alive − `armyCap`), and the wave's
       tide counts from `tideStart` − round(min(`overTideMax` 60, `overTide` 2 × s) × min(1, (wave − `overFrom` + 1) /
       `overRamp` 5)), frozen for the wave (`Game.waveOver`, `waveTideFrom`). `overFrom`, the first wave started over the
       cap, is a new saved key (set then, never on a new run, never cleared). Every monster the wave makes reads it, and
       with `overPace` on (as measured) the spawn gap too. Each troop that falls over the cap gives 2 waves back.
     - The HUD: the wave meter's badge and tooltip show the coming wave's ("Lebih 16 dari batas: Pasang +32
       gelombang"), the cap's warning its percent, and a save over the cap is told once "Batas pasukan 32. Tiap prajurit
       lebih: Pasang +2 gelombang" (note `over`). Telemetry `start.tide.over`, `telemetryVersion` 5.
     - **Why 2 and not the design's 3** (the owner's w86 save forward to w105, buy-back only, ARMY=32 TYPES=4
       OFFERS=rarity REBUY=owner SKIP_REFUSED=1, the same dice as late-baseline's Q0; falls a wave by band w87-91 / 92-96
       / 97-101 / 102-105):
       - Base (OVER_TIDE 0; on ef79f49 byte for byte Q0's line): 0.73 / 0.40 / 0.20 / 2.21, 0 of 6 lost.
       - 3 (6 seeds): 1.27 / 0.40 / 5.07 / 2.65; 1 lost (s6 at w99, 57 falls, from 0 the wave before).
       - 4 (6 seeds): 1.53 / 4.58 / 0.20 / 2.75; 1 lost (s5 at w95, 66 falls, from 0 the wave before).
       - 3 ramped over 10 (6 seeds): 1.03 / 0.50 / 5.50 / 13.45; 2 lost (s6 at w99 from 0 the wave before; s5 at w102
         already at the cap, Beban off).
       - 3 with the pace off (HP and damage only, 12 seeds): 1.20 / 0.18 / 1.65 / 4.94; 1 lost (s8 at w105, 80
         falls, from 0 the wave before); 6 of 48 boss waves over half fallen. It saved seeds 5 and 6, not s8.
       - **2 (12 seeds): 1.20 / 0.10 / 0.50 / 5.65; 1 lost, s10 at w105, and not to Beban:** at the cap since w101 (s 0,
         the tide from 66), 16 falls the wave before, the necromancer pair. That is the 32-troop regime (the w86 save cut
         to 32 averages 39 falls on w105).
     - Every 3 and 4 arm lost a run in one wave from 0 falls the wave before: a cliff, not a slope. A trace of 4's
       s5 at w95: the 38 troops lost nobody for 120 s while the crowd piled up (1 to 61 monsters on the field: at a tide
       from 42 it brings 1.43× the base's crowd HP a second, HP ×1.69 and a monster every 0.69 s instead of 0.78 s);
       then the line broke and 6 crossed in 1 s, the greatsword skeleton boss among them at 97% HP.
     - **2 is soft:** 0.65 falls a wave over w87-96 against the design's 1-3, shipped by the owner's rule "too soft
       rather than a cliff" (the orchestrator, 2026-10-02). `overPace` stays a named switch for a later tune.
     - The other bars at 2: at most 6 falls in a wave over w87-91 (bar 12); 3 of 48 boss waves with more than half the
       army fallen (bar 4 of 24); w97-104 and w105 below the cut-to-32 line; the 2 runs that reach 32 (w101, w103)
       spend 34% and 29% of their income on rebuys after it (bar 15%), the other 10 never reach it by w105.
     - The same save played as recommended (Bangkit, 6 seeds): 0 lost; 0.13 / 0.63 / 0.10 / 0.17, 0.26 ± 0.04 a
       wave over w87-105 (the design's 0.3-2: soft again), 0.07 ± 0.04 above the base's recommended play, and below
       the buy-back-only arm by 0.31 ± 0.03 over w87-104 (w105's one loss in the other arm makes the whole range
       noisy). It never rebuys or recalls over w89-105 (0% of income, bar 15%): it never reaches the cap, and its 29%
       spent is the Bangkit lump.
     - **It fails the younger save** (the 48-troop save at w63, buy-back only, 6 seeds to w95): 4 lost, 3 by w90 (s2
       w84, s4 w83, s6 w83; s1 w94), the worst wave 123 falls, against the base's 0 of 6 by w90 (whose worst wave
       before w90 is already 59). Beban is off in every collapse: it drains the 48 to 32 first (all 6 runs at 32 by
       w89, the first at w78; on the base 3 of 6 by w90), and then the plain 32-troop army breaks over w80-90. Falls
       go to rebuys at the cap, the rebuys drain the bank, and the line goes in one wave. Shipped anyway (the
       orchestrator, 2026-10-02): the only save over the cap is the owner's, and it is at w86, where Beban passes
       (softly). The w63 save with 48 troops is a past state of that save that no player will reach again, and new
       runs (at most 32) are bit-identical. So the failure says nothing against Beban itself.
