163. **Tempa, Bangkit 6+: past Bangkit 5 gold keeps buying levels for a type, priced by the wave's purse; a dot on the
     Toko tab when gold piles up** (late-economy design J2, reports/late-economy-design.md §2.2; the owner on the late
     game's gold: "duitnya itu aku bingung di buat untuk apa"; his w86 save banked 1.8M with nothing left to buy once
     five types were at Bangkit 5; loot-items-relics.md "Tempa", ui-hud.md "Toko page"):
     - **The owner's decisions (relayed 2026-10-02, the defaults until he answers):** 2 (a) Tempa, +5% HP and damage a
       level, ×1.2 a level, no end; (b) would be +4% / ×1.3 (`tempaDmg` 0.04, `tempaRise` 1.3), (c) no Tempa. 4 (a) the
       Toko tab's dot at 3 purses; (b) would add a message every 10 waves.
     - **The purse** (`purse(w)`, lib/tempa.dart): `purseK` 14 × (4 + 2w) × (1 + `killGoldGrowth`)^(w − 1), rounded to
       `purseRound` 1000: wave 87 166k, 100 358k, 105 479k, 0.87-1.0 of the formula's kill gold, so prices follow the
       income without reading what a run actually earned.
     - **The gate:** a type at Bangkit 5 (`tempaFrom` = `awakenTop`), between waves (the store's own refusals first), in
       the Toko's Bangkit rows; refusals "Butuh Bangkit 5 dulu", "Sudah Tempa +30 (Maks)", "Emas kurang".
     - **The effect:** HP ×(1 + `tempaHp` 0.05) and damage (a heal) ×(1 + `tempaDmg` 0.05) a level, compounding, in
       `statsOf` right after Bangkit 4-5's `ascendFactor` and before the heavy types' +20%, the Pusaka and the oath;
       Heroes included (their ×3 on top), the skills unchanged, the troop price ×`tempaTroopPrice` 1.0 a level (no
       dearer). Levels count only while the type is at Bangkit 5 (`tempaOf`).
     - **The price:** level n + 1 = `tempaK` 0.2 × purse(wave) × `tempaRise` 1.2^n, rounded to 1k and at least 1k
       (`tempaPrice`): wave 87 33k, 40k, 48k, 57k, 69k; wave 100 72k, 86k, 103k, 124k. "No end" with a guard,
       `tempaMax` 30 (×4.32), which no run reaches: at wave 105 the 30th level alone costs 19.0M, all 30 113M.
     - **Saved** as `tempa {type: n}` (only once one is bought, loaded before the troops so they come back at their
       Tempa HP; old saves have none). **Lepas jenis keeps the levels and refunds none of them** (its refund stays
       half the troops' price).
     - **The dot** (`tokoNudge`): gold ≥ `nudgePurses` 3 × purse(wave + 1) and a type with a living troop can buy its
       next Bangkit or Tempa level now; a red dot on the Toko tab like the Tas tab's.
     - **UI:** a Bangkit 5 row sells "Tempa  33k" on the same purple button; "+n" in Bangkit 5's slate ink after the
       stars on the Pasukan, Tas and Toko rows; the row's hover is the next level's card ("Tempa +4"), the stars' the
       level held. Battle log "Ksatria: Tempa +1 (33k emas)" under "Lain"; telemetry event `tempa` and
       `gold.tempaSpent` (`telemetryVersion` 6, after Beban's 5; `eventVersion` 6, after the recall swap's 5).
     - **Measured** (the design's J2 probe, §4 steps 1-2, on f34a138 = the J1 head before the recall swap; probes/tempa/
       in the agents' cache, reports/tempa.md; 6 seeds each to w105, ARMY 32, TYPES 4, OFFERS rarity, REBUY owner,
       SKIP_REFUSED). Policies: tp keeps one purse and spends at most half the last wave's income; gr keeps two purses
       and spends the rest, cheapest level first. With TEMPA=0, tp = Beban's b86 rec at overTide 2 (99 lines, seeds
       1-3), so rec is Beban's line. Troops fell a wave over w87-91 / 92-96 / 97-101 / 102-105:
       - b86-rec: 0.13 / 0.63 / 0.10 / 0.17. w88-105 0.28 ± 0.04, boss kill 37 s, bank 5.32M.
       - b86-tp: 0.17 / 0.20 / 0.27 / 0.21. Spends 34% of income, Tempa +4-5 a type, boss kill 32 s, bank 3.64M.
       - b86-gr: 0.00 / 0.20 / 0.03 / 0.08. w88-105 0.08 ± 0.04, spends 78%, Tempa +7-8, boss kill 28 s, bank at w105
         1.67M (max 1.79M).
       - c86-rec: 0.23 / 0.27 / 0.47 / 0.71. c86-gr: 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.08. Over w95-105: 0.03 ± 0.03 vs 0.59 ± 0.19.
       - b63-gr (32 troops, to w95): every band ≤ 0.17. Beban's no-spend b63 lost 3-4 of 6.
       - Game overs: none in any arm.
     - **The bars:**
       - Pass: the bank at most 4 purses on b86-gr (1.67M ≤ 1.92M); Worth it (c86-gr below c86-rec); the boss kill time
         at least 60% of rec's (28 vs 37 s); tp spends 30-70% of income over w89-105 (34%).
       - Fail: b86-gr's falls at least half of rec's (30%); more than 0.5 on the slot waves (0.33 ± 0.15); the
         orchestrator's floor of 0.3 a wave over w88-105 (0.08); gr's 30-70% spend (78-79% on b86, c86 and b63).
       - Two of the fails don't depend on the constants. Rec itself falls only 0.28 on the J1 head, so no arm that helps
         clears the floor. gr's spend is its policy (two purses kept, the rest spent), and the price scales with the
         purse, so `tempaDmg` 0.04 or `tempaRise` 1.3 can't move it. The orchestrator (2026-10-02) therefore dropped the
         floor and judged gr's spend by the bank (Room) alone.
     - **Push-back on the owner's save is the tide's job, not Tempa's** (the orchestrator, 2026-10-02): Tempa makes a
       spender's late game easier by design. The b86 and c86 numbers show how much push-back is left. b63-gr shows Tempa
       holds the 32-troop regime that a no-spend army lost.
     - **The fallback, measured, and the defaults kept** (the orchestrator's call): the orchestrator's rule was to
       confirm and ship `tempaDmg` 0.04 if b86-gr at 0.04 fell at least 0.14 a wave over w88-105 (half of rec's), and
       otherwise to ship the defaults, with no `tempaRise` 1.3. At 0.04 (seeds 1-3) b86-gr falls 0.11 ± 0.08, against
       0.06 ± 0.06 at 0.05 and rec's 0.22 ± 0.06 on the same seeds. Its spend, Tempa levels (+7-8) and bank (1.74M at
       w105) match 0.05's, since the prices are the same. So the owner's 2 (a) ships as decided: +5% / ×1.2.
164. **Lebur: a Pusaka in the Gudang melts into another owned one for +1 star at Asah's price, with no limit per boss
     interval** (the late-economy design's J3, reports/late-economy-design.md §2.3; owner decision 3 at its default
     "(a)", relayed 2026-10-02: "Pusaka Gudang boleh dilebur ke Pusaka lain untuk +1 bintang seharga Asah, tanpa batas
     per babak?"; loot-items-relics.md "Lebur", ui-hud.md "Tas"):
     - **Why:** late in a run the chest's cards pile up in the Gudang with nothing to do (the owner's w86 save keeps 3
       there to w105), and gold has few sinks after Bangkit 5. Lebur turns a card that fits no type into a star on one
       that does, and prices it like Asah's.
     - **The rule:** between waves a Gudang Pusaka (the fodder, not a Legenda) goes into any other owned Pusaka (bound
       or in the Gudang, not a Legenda, under ★3): the target gains `leburStars` 1 for `leburPrice` = `asahPrice` by its
       stars (60k to ★2, 150k to ★3), `leburRelics` 0 small relics; its type refits at once with the gold burst. The
       fodder is deleted with its stars, nothing paid back, and the chest may deal it again (`_offerable`).
     - **Apart from Asah** (`leburUsesAsah` false): `asahAt` is untouched and a spent Asah never refuses it, so the
       fodder supply (chest cards, paid rerolls) is the limit, which keeps "duplicate cards keep their worth"
       (pusaka.dart). Any rarity into any target (`leburRarity` false; decision 3's "(b)", "Langka hanya untuk Langka": a
       Langka fodder only into a Langka target, an Epik one into any, is the switch; "(c)", a second Pusaka slot, isn't
       built).
     - **Refusals**, in order: game over, not owned, not in the Gudang (bound, or an oath), mid-wave, a Legenda fodder,
       then (the button) no Pusaka that could take a star, or (a target) the same Pusaka, not owned, a Legenda, ★3, the
       gold.
     - **UI:** "Lebur" left of the Gudang line's Jual (the design said "on the Gudang strip": the picked one's line,
       under the Gudang's chips, is where a Gudang Pusaka's actions are, and a button on the chips' row would shrink
       them); it opens a target picker on the facing page, a row per target with "★n ▸ ★n+1", the price and what it
       does at the new star, two taps like Asah's. It fits 1266×713 and 412×860.
     - **Telemetry:** event `pusakaLebur` (`eventVersion` 7), wave record `gold.leburSpent` (`telemetryVersion` 7). No
       saved key.
     - **The probe** (design §4 J3, on the J2 head 28fdd4f; the policy lb is rec, then the chests between waves, each
       rerolled at most twice while no card fits a type, then every Gudang Pusaka but a Legenda melted into the bound
       one with the fewest stars; 6 seeds; reports/lebur.md): identity at LEBUR=0 equals the J2 head's rec line for line
       (b86, seeds 1-3, to w105), and lb equals rec until its first melt (b63 seed 2, with none, to w105). 0 game overs
       on b86-lb and b63-lb. Falls over w88-105 on b86-lb 0.29 ± 0.03 a wave, 103% of rec's 0.28 ± 0.04. The Gudang's
       fodder at the end (not counting a Legenda) is 0 in 6/6 runs on both, **but melts are 0 a run on b86 and 0.17 on
       b63, under the orchestrator's "at least 2 a run"**: Lebur melts whatever fodder there is, and there is little.
       The policy's rerolls (b86: 10 in 6 runs, 724k) nearly always find a card that fits, and even without them
       rec makes about 1 non-Legenda fodder a run on b86 before w105 (seeds 1-3: 2, 1, 0) from one chest per 5 waves.
       The bar measures the chest's supply, which Lebur cannot raise; Lebur is left as is, for the orchestrator to
       weigh. b63-lb's falls at w104-105 (19 ± 6 a wave, no game over) are the board's own: the J2 head's rec plays
       them the same (seed 2's lines equal).

166. **The overtime clock starts afresh while the wave's mini boss and boss keep losing HP, and a wave marches at the
     latest 300 s after its last spawn or life lost** (qa-4's FINDING, low, 2026-10-02: "kite-stall's overtime march
     fires in slow late slot waves the army was still winning"; amends 153; the orchestrator chose qa-4's first option,
     and the drift rule stays as it is; units-and-combat.md "Stalled waves", telemetry.md, architecture.md):
     - The finding: 983b010 with the range's switches off replays 14437d0 the same except for the march rule. In 252
       plays of the late slot waves (live86 w87–100, live48 w48–62, dice 0–3) 14 differed, and all of them marched. The
       overtime marches at w60/90/99, with 10, 7, 6, 5, 3 and 2 troops alive, cost +1, +1, +1, +1, +2 and +1 lives
       where 14437d0 won with 0 (live86 s1 w90 r0: won at 515 s; the march at ~365 s let the necromancer mini boss
       leak). The one STALL (live86 s3 w90 r2, still on at 600 s) became a win with 1 life lost.
     - **`stallProgress` 0.05:** the slot monsters (the mini boss and the boss, alive) having lost 5% of their summed
       max HP since the overtime clock last started starts it afresh. The clock also restarts, as before, on a spawn or
       a life lost; it doesn't on a plain monster's death or HP. Only a spawn brings a slot monster, so the same ones
       count until the next start, a dead one at 0 HP; HP healed back has to be lost again. With no slot monster alive
       the rule is 153's. In the traces, a slot fight the army is winning loses 5% every 2–37 s.
     - **`stallOvertimeMax` 300 s:** this long after the last spawn or life lost the monsters march whatever the
       slots did (`MarchCause.overtimeMax`). Progress alone ran the STALL play to 600 s again: its last troop whittled
       the boss 5% every 16–24 s, and the drift rule's march at 545 s hadn't reached the base by the cap. 300 is qa-4's
       other number (`stallOvertime` ~300 s). With 300, the slowest win of the 14 (live48 s4 w60 r3, 278 s after its
       last spawn) still ends before the cap. The brief's 420 s would have marched the STALL play at 605 s (its last
       spawn at 185 s).
     - The repro on 983b010 + this change (a0, the same dice k = seed·1000 + wave·10 + rep), secs into the wave:

       | play | 14437d0 | 983b010 | this change |
       |---|---|---|---|
       | live48 s4 w60 r1 | won 311.5 s, 0 lives | overtime (7 alive), 0 lives | identical to 14437d0 |
       | live48 s4 w60 r3 | won 406.9 s, 0 lives | overtime (5 alive), 1 life | identical to 14437d0 |
       | live86 s1 w90 r0 | won 515.5 s, 0 lives | overtime (10 alive), 1 life | drifting at 419 s (3 alive), won 477.8 s, 1 life |
       | live86 s1 w99 r0 | won 453.5 s, 0 lives | overtime (7 alive), 1 life | drifting at 416 s (5 alive), won 450.5 s, 1 life |
       | live86 s2 w90 r3 | won 443.0 s, 0 lives | overtime (6 alive), 1 life | drifting at 401 s (3 alive), won 434.8 s, 1 life |
       | live86 s1 w90 r3 | won 539.4 s, 0 lives | overtime (3 alive), 2 lives | drifting at 396 s (2 alive), won 427.6 s, 2 lives |
       | live86 s3 w90 r2 | STALL at 600 s | overtime (2 alive), won 428.4 s, 1 life | overtimeMax at 485 s (1 alive), won 517.0 s, 1 life |

       The other 7 of the 14 plays (5 drifting marches with 37–40 alive on live48, 1 with 10 alive on live86, and the
       LOST play) are identical to 983b010. A play without an overtime march can't change: the rule only moves the
       overtime clock, and it draws no dice.
     - **Known remainder:** on live86 three of the four fights that marched on overtime with 6–10 troops alive now go
       on until the drift rule (153) marches them 30–60 s later with 2–5 troops left, after the last ranged troops kite
       the slot monster off. Those lives stay lost (1, 1, 1). The orchestrator kept the drift rule unchanged: such
       fights are close to a wipe and rare on today's head (1 overtime march in 558 plays), and the next QA cycle
       watches for them there. Letting the slots' progress also hold off the drift rule was not built.
     - Tests: test/kite_stall_test.dart (153's 7, with 5 and 6 now on a plain monster; plus a slot fight that keeps
       losing HP going on past `stallOvertime` until `stallOvertimeMax`, a life lost restarting that too; one that stops
       losing HP marching `stallOvertime` after its last progress; HP healed back having to be lost again; a mini boss
       falling counting as progress). FAST LANE: reports/stall-progress.md "PROBE PLAN".

       (each Pusaka at each star, bound, asleep, in the Gudang, not owned; an item over every type's row): in the
       font, no line twice, one "Oath", no Indonesian left, and it fits a 412-wide phone (the widest 250 px of 404).
       The offscreen shots at 1266×713 (×2) and 412×860 (×3), every tooltip, card and strip, were looked at one by one
       (<agents>/shots/item-text/).
     - The 5 is redrawn (the same screenshot: "+5%" read "+S%"; the orchestrator's (a), 2026-10-02: "redraw the 5 only,
       no dotted 0"; ui-hud.md "The font", assets.md, CREDITS.md "The font"). Pixelify Sans's 5 is its S with two pixels
       moved; 0 and O are one outline too, but a 0 stands among digits. PohDigits, a Modified Version under the same
       OFL with a name of its own (Pixelify Sans declares no Reserved Font Name), holds the 5 alone with a flat top and
       a square corner, at 500 and 700; `hudStyle` names it first, Pixelify Sans the fallback. `tool/make_digit_font.py`
       writes it byte for byte from Pixelify Sans's own 5 (its pixel grid at each weight, checked by rebuilding the old
       5 exactly) on 3 × its units per em, since the 5 at 500 is 591⅔ of its units wide: a whole-unit 592 made "+5%"
       0.004 px wider at 14. test/digit_font_test.dart pins the sha256s and checks every text as wide (to 0.001 px), as
       tall and on the same baseline as in Pixelify Sans alone, and the same pixels where it has no 5, body and bold.
       Its licence, `OFL-PohDigits.txt` (what was changed and from what, then the OFL with a copyright line for the 5),
       is bundled, in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt's part 3 and on the Lisensi page as "PohDigits"; the release allowlist,
       the asset manifest (own, OFL) and the public export's OFL list (sha256 and blob) hold its three files.
     - (Amended 2026-10-03, glyph-c; the orchestrator's (a), from its shots: the Cara Main page's title read "Oara
       Main", the foe splash's ribbon "Ourse of Frailty", "Peti Bos" "Peti Gos", "Gelombang" "Belombang".) PohDigits
       redraws the B, C and G too. Not the font file loaded wrong: its cmap maps the 5 alone and no GSUB feature touches
       them; Pixelify Sans's own C is its O with one pixel out and its B and G an O with a mark in the middle, and a
       one-pixel gap is 80 units at wght 400, 65 at 500, 34 at 700 (the pixel grows on a fixed grid), so at the HUD's
       sizes it blurs shut, worst in bold. New: the C open on the right over three rows, the G the same with a bar on
       its fifth row, the B with a flat left side (not an 8 or a G); the same advances and line metrics, the files'
       names kept. Pixelify Sans kerns some pairs with them ("Bo" -20 of 1000), and a kern doesn't cross fonts: a line
       with one is up to 90 units wider (the orchestrator: a small drift is fine, Pixelify Sans's file stays
       unmodified). test/letter_shapes_test.dart: every two capitals drawn 2 font pixels of ink apart (C and O were 0.2
       to 0.9); test/digit_font_test.dart: as wide as before but for exactly the lost kerns. The lower case c (its o
       with one pixel out: "Koook ulang" in bold) and the i (its dot blurs into its stem) stay: c is kerned with nearly
       every letter, so taking it from PohDigits would move lines by up to 320 units; they wait for a fixed copy of the
       font.
     - (Amended by 179, 2026-10-03.) That fixed copy is Poh Sans: the 5, B, C and G (the B now also with a narrower top
       bowl) are drawn in the font itself, with the kerns PohDigits lost; PohDigits and its tool are retired.

178. **The Pusaka run on one engine: each Pusaka is a row of data in `pusakaCatalog` (its rarity, Ukir role, icon,
     counter and effects), and the engine dispatches each effect at its trigger; today's ten that aren't oaths moved
     onto it with nothing changed in play, and the oaths stay as they were** (step 0b of reports/catalog-design.md
     §5.1, built by cat-0b on cat-0a's accessor, Ukir's U1; loot-items-relics.md "The Pusaka catalog and its engine",
     units-and-combat.md, architecture.md, testing.md):
     - The shape (the design's §2.1, lib/pusaka_catalog.dart): an `Fx` is a trigger (`Trig`, 16), an optional
       condition (`If`), an effect (`Eff`) on a target (`To`), its numbers by star (`k`, `boss`, `count`, still read
       only through `pusakaAt` / `pusakaCountAt`, now by the row and the Fx's index) and its fixed ones (`every`, `r`,
       `cd`, `cap`, `time`, `regen`, `stat`, `status`). An `Art` is a row: rarity, role, icon (`IconRef`, a sheet's
       cell and a tint), its Fx, epithet, counter (and a healer's), `store`, `live` (dealt by a chest and sold).
       `Relic.rarity`, `Relic.store`, `buildEpithets`, the store page's icons and the Tas' and chest's icons read it.
     - The engine (lib/pusaka_engine.dart): each type's book, its bound Pusaka's Fx by trigger with their numbers read
       once, rebuilt after any change of a binding or a star (a count bumped by `OwnedPusaka`'s setters and
       `Game.pusaka`'s own map, so no path can leave a book stale). The calls sit where the old hooks sat, in the same
       order, with the same arithmetic, so the floating point and the order the tallies are made in are the same.
       Inside a leap's hits (God's Thunder) only `dealt` runs: no pierce, no hurt-by, no kill (the depth guard,
       `Game._fxDepth`), so a later batch's effects can't chain.
     - Moved: `_thunder`, `_voidMark`, `_grailSaves` (store.dart), `_dragonCrown`, `_pusakaHit`, `_dawnHealed`
       (pusaka.dart), `_ironBanner`, `_bloodFang`, `_mourningBell`, `_blowK` (draft.dart) and the store page's
       `_artefactIcons`. `Unit.grailUsed` is `Unit.fxOnce`; `fxN`, `fxReady`, `ward` and `emberMark` wait for the
       batches (nothing sets them yet). Each counter's family (`FxFamily`: added, kept off, healed, saves, survived)
       is what the counter text and the wave's report read.
     - The texts: a template per (trigger, effect) for the effect lines and the gist, today's byte for byte. The
       conditions today's ten need: none, so every `If` is a stub (`fxIfsBuilt` is empty) and a row that names one
       fails pusaka_catalog_test.dart. The engine draws no dice.
     - The owner's defaults, one constant each: a new Epik isn't sold in the store (`newEpikStore` false); a Bayangan
       kind may sit in several pools (`OmenKind.tiers`, a stub for step 0c); the texts may say "skill" and "MP"
       (`fxWords`).
     - Identity (test/probe_pusaka_w89_identity.dart, now also two waves played with the telemetry listening):
       a `git archive` mirror of the base 40d101e against the branch, 1754 lines the same byte for byte; the telemetry
       hashes b658c9e8e94774a7 as saved (43 records), f6b88b7ece80b66a with the five Epik at ★2 (38),
       5a6112fae407ae78 with the four Langka and Dragon Crown at ★2 (36). The hot path: the seven 45 s fights took
       5625 ms on the base and 5616 ms on the branch, queued side by side (best of 3; single runs spread from 5180 to
       5705 ms, so no cost shows).
     - Tests: pusaka_catalog_test.dart checks the rules every row keeps (built, its templates, the band, the key, the
       icons, the counters, the families, the books, no dice, the defaults) instead of lists of today's Pusaka:
       pusaka_test's, legenda_test's, pusaka_bukti_test's and draft_test's exact sets now check today's among the
       rest, so a data batch adds rows and no test.

179. **The game's font is Poh Sans: Pixelify Sans with its 2, 3, 5, 6, 9, B, C, G, S, Z, a, c and i redrawn, one font
     with its kerning kept, in place of Pixelify Sans and PohDigits** (the owner, 2026-10-03: "fontnya sudah di
     ganti?", on shots where C still read as O and B as G; the follow-up of glyph-c's report, "a fixed copy of Pixelify
     Sans", built by font-fork. The owner's "boleh dimodifikasi?" isn't answered yet: built on the default, yes, as an
     OFL Modified Version with a name of its own. Amends 158, 168 and 172; ui-hud.md "The font", assets.md, CREDITS.md
     "The font", testing.md, itch-page.md):
     - **Why a modified copy:** Pixelify Sans grows bolder by growing every pixel on a fixed grid, so a one-pixel gap
       is 34 units of 1000 at wght 700 and blurs shut at the HUD's sizes. PohDigits (168) took four glyphs from a
       second font, but a kern never crosses fonts (every B/C/G pair lost its kern) and the lower case couldn't go
       that way. One font, edited in place, keeps every kern.
     - **What changed:** 13 glyphs, on the font's own pixel grid (each edge's position at 400 and its move to 700 read
       from the font, checked by rebuilding each old glyph exactly at both weights): C and c open (three rows, two),
       G the new C with a bar, B a flat left side and a narrower top bowl, i its dot a row higher (two rows clear of the
       stem, a row above the capitals), a a square top right and a flat foot, 5 a flat top and square corner, S without
       its terminals, 2 a flat foot, 3 a short middle bar, 6 and 9 without one terminal each, Z a straight diagonal.
       Each keeps its advance and side bearing: its outline at 400 and one gvar delta set to 700 on the font's shared
       tuple, the phantom points' deltas copied. GPOS, GSUB, GDEF, HVAR, MVAR, the cmap and every other glyph are the
       font's bytes; the composites on them (Ç, Ĝ, Ź, á, ç, …) follow. Names: "Poh Sans" / `PohSans` (IDs 1, 3, 4, 6,
       25, a copyright line and a description added, the trademark and vendor names dropped, the designer kept);
       fvar and STAT name only the weights, so they stay. `tool/make_poh_sans.py` (stdlib) writes it byte for byte;
       `tool/make_digit_font.py` is gone.
     - **How the 13 were chosen:** test/letter_shapes_test.dart now draws every one of A-Z, a-z, 0-9 alone at HUD
       sizes 12-30 and wght 400, 500 and 700, and every two must be 2 font pixels of ink apart (a letter and its own
       capital, and O and 0, aside). On Pixelify Sans 21 pairs fail (C/O and i/l down to 0.20 in bold, c/o, a/o, B/G,
       B/8, S/6, 6/8, 8/9, 3/9, S/9, Z/2, S/3, S/8, 2/3, 2/8, 3/8, B/6, B/9, G/8, C/0), each with a glyph Poh Sans
       redraws; on Poh Sans none, the closest c/o 2.44. The first set of ten (without S, 2, 3, and the B with a full top)
       still left S/8, 3/8, 2/8, S/3, 2/3 and B/8 at 1.80-1.99 in bold: Pixelify Sans draws S, 2, 3 as its 8 less two
       side pixels, which bold partly fills ("S8" read "88" in the shots). An hourglass 8 fixed those but read as an X,
       so the S, 2, 3 and B were redrawn instead, as gently as would pass (the shots: "Skor 38 S8 B8" reads right).
     - **liga stays off** (172): the fi ligature is one letter wide, so no redraw reads right; each letter is drawn on
       its own, the redrawn i included.
     - **Kerning, no drift:** test/poh_sans_test.dart checks that a text is exactly as wide as in Pixelify Sans, as tall
       and on one baseline, at 400, 500 and 700, the same pixels unless it holds a redrawn glyph, and pins both
       sha256s and the tool's `--check`. Against main's pair (Pixelify Sans + PohDigits), strings with a B, C or G pair
       get their kern back (up to 90 units, as 168 measured).
     - **The files:** `assets/fonts/PohSans.ttf` and `OFL-PohSans.txt` (what was changed and from what, with the
       source's sha256, then the OFL with Pixelify Sans's copyright and a line for the change), bundled and on the
       Lisensi page as "Poh Sans"; the source in `tool/fonts/` (the same bytes as before, with its OFL text), public
       and not bundled. The old five (`PixelifySans.ttf`, `PohDigits-Medium.ttf`, `PohDigits-Bold.ttf`, their two
       licences) stay under `assets/fonts/` while the owner's game runs from main: out of pubspec.yaml, the bundled
       licences, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt and the public export, classified in the manifest, and `RETIRED_ASSETS` in
       scripts/release-build.sh (the checkout may hold them, a build may not). Deleting them, and their lines, waits for
       the game to be closed.
     - **Fit, nothing moved but the kerns:** font-fork's dump of every string `_text` draws (glyph-c's probe, with
       each string's width added: every guide card page, K4's two included, every foe splash at each rank, the welcome
       screen, Pengaturan, Toko, Tas, Pasukan and every Cara Main topic, at 412×860, 915×412 and 1266×713), main's
       pair (b289601) against Poh Sans: 52,953 strings each, the same text, lines, size (no shrink-to-fit changed) and
       anchor in all. 876 are narrower, by up to 0.72 px ("Bone Bash" at 22 px, its kerns back), none wider; card K9's
       lines at 915×412 sit 0.5 px further right (the block is centred on its widest line, 0.26 px narrower). Nothing
       wraps, clips or shrinks. Dumps: `<agents>/shots/font-fork/fit-{before2,after2}.txt`.
     - No rule moved: no probe plan.

181. **Every heal a troop gets goes through one function, tagged by where it came from, and a troop can hold a ward
     (a shield); nothing changed in play** (step 0e of reports/catalog-design.md §5.1, built by cat-0e;
     units-and-combat.md "The heal funnel" and "The ward", loot-items-relics.md, architecture.md, testing.md):
     - Why: the Bayangan Wound (troop heals in a wave are less), today's heal Pusaka and about 15 new ones need one
       place where a heal lands. `_healTroop` (lib/heal.dart) takes the heal and a `HealSrc` (13 tags, one per site:
       heal, prayer, overTime, lifesteal, killHeal, sacrifice, unbroken, lifeline, regen, fang, pusaka, queue, grail)
       and returns the heal past full HP (for `healPastFull`). Sites both sides share go through `_healUnit`.
     - Wound's seam, agreed with cat-0c: `_woundK` (today `woundForce ?? 1.0`), cutting only `inWave` heals; the
       Grail's save and the after-wave heal (even carried into a wave) never, nor any heal between waves. Step 0d
       writes `1 - min(k.max, k.perE * omenE(OmenKind.wound))` there.
     - Exactness: each site keeps `min(maxHp, hp + heal)`; the after-wave heal is a heal of its whole max HP (full
       exactly); the Grail's save sets HP to 0, then heals its share (0 + x is x).
     - The ward: `giveWard` up to `wardMax` 0.20 of max HP, soaked in `_hurt` after every cut, cleared in
       `_endEffects`. Nothing grants one yet.
     - Identity: test/probe_pusaka_w89_identity.dart, base c87889c (a `git archive` mirror) against the branch:
       1754 lines SAME; telemetry hashes b658c9e8e94774a7 (43), f6b88b7ece80b66a (38), 5a6112fae407ae78 (36), as on
       the base; fights 5522 ms base, 5486 ms branch (best of 3).

182. **The catalog's shared hooks: every blow names where it comes from, every effect's time goes through one scaler,
     and the engine checks its first six conditions, with nothing changed in play** (step 0f of
     reports/catalog-design.md §5.1, built by cat-0f on cat-0b's engine (178); units-and-combat.md "Damage" and "The
     effect store", loot-items-relics.md "The Pusaka catalog and its engine", architecture.md, testing.md):
     - The hit-source tag (the design's §2.3): `enum Hit {normal, smite, skill, extra, hitBack, bleed}`, and
       `_hurt(u, dmg, src, [by, cap])` takes it as its third argument, so all 40 calls name one. A fighter's blow or
       shot on its target and the necromancer's scythe are `normal`; past the target a normal attack's splash is
       `extra` (a skill's area stays `skill`), and so is God's Thunder's leap; a troop healer's holy light `smite`;
       worn thorns, a reflect, Parry's answer and the Bayangan's Thorns (188's `_omenThorns`, tagged when this branch
       merged it, as agreed with cat-0d) `hitBack`; a bleed's tick `bleed`; everything else is a skill's
       (a troop's, an awakening's, a Hero's, a monster's). A `Shot` carries its own (`Shot.src`, `Shot.special` a
       skill's), `_holyHurt` passes its caller's on (the smite, or Holy Nova's and Judgement's skill), and a linked
       ally's share keeps the blow's. Nothing reads it yet: Scatter, Spell Ward, Thornproof, Holy Ward and the Oath of
       Spells will. test/hit_source_test.dart scans lib/ itself, so a new blow can't come without one, and lists the
       blows that aren't a skill's: a new one is added there on purpose.
     - The duration scaler: `addEffect` reads every effect's time through `_effectTime` (pusaka_engine.dart), its one
       place, at 1 today (`scaledEffectTime(time, 1)` is `time`, to the bit). Shortened, an effect never lasts under
       `effectTimeFloor` 0.3 s, or its own time when that is shorter; Unshaken, Mark Ward and Lingering will scale it.
       A stun (`stunUntil`, `_stunFor`) is no effect, so it doesn't go through it: Unshaken's batch decides whether its
       "stuns" mean it too.
     - The per-unit hooks, none saved: `Unit.firstStrikeAt` (its first blow through `_hurt` as the attacker, +∞ until
       then; Enrage), `Unit.belowHp` with `belowOnce(u, share, flag)` (true the first time living `u` is at or under
       `share` of its max HP for that bit, a killing blow using none; Second Skin, Last Rage, Last Gasp, Hidden Flask),
       and `alliesNearOf` / `foesNearOf` (the units within a reach, counted at most once a tick for a reach, stamped
       with `Game._ticks`, so a hot trigger such as `struck` scans the field once a tick, not once a blow). A troop's
       first strike and HP bits start again when a wave starts; a monster lives one wave anyway.
     - The conditions (§2.2): `_fxWhen` now gets the holder and the monster in play at every trigger (the one it hits,
       or the one hitting it) and checks `hpBelow`, `hpAbove`, `foeHpBelow`, `foeHpAbove` (a share of max HP, `ifK`),
       `alliesNear` (`ifK` other troops within the new `Fx.ifR`) and `firstOfTypeThisWave` (the first ask this wave
       that passes uses it up, `Game._fxFirsts`, cleared by `startWave`). `fxIfsBuilt` lists them; the others stay
       stubs for their batches, and today's ten rows use none.
     - Identity (test/probe_pusaka_w89_identity.dart): the branch, merged with each main as it moved, against
       `git archive` mirrors of the base c87889c and of mains b289601, defd22b, 0981123, 776f8a6 and e71a741: every time
       the same byte for byte, 1754 lines. The telemetry hashes as on 178 (b658c9e8e94774a7 as saved, f6b88b7ece80b66a,
       5a6112fae407ae78) through defd22b; from 0981123, whose own golden moved with 180's Bayangan events,
       f1e6c25e40b1b83f, facdda226fe3a222 and bedd463d6effe460 on main and branch alike (on e71a741 too: 188's hooks
       are off with the Bayangan); every run reaching wave 91. The hot path: the seven 45 s fights took 5422 ms on main
       and 5399 ms on the branch, the best of three runs each (each run itself best of 3), interleaved in the queue; on
       defd22b 5264 against 5229 ms, on 0981123 5267 against 5222 ms, on 776f8a6 5322 against 5509 ms (two runs each,
       not side by side), on e71a741 5197 against 5171 ms (two runs each; the back-to-back pair). Single runs spread
       from 5171 to 6510 ms under the queue's load, so no cost shows.
     - Tests: test/fx_hooks_test.dart (the scaler at 1 is the identity for every status on a troop and a monster, the
       near counts against a brute count over a random field, `belowOnce`, `firstStrikeAt`, and each built condition
       through a real trigger on Iron Banner's or War Drum's row swapped for the test) and test/hit_source_test.dart.
     - No rule moved, so no probe plan. No shape drawn in code: no exception for the owner.
183. **Ukir: between waves from wave 40, spare items fill a Pusaka's Ukir bar, and each full bar is a step worth part
     of a star (five steps, 0.8 star in all); the rules, the save and the telemetry are in, shipped dark with no screen
     to feed it yet** (the owner, 2026-10-02: items should also make the artefacts stronger, so spare items stay useful
     late in a run; reports/item-artefact-design.md §2 and §5 U2, built by ukir-u2 on U1's `pusakaAt` and cat-0b's
     engine; loot-items-relics.md "Ukir", telemetry.md, architecture.md, testing.md):
     - The rules (lib/pusaka.dart, `extension Ukir on Game`, every number one constant): a Pusaka with an Ukir role
       (its catalog row's `role`), bound or in the Gudang, never an oath. An item of its role gives `ukirMatch` 2
       points, any other kind `ukirAny` 1. Five steps of `ukirCost` 60/90/135/200/300 points worth `ukirWorth`
       0.2/0.2/0.2/0.1/0.1 star. A tap gives at most `ukirTap` 60 points, the budget left and what the step lacks: no
       point spills and a role's item is never split. All Pusaka share `ukirPerBoss` 180 points a boss interval
       (Asah's). The fill order is the role's kinds first, the kind with the most spare each pick (ties in `Item`
       order), and `ukirKeep` keeps back what a fielded type needs for its next Bangkit. The refusals come in the
       design's order (`ukirRefusals`), in simple English rather than the design's Indonesian (the owner, 2026-10-03:
       every in-game text is English; the English names' defaults "Carve" for Ukir and "Artifact" for Pusaka until
       the owner picks: "Carving opens at wave 40", "Oaths can't be carved", "Fully carved").
     - The effect is read only through `pusakaAt(relic, stars, ukir:)`: the level is the stars plus the steps' worth,
       linear between two stars and past ★3 by the last gap. At Ukir 0 it gives exactly the table's number, so a game
       without Ukir plays as before. Whole numbers (God's Thunder's leaps, War Drum's `every`) read the stars only.
       God's Thunder's share (+`thunderSharePerStar` 0.2 a star of worth) and Dragon Crown's cap (−`crownPerStar`
       0.15) move by named rules (`ukirPerStar`). The engine's books, the stats and every text read the same accessor.
     - The owner's four questions (design §6) are still open, so each default is one constant. The cap is +5, worth
       0.8 star (`ukirCost` / `ukirWorth`). A Lebur keeps the higher Ukir and a sale loses it (`ukirMelt`
       `UkirMelt.higher`; `sum` and `lost` are there). Bound and Gudang Pusaka can be fed (`ukirGudang` true). Asah
       takes no items (`asahItems` [0, 0]; any other value makes Asah take that many items from `ukirSpare`).
     - A star-up (the chest, Asah, Lebur) keeps `ukir` and `feed`, a Pindah or the Gudang moves them, and a sale
       loses them.
     - Bayangan: each full `ukirOmenStars` 1.0 star of worth fed in a run calls `_omenStarUp(relic)` once.
       `UkirRun.milli` passes a multiple of 1000 and a sale never lowers it. The hook's name and signature are agreed
       with cat-0c (`void _omenStarUp(Relic relic)` on `Game`): cat-0c's omen.dart merged first, so Ukir calls its
       hook, and the stub that stood in for it on this branch is gone. While the Bayangan are on, from wave `omenFrom`,
       the Pusaka's counter gets levels as a chest's take would; off by default. Ukir draws no die.
     - One change from the design: `Game.ukir`'s `tenths` became `milli` (thousandths). The design's fallback worth of
       0.075 a step isn't a whole number of tenths.
     - The save: `OwnedPusaka.ukir` / `feed` and `Game.ukir` `{iv, pts, milli}` are written only when above 0 (or once
       anything was fed). A save from before Ukir, or one never fed, loads and writes byte for byte as before. Bad
       values are clamped on load. Telemetry `tv` 8: the trace events `UkirFed` / `UkirStep`, the wave record's
       `ukirItems` / `ukirPoints` / `ukirSteps` (only when some was fed) and each Pusaka's `ukir` (only above 0).
       cat-0c's Bayangan also takes `tv` 8: one bump for both, agreed.
     - Probe hooks: `givePusaka(..., ukir:)` and `ukirFill({bound})` (taps until no Pusaka takes more, each tap to the
       one with the fewest steps). On the w89 save God's Thunder's first tap takes bow 15, sword 13 and gloves 2 (60

     - Identity (test/probe_pusaka_w89_identity.dart, its records' version labels masked as cat-0c's): a `git archive`

185. **Peti Bos's odds rise a chest at a time: each boss chest after wave 5's moves a card's Legenda chance 0.0025
     further toward a cap of Langka 0.40 / Epik 0.35 / Legenda 0.25, reached at wave 345** (the owner, 2026-10-02 and
     2026-10-03, through the orchestrator; built by chest-odds; loot-items-relics.md "Peti Bos", architecture.md,
     testing.md):
     - His words: 2026-10-02 "makin tinggi wave maka change untuk item buff langka naik 0.05 per wave dan stop di angka
       yang ngebuat change normal item turun ke angka 50%" (the higher the wave, the rare buff item's chance rises 0.05
       a wave, stopping where the normal item's chance is down to 50%); 2026-10-03 "peti bos, tapi angka dari epic di
       turunkan ke 27% dan legend 23%" (the boss chest, but Epik down to 27% and Legenda 23%); then, slower, "wave 5
       8%, nanti di wave 10 8.25%"; then the cap, "aku mau rebalance wX dan seterusnya -> 40%, 35%, 25%".
     - The reading moved twice while it was built. First (the orchestrator's): from `legendFrom` (w20) a straight line,
       Legenda +0.05 a wave, to 0.50 / 0.27 / 0.23 at w23. Then his example made it a step a chest from w5: n = max(0,
       wave ÷ `bossEvery` − 1) (w5 0, w10 1, w100 19), Legenda 0.08 + 0.0025·n (0.05 a wave × 5 waves a chest), to the
       same cap at n 60 (w305). Then the cap became 0.40 / 0.35 / 0.25, at the same speed: n 68 (w345). Langka and Epik
       give up their share in the cap's proportion: Langka 0.55 − (0.15/68)·n, Epik 0.37 − (0.02/68)·n (w10 0.5478 /
       0.3697 / 0.0825, w100 0.5081 / 0.3644 / 0.1275). He may still pick where the cap lands, so the speed is its own
       constant.
     - What: `chestOddsCap` (0.40, 0.35, 0.25), `chestOddsStep` 0.0025 and `chestOddsAt(wave)` beside `chestOdds`
       (lib/draft.dart). The number of steps is (cap − first Legenda) ÷ step, rounded (68), so a new cap or step is one
       constant and the slopes follow. `_rollRarity` reads the odds of the chest's own wave (`Chest.wave`): a chest put
       off with Nanti and rerolled later keeps them, and a catch-up chest has its load wave's (the w86 save's: n 16).
     - Unchanged: a Legenda before w20 is still an Epik (there Epik or better comes at 0.45 + (0.15/68)·n), and so is
       one with all three found; the pity, the first chest (three Epik), catch-up chests and Kocok ulang keep their
       rules. Still ONE `draft` draw a card: only the thresholds move, so a seed draws as many values at every wave
       (test/chest_odds_test.dart: three chests and a reroll draw 24 at waves 1-400). In waves 1-9 (no step) the cards'
       rarities are the head's (7bb3a8e): a table of three chests on seeds 1-8, generated on a `git archive` mirror of
       the head before the change. From w10 on the cards move where a roll falls in the moved band, and in a whole run
       every later fight's dice move with them, as any change to a fight does.
     - No text shows the odds (the guide, Cara Main and the chest's popup don't), so no line changed. Nothing drawn.
     - Behaviour probe (test/probe_chest_odds.dart, 1000 chests a wave on seed 1, nothing taken; chest-odds-1790987227-
       probe): w25 Langka 0.530 / Epik 0.383 / Legenda 0.087 (odds 0.541 / 0.369 / 0.090), w100 0.500 / 0.372 / 0.128
       (0.508 / 0.364 / 0.128), w345 0.392 / 0.360 / 0.248 (0.400 / 0.350 / 0.250); 3000 cards each. Epik runs a little
       over its odds: the pity's Epik first cards and the noise (one standard deviation is about 0.009).
     - PROBE PLAN (the next QA cycle): Legenda come more often as the run goes on (w50 0.1025, w100 0.1275, against
       0.08). Measure on the b86 / b89 / c63 forward runs (the 'rarity' policy, 6 seeds) the falls a wave and the
       Legenda found by w60 and w90, against the head. The bar: falls a wave over w87-105 at least 0.9 × the head's (not easier).
       The Bayangan are still off on main, so report it with that caveat; once they are on, a Legenda card also gives
       the enemy 3 levels.
186. **Every agent the scripts start runs on a pinned model: a woken one keeps its own family on that family's newest
     model, a spawned one gets `claude-opus-5-5` unless told otherwise** (the owner, 2026-10-03: "untuk spawn agent opus
     selalu pakai opus 5.5 dan untuk sonet selalu pakai sonet 5.5"; built by sdlc-sync8; dev-workflow.md "Waking agents
     after a usage limit", sdlc.md sections 3, 5, 8 and 9):
     - Why: `scripts/wake-limited-agents.sh` started `claude --bg` with no `--model`, so a woken worker, test runner,
       the resumed orchestrator and other projects' resumed agents got the account's default model. Today that
       default is Opus 5.5, so a Sonnet agent would have come back on Opus, and a change of default would have moved
       every woken agent with it.
     - The wake script passes `--model` on every start it makes, fresh or `--resume`d, the orchestrator's and other
       projects' agents' too. The model comes from the stopped session's transcript, the `message.model` of its last
       assistant entry. Entries Claude Code writes itself for an API error (the rate limit among them) say
       `<synthetic>` and are skipped: on this Mac's 300 newest transcripts, 75,042 assistant entries said
       `claude-opus-5-5` and 303 `<synthetic>`.
       - opus → `claude-opus-5-5`, sonnet → `claude-sonnet-5-5`;
       - any other model (haiku, fable, …) → its own id, as it was;
       - none in the tail → `WAKE_MODEL`, default `claude-opus-5-5`.

       The state records the model each wake started (`"model"`), and the log and `--dry-run` name it.
     - A first version pinned `${WAKE_MODEL:-claude-opus-5-5}` on every wake. The orchestrator sent it back before the
       merge: a Sonnet session must stay Sonnet, other projects' agents included.
     - The orchestrator had already pinned `prompts/spawn-worker.sh` and `prompts/respawn-worker.sh` (`TD_MODEL`,
       default `claude-opus-5-5`; a Sonnet worker gets `TD_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5`, by hand on a respawn too).
       sdlc.md's blocks now carry that, and its test-runner start commands pass `--model claude-opus-5-5` (with
       `</dev/null`).
     - Checked:
       - `--selftest`, with `WAKE_STATE_DIR` on a throwaway copy: 104 ok, 0 BAD. It covers opus (an older opus too),
         sonnet, haiku and fable transcripts, none (only the synthetic limit), an empty one, and the newest model
         winning; a Sonnet worker woken fresh and another project's Sonnet agent resumed, both on
         `claude-sonnet-5-5`; and the model in the state. It passes with `WAKE_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5` too.
       - `--dry-run` on a copy of the real state: nothing to wake (0 woken).
       - The script was not run for real and woke nothing.

188. **The Bayangan act on the field: every monster's stats go through one wrapper, `spawnStats`, and today's seven
     kinds each have their hook (Armor, Haste, Mend, Thorns, Wound, Shield, Guard); Lewati's skip buff gives the next
     wave's first 30% of monsters by spawn order +10% to HP, damage, attack speed and walk speed. Still off on main**
     (step 0d of reports/catalog-design.md §5.1, part 2 of reports/enemy-buff-design.md, with the owner's Lewati rule of
     its §8: "buff emeny temporary first 30% enemy got 10% buff all attribute"; built by cat-0d; units-and-combat.md
     "Bayangan on the field", loot-items-relics.md "Bayangan", architecture.md, testing.md):
     - `spawnStats(type, tier, {raised, skipBuff, at, tideStart})` (lib/omen.dart) is `enemyStats` with the wave's tide,
       then `_omenStats`. It replaces `enemyStats` at all six sites: `Game.monster`, `_summon`, `decideSummon`'s count
       (the two must match), `_bringIn`, Slime Hex's form and the Dragon Crown tooltip's boss blow
       (`bossBlowsLived`). Off it returns `enemyStats`'s own `Stats`, so nothing moves.
     - Each kind's strength is `omenK(kind)`: perE × E at most its `max`, E through `omenE` only (so the probe's factor
       knobs cover every hook). Armor in `_hurt` after the target's defence and its `struck` Fx, on any blow whose `by`
       is a troop (cat-0f pointed out this includes Parry's answer and a bleed with a living source: intended, Armor is
       "troop damage to monsters"); Haste on `rate`, so `attackEvery`'s floors stay; Mend as `regen`, never a slot's;
       Thorns after the HP change beside worn thorns, melee troops only, capped by `omenThornsCap` 5% of the troop's max
       HP a blow and sent with no `by`; Wound plugged into cat-0e's seam (`_woundK` = `woundForce ?? 1 − omenK(wound)`);
       Shield its own `Unit.shield` field, not `Status.absorb` (catalog-inputs/1-enemy-hooks.md: as absorb Unholy Ward
       would never land and a later Ward would replace it), soaked next to the ward and cleared in `_endEffects`;
       Armor's and Haste's slot share `omenSlotShare` 1 (the probe's OMEN_SLOT arm).
     - Guard: `_omenQueue` puts `omenGuards` (⌈0.5 L⌉: 1, 1, 2, 2) high elites of `poolOf(wave).last` behind each slot's
       escort. The queue keeps its `(String, Tier)` record (some 30 test files read it): the guards are marked by their
       place in the wave (`_guardsAt`, matched against `waveSpawned`), come on their slot's row (`_guarded`) without
       the `rng.nextInt(rows)` draw, and nothing draws a die, so `rng` and `slots` stay paired. `Unit.guardOf` links a
       guard to its slot for the UI and the probe kit.
     - Lewati's buff: `Game.skipBuffN` = round(0.3 × the queue) at the wave's start, guards included; the spawn at
       `waveSpawned < skipBuffN` gets `skipBuff` (`Unit.skipBuffed`). No die, the spawn gap untouched, one wave.
     - Knobs agreed with cat-0i (the probe kit): `omenSlotShare`, `omenThornsCap`, `skipBuffShare`, `skipBuffK` are
       plain top-level consts, never used in a const context, so the kit's mirror can make them defines.
     - No player-facing line is new in this step (the HUD lines are the UI step's). On the remerge with main 776f8a6
       the kinds' titles took the English glossary's names (reports/english-text-design.md §3.7): Thorns, Shield and
       Guard show as Spikes, Barrier and Escort (the small relics Thorns and Guard and the item Shield keep theirs), and
       cat-0c's log lines read "Monsters got Armor 2 (chest w90)", "Late Shadow: Wound 2", "Carve: monsters got Haste
       1", "Shadow eased: Armor down to 1" (`Words.shadow`, `Words.carve`). Enum names, saves and telemetry unchanged.
     - The same remerge brought cat-0g's monster heal funnel: Mend's regen lands in `_healMonster` as
       `MonsterHeal.regen` through `_healUnit`, so a monster under `noHeal` gains nothing from it.
     - Checked on main 05b97a1 (the branch's base, main unmoved): test/omen_hooks_test.dart 10 tests; the full suite
       +1206 −0 (cat-0d-1790992512-suite); `analyze lib test` the 8 baseline infos; the identity probe
       (test/probe_pusaka_w89_identity.dart, omens off) on a `git archive` mirror of main and of the branch: the same
       1754 lines byte for byte, telemetry hashes f1e6c25e40b1b83f / facdda226fe3a222 / bedd463d6effe460 on both
       (cat-0d-1790991876-idmain, cat-0d-1790992524-idbranch); the 7 fights 5289 ms on main, 5244 ms on the branch.
       The public export's dry run: EXPORT OK. Balance is not weighed here: the QA cycle runs the design's P0-P2.
     - Re-checked after the remerge with main 776f8a6 (branch 455f78b): omen_hooks, omen, heal_funnel, ukir and cleanse
       tests +94 −0 (cat-0d-1791003914-focus); the full suite +1254 −0 (cat-0d-1791003914-suite); `analyze lib test` the
       8 baseline infos; the identity probe, omens off, on `git archive` mirrors of main 776f8a6 and the branch: the
       same 1754 lines byte for byte, the same three hashes as before (cat-0d-1791003914-idmain, -idbranch); fights

189. **The Bayangan's balance is weighed with one kit, the omen kit (`<agents>/probes/omen/`): the QA cycles'
     forward board probe with a knob for each of the design's arms and an `M` line a wave** (step 0i of
     reports/catalog-design.md §5.1, part 5 of reports/enemy-buff-design.md; built by cat-0i on 2026-10-03, whose
     branch never reached main; this entry filled its slot on 2026-10-08, 276; testing.md "The Bayangan"):
     - Why: the Bayangan ship dark (`omensOn`, 180), and the hooks (188) act only with it on. Their bars (P0 the OMEN=0
       identity, P1 each kind alone at L3, P2-P4 the b86/b89/c63/c86 bars, P5 Lewati against the take) need runs with
       omens forced on, a constant moved, levels forced, a pool cut, a Pusaka forced or the chest taken another way.
       None of that may touch main. The kit is QA-loop infra, not repo code: the repo holds only this entry and
       testing.md's note.
     - What it is: qa-12's `probe_board_late_qa12.dart` (qa-6's forward probe and the L line) with knobs, each listed
       in the kit's README: `OMEN=1|0`, `OMEN_SCALE`, `OMEN_ATCAP`, `OMEN_FACTOR`, `OMEN_TILT`, `OMEN_EASE`,
       `OMEN_CATCHUP`, `OMEN_CAP`, the hooks' `OMEN_SLOT`, `OMEN_THORNS` and `SKIP_BUFF`, `OMEN_FORCE` with `OMEN_PIN`,
       `OMEN_POOL`, `LIVE_OFF` / `LIVE_UPTO`, `FX_FORCE` and `DRAFT=rarity|fewest|skip`. `omenDice` is seeded k + 600,
       and an `M` line a wave gives the levels and E, the factor, the gains, eases, catch-up owed, the skip buff and the
       guarded, buffed and shielded spawns. `mkmirror.sh` makes a `git archive` mirror; `patch.py` turns each knob's
       constant in lib/omen.dart into a probe-only var (default: the ref's own expression), and a knob the ref lacks
       fails the run. `plan.sh p0 ... p5` queues the design's steps, `omen_agg.py` prints the bars, `same.py` is the
       identity, and `dryrun.sh` plus `drycheck.py` re-check every knob.
     - The rule it puts on the code: lib/omen.dart's tunable constants stay plain top-level `const`s, never used in a
       const context; `omenCap`'s default parameter in `omenPlace` is the one the patch rewrites. Checked on main
       222bde4: the twelve constants the patch takes are all still such consts, and `omenCap` is still the only one in
       a const context.
     - Its state: the dry runs gave 38 PASS on main 05b97a1 (the OMEN=0 identity, DRAFT=rarity as the lib's own pick,
       every knob; ids in the kit's ids-dry-cat-0i-05b97a1.txt). The dry set on main 776f8a6 (and dry-J/J0 on wt/cat-0d)
       was queued but never checked: cat-0i stopped at a usage limit, so its branch (23452ed, 54d8368) was never READY.
       29 commits have touched lib/omen.dart since 05b97a1. So a QA cycle runs `dryrun.sh check` on its head before any
       arm. No arm has run: balance runs wait until the features are done (the owner, 2026-10-03).
190. **Everything a player reads in the game is simple English, one word for each thing; 168's mixed rule is replaced**
     (the owner, 2026-10-03: "semua in game text di rubah ke bahasa ingriss"; english-text-design.md; ui-hud.md
     "In-game text"; amends 168):
     - Why: 168 put only the item text in simple English, so a tooltip said "Oath" beside a button saying "Sumpah"; the
       owner wants all of it in English.
     - What: about 470 strings in 34 files, in six batches (english-text-design.md §4); this one (B1, en1) the names:
       items (Sword … Staff), small relics (Fang, Thorns, Fury, Guard), troop types (Soldier, Knight, Swordsman,
       Archer, Lancer, Priest, Axeman, Wizard, Templar), monsters (Slime … Greatsword Skeleton, Necromancer, Necro
       Healer), ranks (Normal, Elite, High Elite, Mini Boss, Boss; first in a foe banner's line: "High Elite Orc"),
       a plate's kinds (Undead, Healer, Summoner, Raised), boss titles ("Morgath the Summoner"), the drop popup's stats
       (Defense, Attack, Heal, Range, Speed, Attack wait, Regen), the awakening and Forge levels ("Not awakened",
       "Awaken 3", "Awaken 5 (Max)", "Forge +6"), build names epithet first ("Giant Templar", "Undying Templar"), the
       Shadow titles Thorns, Shield and Guard shown as Spikes, Barrier and Escort (they clashed with the small relics
       and the item; cat-0d chose the same words on its branch), and the refusals beside them: the item picker's (Not
       for this type, Awaken first, At max, Max range), the relic's (Already holds <relic>, Relic slots full, Fallen,
       Bag is empty, Not held), the buy's (Not enough gold, No room), the release's (Not a type in your army, A Hero
       can't be sent home), and the shared "Only between waves" and "Game over".
     - The glossary's defaults are built (english-text-design.md §2; the owner hasn't picked yet): Artifact, Shadow,
       Awaken, Forge, Sharpen, Melt, Carve, Vault, Boss Chest, Reroll, Room, Tide, Rare/Epic/Legendary, Swordsman,
       Priest, Axeman. A later pick is one line: lib/words.dart, or a name table in game.dart, or a catalog row's
       epithet; the tests read the tables, not the words.
     - One word for one thing: the glossary is in ui-hud.md "In-game text"; the mechanic words and the shared refusals
       are constants in lib/words.dart (`Words.awaken` in `awakenName` and the picker's "Awaken first", `Words.forge` in
       `tempaName`, `Words.onlyBetweenWaves`, `Words.notEnoughGold`, `Words.gameOver` in `takeOffRefusals`,
       `buyRefusals`, `assignRefusals`), so a button, the guide's quote of it and its width probe can't drift. game.dart
       imports words.dart now (it only exported it).
     - Unchanged: save keys, enum names, telemetry fields, test ids, settings keys; the legal texts until the owner
       says; personal names. The other batches' sentences keep their Indonesian around the English names for now
       ("Budi (Soldier) gugur oleh Orc Rider Mini Boss", "Sudah Awaken 5 (Max)", "Knight: Bangkit 4!"): the store's,
       the chest's, the Pusaka's and the log's own refusals and lines are theirs.
     - test/english_text_test.dart fails on an Indonesian word in a lib/ string beyond each file's remaining count
       (`pending`: 407 literals in 28 files today; the later batches lower the counts to none), allowing the ids
       never shown and the legal texts. Its literal finder moved out of guide_text_test into test/lib_literals.dart,
       shared by both. The tests that pinned the old names read them from the tables (`troopTypeNames['knight']`,
       `awakenName(4)`, `holdsRelic(Relic.fang)`, `refusalNames[...]`, `buildEpithets[...]`); the catalog's epithet
       table and `statName`'s list are pinned in English. A Hero's recall label on a phone now fits one step longer
       ("Panggil  57k, tukar 1 Knight (+25)": "Knight" is shorter than "Ksatria"); recall_hud_test checks the swap is
       there, not which fallback.
     - No rule of play moved: no probe plan.

192. **The Bayangan v2 rules: the combined caps (`omenTakenFloor` 0.5, `omenDealtMost` 1.6), the omen flag
     (`Effect.omen`, `Unit.guardOmen`), the troop-side cap (`omenTroopRulesMax` 4), the acting faces (`OmenKind.needs`,
     `omenCanAct`) and the HUD numbers (`omenShown`). Still off on main** (step 0j of reports/catalog-bayangan-v2.md
     §5.1, the rules that keep the owner's 90 distinct kinds fair, "3a. tidak"; built by cat-0j; units-and-combat.md
     "Bayangan on the field", loot-items-relics.md "Bayangan", architecture.md, testing.md):
     - Why: before the data batches add 83 kinds, the engine needs rules that hold whatever mix is held: several cuts
       on one blow can't make a monster near-immune, several adds can't make one blow a kill, the troops can't be under
       more than 4 rules at once, and a face never offers a kind that would do nothing to this army.
     - The taken floor (`_omenTaken`, at Armor's site in `_hurt`): the product of every Bayangan damage-taken factor on
       one blow on a monster, never below 0.5. Today Armor (at most ×0.6, above it) and a Bayangan's guard while it
       holds the guard slot. A monster skill's guard isn't counted and still cuts after it, so `_hurt`'s guard line
       skips only an omen guard. `src` and `dmg` go in for the kinds that need them (Adapt's run, Blunt's line).
     - The dealt cap (`_omenDealt`, a monster's blow on a troop after its might, before the troop's defence): the blow
       with every Bayangan add, never more than 1.6 × the blow without them. The add counts an omen might, which stays
       in `_beforeDefence` like any might (so a link's share sees it), and the blow without it is the blow ÷ its k. The
       dealt factors and Wear Down's share join at the same site. With no omen might the blow is returned as it came,
       to the bit.
     - The omen flag: `Effect.omen` (`addEffect(..., omen: true)`) and `Unit.guardOmen` (set after a Bayangan's
       `_guard`; `_guard` and Bulwark clear it). `_wardable` ignores an omen absorb (catalog-bayangan-v2 §3's
       Counterspell row). The haste ring for an omen haste is left to the batch that brings the first one (Triumph,
       E-2B): agreed with cat-0h, whose 0h UI doesn't key off a field nothing sets yet.
     - The troop-side cap: `OmenKind.troopSide` (today Wound alone; the 12 of §5.1 come with their batches) and
       `omenPlace(..., troopMax)`. A troop-side kind not held yet has room only while fewer than 4 are held, and its
       levels overflow along the pool as past `omenCap`; the reveal names what was given.
     - The acting faces: `OmenKind.needs` (a set of `OmenNeed`, any one met; empty: always acts) and `omenCanAct`, a
       pure test on what the army meets, read once a roll (`omenMet`). `omenFace` maps the same single draw onto the
       acting kinds, so a card stays one draw and the faces are the same when every kind acts; the tilt's counter is
       exempt; with none acting the draw spreads over the whole pool rather than giving no face. `omenActFilter` (a
       plain const, so the probe kit can make it a define) turns the filter off for §5.3's OMEN_ACT=0 arm.
     - Every need of §5.1's table is built from today's code except `spiteMark` (Vengeance Mark or Ember Brand bound,
       G-1P / E-2P). The parts of a built need that wait for their batch: Vow of Silence's "not under it" (mpSkill,
       G-1P), Twin Fury's exception (everyFx, L-1P), Challenge Letter and Warden's Horn (taunt Fx, L-1P / E-2P), Ember
       Brand and Vengeance Mark (mark), Riposte and Mirror Shield (hitBack, L-2P / G-1P), Snare Cord and the other
       status Fx (slow, hold, weaken, hex: a bound status Fx is already read). Read beyond the table's examples,
       because they are the same thing in today's code: Parry and Iron Skin as hit-backs (their blow back is a
       `Hit.hitBack`), Curse of Weakness as a slow too.
     - The HUD numbers, agreed with cat-0h (0h fills the lines): `omenShare(kind, e)` is the one capped formula, which
       `omenK` (the hooks) and the HUD both read; `omenShown(kind, level, e)` gives `{x}`, `{n}` (`OmenKind.byL`,
       Escort's 1, 1, 2, 2, which `omenGuards` now reads), `{who}` (`OmenKind.who`) and `{cap}` (the share ×
       `OmenKind.steps`). 0h landed first (191), so this step made the agreed switch: `omenShownK` is
       `omenShare(kind, its level × omenShownFactor)`, and `omenEffect` fills `OmenKind.hud`'s `{x}`, `{n}`, `{s}`
       (0h's plural "s" of the count), `{who}` and `{cap}` from `omenShown` at the shown level (0 while off, as
       `omenGuards` was). The template token is `{x}` (the catalog's `{5E}` is design notation for perE). Grudge's
       `{type}` reads the game and is L-3B's.
     - No player-facing string is new (no kind has a `who` word yet).
     - Checked: test/omen_rules_test.dart 10 tests, with the omen, hook, boss and monster skill and hit-source tests +86
       −0 (cat-0j-1791008684-focus); on the branch merged with main 1578101: the full suite +1337 −0
       (cat-0j-1791028318-suite), `analyze lib test` the 8 baseline infos; the identity probe
       (test/probe_pusaka_w89_identity.dart) on `git archive` mirrors of main and the branch, omens off: the same 1754
       lines byte for byte, hashes f1e6c25e40b1b83f / facdda226fe3a222 / bedd463d6effe460 (cat-0j-1791025442-idmain-off,
       cat-0j-1791028318-idbranch-off); omens on (OMENS=true): the same 1776 lines byte for byte, hashes ad1ba1cf1ed1766a /
       0b6c08f13bd9a4d7 / 7b4827cf86c6b929 (-idmain-on, -idbranch-on). Again after the merge of main a6bb826 (en4): suite
       and analyze (cat-0j-1791029459-suite, -analyze), the identity off and on (cat-0j-1791029459-idmain-off/-on, -idbranch-off/-on).
       After main 97dc5cf (Carve UI, Bag cells; no engine change): suite and analyze (cat-0j-1791031544-suite, -analyze).

199. **A shooter stands at its hold, half a second of its shot's flight from its foe, not wherever its reach first
     touches it** (the owner, 2026-10-03 19:10: "butuh rework juga ai long range troops/enemy untuk jangan terlalu jauh
     juga dari center battle field tapi tetap maintain jaraknya agar particle/anak panah travel timenya tidak jadi lama
     karna enemy/troops terlalu jauh dari target"; worker ranged-ai; units-and-combat.md "Long range hold" and "Long
     range kite", lib/engage.dart `holdAt`, `kiteAt`):
     - The rule: `holdAt` = min(reach, max(`rangedGap` 4 tiles, `shotSpeed` × `rangedFlight` 0.5 s)), for troops and
       monsters alike: an archer 100 (or its reach, if shorter), a wizard 70, a skeleton archer 75 (or its reach). In
       reach but further off, a shooter steps up to its hold while it shoots; out of reach it walks there. A troop
       shooter kites a foe nearer than `kiteAt` = min(0.75 × its hold, 4 tiles) (it was 0.75 × its reach). Reach,
       damage and rate are unchanged: bows still let it hit further, they no longer set where it stands.
     - Why 0.5 s: before, the skeleton archers' bolts flew 0.40 s (median) and 0.57 s (one in ten longer), the owner's
       unhurried case; a base archer's 64 px is 0.32 s, a base wizard's 72 px 0.51 s. Half a second keeps those three as
       they were (the archer and the wizard hold at their reach) and brings every longer reach back to it.
     - Why the kite stops at 4 tiles: 0.75 × an archer's 100 is exactly a late skeleton archer's hold (0.75 × 200 =
       150 × 0.5 = 75), so an archer would back away from one that keeps stepping up after it, the drift of 153. Under
       4 tiles it never backs off a ranged monster standing at its hold (75 from wave 26 on). test/kite_stall_test.dart's
       scene became a melee mini boss: a wizard no longer kites from a skeleton archer one.
     - The leash the brief asked for (`rangedLeashTiles`, a cap behind the front line or the fight's centre) wasn't
       needed: a shooter's nearest foe is the front monster, and its hold already keeps it within 6.25 tiles of it.
       Healers keep their rules: a heal doesn't fly, a priest rests a tile behind the rearmost fighter, and the healing
       necromancer keeps out of the troops' reach.
     - Measured (test/probe_ranged_flight.dart: every shot from the tick it is fired to the tick it lands, and where
       each shooter stands twice a second; the w89 save's wave 90, three seeds, the view 341 px, the Mac's 1266×713
       window, and 219 px, a 412×860 phone; main's auto-player states w30 and w60 and the w86 board's w90, three seeds
       each, <agents>/qa-loop/states/57be560). Before (main a6bb826), fire = shooter to target when fired,
       centre = its distance from the fight's centre (`meetX`) in contact, screen = its x across the view:

       | Set | Shooter | Shots | Fire px med / p90 | Flight s med / p90 | Lost | Centre tiles med / p90 | Screen med |

       | w89 w90 | wizard | 3149 | 422 / 426 | 2.97 / 3.03 | 10480 | 25.9 / 27.3 | -0.67 |

       | w89 w90 phone | archer | 3907 | 103 / 139 | 0.50 / 0.67 | 1380 | 5.3 / 6.7 | 0.18 |

201. **A cap per troop type replaces the roster of 4 types a run: priest 5, archer and wizard 8, the six melee 10; the
     oaths count the types alive** (the owner, 2026-10-03 19:35: "kemarin yang aku maksud bukan jumlah troops yang di
     batasi dalam 1 group. tapi jumlah 1 trops yang bisa di beli, misal user tidak bisa beli lebih dari 5 priest, tidak
     bisa beli 20 archer supaya game tetap balance"; type-cap's design in <agents>/reports/type-cap.md;
     units-and-combat.md "The owner's limits" and "Hero Gugur", loot-items-relics.md "Legenda", ui-hud.md "Army" and
     "Troop counter"). It **amends 141** (the roster) and **155** (the oaths):
     - What he asked on 2026-10-01 ("ada batasan jumlah jenis troops yang bisa di spawn", built by 141 as a roster of 4
       types a run) was a limit on how many of ONE type can be bought, not on the types in the army.
     - **The caps** (`typeCapBoard`, a named map; the board turns them on, `boardRules` sets `Game.typeCap`; a plain
       `Game()` has none, so the tests and probes keep their rules): from his example and the roles, the healer 5 (heals
       stack: 17 priests made his w86 army almost unkillable; 5 is one in six of 32), the long range 8 each (half the
       army together), the melee 10 each (the line). Against `armyMax` 32: no type fills the army, nor do three; four
       do unless only one is melee (5 + 8 + 8 + 10 = 31); all nine add up to 81. His w86 save (priest 17, templar 13,
       wizard 9, axeman 6, archer 3) is over three caps. The owner tunes the numbers later.
     - **What counts** (`aliveOf`): the type's troops alive, its Heroes too (default; a Hero is a troop of its type),
       mid-wave too; the fallen don't. Read in one place, `Game.typeCapOf(type)`; `typeFull` = alive ≥ cap.
     - **Nobody is cut:** a type over its cap keeps its troops until they fall; its buys wait ("Priests full 17/5", the
       Army row's "x17/5" in red), as 141's army of 48 does. A one-time note (`caps`, `capsNote`) lists the types over
       ("Priest 17/5, Wizard 9/8, Templar 13/10").
     - **One gate:** `buyRefusal` asks `typeRefusal` first ("<Plural> full n/cap" from `troopTypePlurals`, or Oath of
       One's bar), so `place`, `autoPlace`, "Replace fallen" and the recall all meet it. Resurrection raises only a
       type under its cap (`_revivable`). A fallen Hero's recall swaps at a full type as at a full army (167's swap):
       one plain troop of its type goes home for half its price, so the type's count stays ("Knights full: … goes
       home").
     - **The roster is gone:** `runTypes`, `typeLimit`, `typeLimitBoard`, `rosterLimit` and the "Types full 4/4"
       refusal are removed; no type is locked by a count of types. Nothing needed the roster: the oaths now count the
       types alive, and the telemetry never recorded it (`TypeReleased` stays, no version bump). The save stops writing
       `runTypes` and ignores an older save's (one key fewer; an older build reading a new save takes the types alive).

       cap whole, and to bring Oath of One down to its two types. It now refuses a type with none alive ("Not a type in

       allies, Mourning Bell), so a healer passes over a troop at its ceiling; `_fxHealed` now gets the heal past full
       and runs no `heals` Fx (and no Dawn Star counter) for a heal that gave neither HP nor HP past full; **Gloat**
       (`_omenGloat`) in `_hurt`'s troop fall beside `_fxFell`, the killer through the monster funnel's new tag
       `MonsterHeal.gloat`; **Rekindle** (`_omenRekindle`) at the top of `_castMonsterSkill` for a high elite, tag
       `MonsterHeal.rekindle`; **Pummel** (`_omenPummel`) counts a monster's normal attacks on `Unit.blows` in `_strike`
       (only while the Bayangan are on) and marks every 3rd: `Game._pummeled` around a blow, `Shot.pummel` on an arrow to
       its landing, read in the dealt cap on the target's `Hit.normal` blow only (never a splash past it); a skill's blow
       never counts.
     - Grudge's piece (the M of §3.1, and nothing more): while on, `_omenKill` counts each monster a troop kills for its
       type (`_hurt`'s monster death, `by` a troop; a kill with no troop behind it counts for none) in `Game._waveKills`,
       emptied at each wave's start; at a won wave's end (`_omenTopKiller`, after the ease) the type with the most
       becomes `grudgeType`, a tie to the first in `troopTypes`' order, null after a wave no troop killed in. So the
       target is fixed for the whole next wave and named on the HUD between waves. `grudgeType` is saved (only while
       on, only when set; an unknown type is skipped on load); the tally isn't (a save holds no wave in progress).
     - Choices the table left open: Grudge's target is computed at the win rather than at `startWave` (the same target,
       and the HUD can show it between waves); with none its line says "none". Gloat and Pummel exclude the boss and a
       mini boss by rank, as Defiant and Straggler (a raised mini boss too). Rekindle heals as the cast lands, before

       second, folded in `_pusakaStats` as Dragon Heart's) and attack ×0.9 (its trade, one k at every star, so Carve
       never moves it). A ward now remembers the Pusaka that last added to it (`Unit.wardFrom`, not saved), so what Full

219. **Shadow batch E-3B: seven more Epik kinds (Prey, Herd Hunt, Old Bones, Grave Pact, Heal Siphon, Trickle, Toll), in
     the Epik pool alone. Still off on main** (data batch E-3B of reports/catalog-bayangan-v2.md §5.2, after E-2P (214);
     the owner, 2026-10-03: about 30 Shadows a tier, each kind in one tier, all in-game text simple English, features
     first, no balance work now; built by cat-E3B on 0j's rules (192); units-and-combat.md "Bayangan on the field",
     "Heals", loot-items-relics.md "Bayangan", ui-hud.md "Shadows", architecture.md, testing.md):
     - What: seven `OmenKind` rows, `tiers` {Epik}, each in its place in the enum so the Epik pool keeps the design's order
       (§2): today's seven, Prey, Dark Hymn, Bone Arrows, Arrow Ward, Second Skin, Bile Sacs, Blood Moon, Mark Ward, Herd
       Hunt, Last Rage, Parting Gift, Old Bones, Grave Pact, Captain, Enrage, Heal Siphon, Hunker, Counterspell, Close
       Ranks, Wear Down, Blindside, Envy, Trickle, Toll, Zeal, Triumph, Muster (34; Bat Venom goes in its place with E-3).
       Langka's 30 and Legenda's seven unchanged. Numbers are §3.2's: per E and most 0.06/0.4, 0.04/0.3, 0.08/0.4,
       0.05/0.3, 0.05/0.3, 0.4 s/2 s, 0.01/0.04; their lines, reaches and clocks are constants (`omenPreyBelow` 30,
       `omenHerdHuntAt` 10, `omenHealSiphonReach` 3 tiles / `Every` 1, `omenTrickled` {heal, prayer, sacrifice, pusaka},
       `omenTollEvery` 2 / `Above` 25).
     - Hooks, through what was there: **Prey** and **Herd Hunt** in the dealt cap (`_omenDealt`: the troop under 30% of
       its max HP before the blow; `_omenHerdHunt`, `aliveOf` its type ≥ 10); **Old Bones** a stat kind in `_omenStats`
       (`skeletonKinds`' HP, any rank, raised too, × the skip buff when both); **Grave Pact** in the taken floor
       (`_omenTaken`: `raisedBy` alive); **Heal Siphon** in the heal funnel (`_healTroop` adds share × what the heal gave
       to `Unit.siphonDue`) and a once-a-second tick step (`_omenHeals` → `_omenSiphon`, `Game._siphonAt`) paying it to
       the nearest monster below a mini boss within 3 tiles through `_healMonster` with the new tag `MonsterHeal.siphon`,
       the heal sparkle on it when it gained; **Toll** `_omenToll` in the kill path after `_monsterFell`: a `Hit.hitBack`
       of share × the killer's max HP, never below 25%, once per 2 s (`Unit.tollAt`), the necromancer's skull burst.
     - Trickle's M piece, exactly what its row names: a branch in `_healTroop` (after Wound) puts an `omenTrickled` heal on
       the troop as its own `TrickleHeal` (rate, end, paidTo; `Unit.trickle`), so a newer heal never moves an older one's
       end; `_omenTrickle` pays each its rate every tick up to its end, Scar's ceiling at each payment, never past full;
       past full is counted at the call against the HP plus what is still to come (`trickleLeft`); a fallen troop loses
       the rest and `_endEffects` drops it (with the Siphon debt). The readers: the heal sites that count a heal (the
       priest's and Healing Prayer's `heals` Fx and Dawn Star's counter, Hidden Flask, Blood Fang, Mourning Bell and Wolf
       Feast's tallies) read `Game._healGained` instead of the HP before and after (the same number with the Shadows off),

225. **The spawn floor: while a wave's queue holds monsters, at least one monster alive on the field for every 8 living
     troops; below it the next one comes on at once** (the owner, 2026-10-04, note.md: "minimal jumlah enemy di field
     adalah jumlah troops/8 jadi misalkan quota spawn enemy masi ada dan jumlah enemy di field kurang dari n maka system
     akan skip spawn time enemy, dan akan pakai timer spawn time lagi ketika musuh jumlahnya >= minimal enemy di battle
     ground."; built by spawn-floor; units-and-combat.md "Waves", testing.md):
     - `spawnFloorPer` 8, `spawnFloorOf(troops)` = troops / 8 rounded up, `Game.spawnFloor` over the living troops
       (Heroes count, the fallen don't): 0 with none, 1 with 1-8, 2 with 9-16, 5 with 33, 6 with 48.
       `Game.belowSpawnFloor`: the queue holds more and fewer monsters are alive than the floor.
     - In `tick` the spawn check reads `queue.isNotEmpty && (belowSpawnFloor || (_spawnTimer -= dt) <= 0)`: below the
       floor the timer is skipped and the queue's next monster comes on at once, one a tick at most, at the usual
       spawn point and lane. Every spawn sets the timer to `spawnGapOf(wave, wavePaceFrom)` as before, so once the
       floor is met the gap runs again from the spawn that met it (the owner's "pakai timer spawn time lagi").
     - Defaults the owner didn't name (in the report for the owner): every living monster counts toward the floor, a
       raised minion too, since it keeps the wave on like any monster (`waveActive`); a dying one doesn't. Troops
       still walking in count. No troop alive: no floor (the timer alone). The floor isn't saved (a save holds no wave
       in progress) and shows nowhere in the HUD; the wave meter's "A monster every N s" still holds above it.
     - Unchanged: the queue's order and contents, the tide's gap above the floor, the mini boss and boss slots and their
       escorts (`escortOf` by order), the Guard Bayangan's places and Lewati's skip buff (both by spawn order), the
       Town.
