232. **The asset vault: the licensed art and the packs in the repository only encrypted, for CI and members, with a
     JSON that makes sure every needed asset is there** (the owner, 2026-10-04: "semua asset dari komputer di zip dan
     kasikan password lalu di masukkan ke dalam repostiry supaya bisa di pakai di buid di ci, dan supaya kita tetap
     tidak menyebarkan ulang karya orang makanya di zip dan tidak akan di beritahukan kecuali orang tersebut adalah
     member kita dan perlu di buat kan json file untuk memastikan asset yang dibutuhkan ada semua"). By asset-vault.
     - **The rule it amends** (157, assets.md "Licence rule" and "Tools on this Mac", sdlc.md's bootstrap,
       raw_sprites/README.md): a pack's files never go into git as they are; the encrypted vaults in `assets-vault/`
       are the one exception. The plain licensed files under `assets/` stay tracked (orchestrator, 2026-10-04: taking
       them out of git would delete them from main's checkout at the merge, and history keeps them anyway; that is a
       separate owner decision).
     - `tool/asset_vault.py` (stdlib and the openssl binary): `check` (no key), `pack` (only vaults whose plaintext
       tar's sha256 changed; `--force` after a new key), `unpack` (parts' sha256 → decrypt → the tar's sha256 → every
       file against the JSON → write; never over other bytes without `--force`, and then nothing at all), `list`.
       Format: the tool's own deterministic ustar (sorted, 0644, uid/gid 0, mtime 2026-01-01, no pax headers) → gzip
       -n → `openssl enc -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -iter 600000 -md sha256 -salt` → parts ≤ 45,000,000 bytes
       (`<name>.tar.gz.enc[.partNN]`); one shell command opens a vault (`cat … | openssl enc -d … | tar -xzf -`).
       macOS's LibreSSL 3.3.6 and Homebrew's OpenSSL 3.6.4 open each other's.
     - `tool/asset_vault.json` (a new file, not asset_manifest.json, which goes public and holds only the licensed
       files' shapes): the one source of truth, per vault `name`, `group`, `pack`, `licence`, `needed_by_build`,
       `match` (game) or `slug` (packs), and from `pack` the tar's sha256, the parts' sha256s and every file (path,
       bytes, sha256, `needed_by_build`).
     - **12 vaults, not one "game"**: the brief's vault "game" is the group `game`, split by pack (tiny-rpg, effects,
       ui, icons, backdrops, town) plus `game-app-icon` (the platform icons the export also swaps for placeholders: a
       pack derivative a real build needs). A new icon then encrypts ~30 KB again, not 3.6 MB: assets/images changed in
       17 commits in the week before, and every re-encryption is new bytes in history. `unpack --only game` takes the
       group; game-town also takes battle-bg's coming `battle_floor.png` (the same pack; agreed with battle-bg). The
       packs: GandalfHardcore and Pixel Crawler (raw_sprites/), Kenmi's Icons Premium (its place outside
       every checkout, the packs' index `root`, as 157 wants), and, orchestrator's answer (a), Cute Fantasy UI and
       PixelRPGCursors Lite from raw_assets/ too ("semua asset dari komputer").
     - Sizes on throwaway keys: game ~4.4 MB, packs ~13 MB (Kenmi's 20,974 files 27.6 MB of tar → 9.5 MB), ~17 MB of
       ciphertext; the JSON ~4.7 MB.
     - **The key**: the owner's key file (`openssl rand -base64 32`, mode 600; since 315 a clone names its path with
       `git config poh.vaultKeyFile`), told only to members; CI's secret `POH_VAULT_KEY`, the same value. openssl
       reads it (`-pass file:` / `-pass env:`); the tool never reads, prints or puts it on a command line, refuses a
       key file open to group or others ("run chmod 600"), an empty one or one in the repo. dev-workflow.md "The asset vault's key" (backup, a new key).
     - **Checks**: `scripts/release-build.sh check` runs `asset_vault.py check` (every needed file at its path with its
       sha256, every licensed file and every file under a game vault's patterns in its vault, every part whole), so
       the release checks fail while the vault is older than the art: a job that adds or changes a licensed file runs
       `asset_manifest.py` then `asset_vault.py pack` (the owner's key, by its path). A vault never packed is only
       noted, so the repo passes before the key exists.
     - **CI** (`.github/workflows/release.yml`): a first step per job; with the secret, `unpack --only game` (here over
       identical files) then `check`; without it a `::warning::` and `check`. The secret only as that step's `env:`.
       Deviation from the brief's "else build as today (placeholders)": in this repo "as today" is the checkout's real
       art; a checkout without the art and without the key fails `check`, so no release is ever built on placeholders
       (an artifact that looks like a release). For the owner, if a placeholder CI build is wanted.
     - **The public export**: `--with-vault` (default OFF) puts `assets-vault/` and `tool/asset_vault.json` in the
       public tree, check 3 holding every part to the ref's listing; off, both are on NEVER. The owner decides it: an
       encrypted copy in a public history can't be taken back.
     - Tests: `tool/test_asset_vault.py` (11, throwaway keys, its own HOME), `scripts/test-release-build.sh` (the
       vault check, the workflow's one secret), `scripts/test-export-public.sh` (the switch off and on).
     - docs: assets.md ("The asset vault", Licence rule, Layout, Adding an image, Tools on this Mac, the public Tools),
       dev-workflow.md (Release build, "The asset vault's key"), itch-page.md (source and licence, the export, What a
       build ships, the release script and workflow), testing.md, sdlc.md (bootstrap step 2), raw_sprites/README.md,
       docs/README.md.
     - Checked: full suite asset-vault-1791099094-suite +1962 −0 on 88c0cbe (main 6fbe4bf merged; later commits touch
       only the JSON and docs); `analyze lib test` (-1791099094-analyze) the 8 baseline infos in lib/main.dart;
       tool/test_asset_vault.py 11 OK; test-release-build.sh 224/0; test-export-public.sh 85/0; EXPORT OK with the

250. **The forge's nine small relics act, the relics' cap 3.0 holds, and four hidden pairings work, never named** (the
     owner, 2026-10-04: "aku ingin item item relic nanti bisa di pakai untuk combo jadi nanti para player bisa mencari
     kombinasi dari relic dan artefak agar memberikan dmg sebesar mungkin, tapi jangan secara explisit di sampaikan ke
     player"). Build step F4 of forge-design (sections 5, 6 and 13; the combos C1-C9 of its model). By forge-F4. Dark,
     behind `forgeOn` and the Towns as F1's data (245): with either off no relic of the nine is in play, a troop holding
     one fights as without it, no cap cuts a blow, and the eleven are byte-identical (the w89 identity probe). The rules:
     loot-items-relics.md "The forge's nine"; the code: lib/relics.dart.
     - The nine's effects, at their town.json numbers (`relicKOf`): Chill (every 3rd landed normal attack slows 30% for
       1.5 s), Shark Tooth (x1.25 on a bleeding or poisoned monster), Grit (x1.30 under half HP), Ambush (x1.35 on a held
       monster, `foeHeld`), Weak Spot (a landed attack or smite marks the monster x1.12 taken for 3 s, `Status.vulnerable`),
       Hot Streak (+10% a kill for 4 s, at most 3), Avalanche (+8% a monster within 2 tiles of the target, at most 5),
       Afterglow (a skill's cast charges the next 3 attacks x1.5), Reaper (ends a monster a blow would leave under 15%).
       The new engine steps: a timed stacking buff (`Unit.streak`), a near-foe count (`alliesNearOf` on the target), N
       charged hits after a cast (`Unit.glow`, `_relicCast` beside the Artifacts' cast Fx) and an execute.
     - Defaults taken (no question asked; each a line in the code and the doc):
       - "Bosses" are a mini boss and the boss, as Giant Slayer's: Chill slows them half (15%), Weak Spot marks them x1.06,
         Reaper never ends one and hits one under its line x1.5 instead.
       - The factors multiply the attack as made (`_strike`, `_smite`), so a shot carries them, and so do a splash,
         Sweep, Venom's poison and God's Thunder's leaps (what the design's C1 and C4 figures assume); Giant Slayer stays
         where it is, at the landing. A skill's blow, a bleed tick and a sweep's own share get none of the nine.
       - The cap (`combos.relicMost` 3.0) is cut on the attack's target, over the beat (x2, x2.5 under Relic Altar), Giant
         Slayer and the nine; past it the nine's part comes down (Relic Altar's 3.75 with Giant Slayer → 3.0). The
         Artifacts' own powers and every mark stay outside it. The cap acts only with the forge on, so Relic Altar with
         Giant Slayer is 3.75 as today with it off.
       - Relic Altar's x1.25 stays on its four sites (Fang, Thorns, Fury, Guard); not on the seven or the nine.
       - Chill keeps its own count of hits (not Fury's) and counts normal attacks only; Weak Spot marks on blows, shots and
         smites. Weak Spot's mark is Hunter's Mark's status (the stronger stays); Void Eye's and Vengeance Mark's multiply.
       - The pairings (town.json `combos.secret`) read only with the forge and the Towns on; an Artifact pairing counts
         when the holder's type has it bound at any star. They are in the docs only as design: loot-items-relics.md's
         "The hidden pairings and the combos measured" is the private-section marker, and F1's (245) line naming the four moved
         into a private block (the public export never names them).

     are fine, but more item KINDS on top). Build step F9 of forge-design (sections 10, 13; model
     probes/forge-design/model_grade.py `NEW_EFFECT`), on forge-F1's data (245: the 42 items, town.json `items.<name>.effect`).
     By forge-F9, beside forge-F3 (249, crafting and Awaken by grade) and forge-F4 (250, the nine relics).
     loot-items-relics.md "The forge: the new kinds' effects" holds the rules.
     - Dark, behind `forgeOn` and the Towns: `Game.statsOf` folds `Stats.upgraded(item, k)` with `k = Game.itemK(item)`
       (town.json's effect) only with both on, else null, and the five's arms need a `k`. So with either off a type
       holding them fights as before, and the seven's arms are untouched. The API (`upgraded(Item, [double? k])`,
       `itemK`, the fold) was agreed with forge-F3, which wires the seven's grades and the Cap/Helm (damage taken) and
       the Ring (MP regen) through it: both briefs named Cap and Ring; forge-F3 took them, the orchestrator noted it.
     - Amulet: `hp` × k, rounded at each one. `statsOf`'s awaken line no longer rebuilds HP and MP regen from the base
       alone: the awakening's HP is times what the items added (`held.hp / base.hp`, exactly 1.0 without an amulet) and
       the MP regen keeps what the items added (`+ (held.mpRegen - base.mpRegen)`, exactly +0.0 without a ring), so the
       Amulet and forge-F3's Ring count at Awaken 1+ (owner question 9's default: yes, the Amulet raises max HP).
     - Prayer Beads: a healer's `dmg` × k and a new `Stats.healK` × k; the potion's and the staff's added heal become
       `potionHeal * healK` / `staffHeal * healK` (× 1.0 without beads), keeping the old rule that the order items came
       in doesn't change a heal. The holy damage on the undead (`holyShare` of the heal) follows by itself.
     - Torch: a new `Stats.darkK` × k, and one line in `_hurt` right after Giant Slayer (forge-F4 told, its relic block
       apart): a blow from a striker with `darkK` ≠ 1 on a `Stats.dark` foe is times it, before defence. Thorns' hit-back
       passes no striker, so it never counts; a monster's `darkK` is always 1.
     - Spear: a new `Stats.reachCap` (`meleeMaxRange` by default) × k with the reach (`max(range, min(range × k, cap ×
       k))`), melee only; the bow, `Stats.boosted` (the aura, a Hero), Hawk Feather (`_pusakaStats`), `whyNot`'s
       `Refusal.reach` and the Army detail's red bow ink read `reachCap` instead of `meleeMaxRange`. The design's numbers

255. **Enhance: from wave 30 a Town's Smithy takes an item up to +5 with Mithril and Starmetal, never failing** (the
     owner, 2026-10-04 ~19:15, forge-design §12-13 and the owner's answers 13-14: "Enhance opens from wave 30, up to +5,
     never fails, any grade"; "an enhanced item is its own Bag stack, swapping out the lowest-plus one on a full type").
     Build step F8 of forge-design, by forge-F8, started early (the owner, 2026-10-07: "tambahkan 2 worker lagi untuk
     kerjakan feature only") while forge-F5 (254, the Smithy's strip) was in flight, so in two phases: the data and the
     rules first (this part), the Enhance tab, the colour filter and the "+N" tag after 254 lands. Dark behind `forgeOn`
     and the Towns like every forge step. loot-items-relics.md "The forge: Enhance" holds the rules.
     - **Where it lives:** a new `part of` game.dart, lib/enhance.dart (`extension Enhance on Game`), so lib/town.dart
       (town-polish's 253 nearby) gained only two refusal reasons (`CraftWhy.closed` "Opens after wave 30", `CraftWhy.top`
       "Max: +5") and EnhanceRules' comments. The orchestrator's condition: `Game.enhanceOpen` is the ONE source of the
       wave-30 rule (behind `forgeOn` and the Towns); forge-F5's top-level `enhanceOpen(g)` in smithy_page.dart is replaced
       by it in phase 2, in the same commit that deletes it.
     - **Stacks keyed by (item, plus), additively:** the +0 items stay where they were (`inventory`; `upgrades` lists every
       item a type holds, enhanced or not), and the "+" lives beside them: `Game.enhancedBag` ((item, plus) → n) and
       `Game.upgradePlus` (type → item → its copies' "+", highest first). So the Awaken counts, levels, caps and prices
       read exactly as before (the design: "Enhance never changes the Awaken counts"), every existing caller and test of
       `upgrades` / `inventory` stands, and a save without the new keys is all +0. The save writes `bagPlus` and
       `upgradePlus` as lists of `{item, plus, n}` (the design's shape), only with the forge on and only when any; no
       version bump (saveVersion stays 3: the forge hasn't shipped). The orchestrator asked that a forge-off save carry
       none of them: the test checks it, and the w89 identity covers the rest.
     - **Stats per plus:** `Game.itemK(item, [plus])` → `enhancedK`: a factor 1 + (k − 1)(1 + per × plus), a flat one
       (shield, potion, ring: `flatKinds`) k × (1 + per × plus), +0 returned untouched (bit for bit, so the fold without a
       "+" is the old one: `_itemsOn` keeps the old one-line fold when the type has no "+"). The design's examples hold:
       Royal Sword 1.48, Royal Gloves 0.625, Royal Shield 9, Gold Amulet 1.18 at +5.
     - **Replace by plus at the cap:** `swapOut(type, item, [plus])`: an Awaken kind at its grade's cap swaps out its own
       lowest-plus copy when the new "+" is higher; the Cap's and the Ring's chain ranks by grade, then plus, so a higher
       grade still always wins. The one out returns to the Bag at its "+". `useItem`, `canUse`, `whyNot`, `priceWith` and
       `assignPreview` take an optional `plus`; the two try-ons share `_triedOn` (both lists set and put back).
     - **Stone crafting and the steps** follow the Smithy's Craft (`CraftRow`, `CraftRefusal`, `_payCraft`, its order of
       refusals): `craftStone` (event `StoneCrafted`) needs Enhance open too (the stones only show on the Enhance tab),
       `enhance(item, plus)` (event `ItemEnhanced`) takes the step's stone and gold, no dice. Both pass on to the
       telemetry (`stoneCrafted`, `itemEnhanced`; a wave's `crafted` counts stones, `materialsUsed` and `craftSpent` both);
       the battle log says "Crafted Mithril (1,000 gold)" and "Enhanced Royal Sword to +3 (1,500 gold)" (a literal
       "Enhanced" until 254's `Words.enhance` lands, then from it). `itemUsed` and `storeSold` carry `plus` above 0.
     - **The Shop** buys an enhanced item for the item's price plus half its steps' cost (the gold at
       `shop.itemSellShare`, each stone at its sell price, itself half a stone's worth): `sellPriceAt`, `sellAt`.

261. **The test queue runs fewer `flutter_tester`s: at most 2 per `test` job, and one runner with one test agent** (the
     owner, 2026-10-07: "itu di batasin jumlah spawn flutter_tester makan cpu banget", then "itu sudah banyak banget
     kalau 4. untuk flutter test ini buatkan 1 agent yang lakukan test"; the live queue changed by the orchestrator
     and test-runner, the docs synced by wake-gw; sdlc.md sections 2, 4, 6, 7, 9 and 11, testing.md "Running them",
     dev-workflow.md's wake routes):
     - Why: two runners on full suites ran 8 `flutter_tester` processes at about 95% CPU each, and the load reached
       14 on 8 cores. `flutter test` starts one tester per two cores by default, 4 on this Mac, per runner.
     - Concurrency: `testq/runjob.py` gives every `test` job `--concurrency=<n>`, `<n>` the first number in
       `testq/concurrency.txt` (now 2), clamped to 1..8, and `DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY` 2 without the file. It is read
       per job (no runner restart); a request with its own `--concurrency` / `-j` keeps it. `concurrency.txt` is
       state, embedded in section 11 as a `once` block holding 2.
     - A whole suite is slower for it. The first one run with the flag (val-forge-1791338782-suite2, runner 1,
       2026-10-07 09:13–09:28, 2,373 tests, load 5–6) took 914 s; the 13 suites before it at Flutter's default
       (2026-10-04 to 2026-10-06, runner-1.log and their done files) took 272–526 s, median 341. The one finished at
       09:03 (891 s) had started at 08:49, before `runjob.py` changed at 08:56, and ran without the flag at load
       14–18.
     - The suite's limits follow (test-runner's edits, 2026-10-07; backups `*.bak-20261007b`): `runjob.py`'s
       `SUITE_TIMEOUT` 20 → 28 min, `watch.sh`'s `LONGJOB` mark for a suite 840 → 1320 s (22 min; probes and single
       files stay at 600 s), `runner.sh`'s `RUNNER_MAX_SECS` comment (a suite "may take 28 min"; its 1800 s margin
       stays above it), and PROTOCOL.md's lines. 914 s had been past the old 14-min mark and three quarters of the old
       20-min kill. Raising `concurrency.txt` to 3 was proposed (wake-gw) and turned down: 2 is the owner's call ("itu
       sudah banyak banget kalau 4").
     - The preamble's probe line now says one runner runs one job at a time with at most 2 testers, so a full suite
       takes ~15 min: never queue the same check twice, reuse another worker's result on an identical tree. The
       infra README marks test-runner-2 retired.
     - One runner: runner 2 and its role session test-runner-2 are retired as of 2026-10-07 (runner 2 stopped after
       its job, its claimed request moved back to `req/`). One fresh role session, `test-runner` on Sonnet 5.5, runs
       runner 1 and `watch.sh`; runner 1 serves every lane alone in `pick.py`'s lane-1 order (checks, the features'
       probes, then QA probes). So at most 2 testers run at a time. `prompts/test-runner-2.md`, `pick.py`'s lane 2
       and the wake script's `test-runner-2` role stay, so a second runner can come back on the owner's word.
     - `testq/watch.py`: `save()` writes a per-pid temp file, `.watch_state.json.<pid>.tmp`, before the rename. Two
       watchers had raced on one temp name and crashed.
     - Section 11's `--export` also brought in live changes that had never been synced: the 2026-10-04 rule that a
       request whose done file exists never runs twice (`runner.sh` files it as `req/processed/<id>.dup-<ts>.json`
       on a restart, `pick.py` before a claim, PROTOCOL.md's lines), the preamble's sprite-map, queued-job and
       asset-vault rules, and test-runner-2's overload line (load over 20 for 5 min, was over 12). `--check`: no drift,
       35 files; the bootstrap's `--selftest` passes.

272. **The forge's cut-over: the forge on in every build, the saves from before it keeping their Awaken levels** (the
     owner, 2026-10-08: "di smithy kenapa belum ada opsi utuk crafting item upgrade army?", his game restarted without
     `--dart-define=FORGE=true`; asked whether to cut over, his option verbatim: "Cut-over: forge ON default — forge menyala
     untuk semua build tanpa flag (forgeLive = true), cek save lama aman dimuat (backup dulu), guide/teks, docs, dan
     baseline test diperbarui. Setelah merge, tinggal jalankan ./scripts/dev-macos.sh biasa."). By forge-cutover, on the
     forge's steps 245-255 and 262. loot-items-relics.md "The forge: items crafted, Awaken by grade" holds the save rule;
     every "dark" forge section there, ui-hud.md, architecture.md, telemetry.md, game-overview.md and testing.md now say
     the live state.
     - **The switch:** `forgeLive` (lib/forge_flag.dart) defaults to true; `--dart-define=FORGE=false` still builds the
       game from before the forge (comparisons, the identity probe). Every board game (the Towns on) plays the forge: no
       item drops, about three times the materials, the items crafted at a Smithy in three grades, Awaken by grade, the
       twenty small relics, the Shop's materials shelf, Enhance from wave 30. A plain `Game()` (the Towns off) is as before.
       After this merge the owner runs `./scripts/dev-macos.sh` with no define.
     - **Old saves, for the owner:** a save from before the forge keeps every troop type's Awaken level (and the Awaken 4-5
       and Forge levels bought on top of it), because its old items can't make a grade set. The type's next Awaken then
       takes the next grade's items, made at the Smithy.
     - **How:** Awaken isn't saved but read from the items a type holds (`itemLevel`), and by grade a level takes the
       grade-L set with the type's new kind (Amulet, Torch, Beads, Spear, Prism), which no old save holds: on the w89
       fixture every type fell to Awaken 0, and since Bangkit 4-5 and Tempa count only from Awaken 3 the priest's, the
       axeman's and the wizard's bought levels (gold paid) went too. So a save without the new key `awakenKept` keeps, per
       type, its old-rule level (`oldItemLevel`: the recipe's whole repeats, at most 3) in `Game.awakenKept`, and by grade
       `itemLevel` counts on from it (`keptLevel`): `awakenNeeds` / `awakenShort` start past it, so the next Awaken takes
       the next grade's set alone. The old grade-I items stay on the type with the stats they had (grade I's numbers are
       the old constants) and count against nothing new: past the grade-I caps they only block more grade I, like the
       items from before the caps. Bag items are grade I: given within the grade-I caps, or sold. Every by-grade game saves
       `awakenKept` (`{}` included), so a by-grade save is never read by the old rule again and a new game's stays empty
       (its grade-I items never make a level: a knight with the old recipe and no Amulet stays Awaken 0 after a reload).
       A forge-off game neither writes nor reads it: its save is byte for byte as before. The orchestrator approved this
       (option A of three; B a saveVersion 4 as the trigger, C no migration) with four conditions, all met: Bangkit and
       Tempa stay valid (w89: priest, axeman, wizard Awaken 5 with Tempa 4, 6, 1, archer and Templar Awaken 2, the same
       stats on and off), the Army detail says it ("Awaken 3 (kept from old items)", "(kept)" where narrow; `Words.keptFromOld`,
       `Words.kept`), a new forge game never writes a non-empty `awakenKept`, and these sentences.
     - **saveVersion stays 3:** the migration is additive and keyed on the key's absence, which a forge-off build never
       writes; an older build loads a newer save (it checks only `v` ≥ 2) and ignores the key. A dev save written with
       `FORGE=true` before this (no key) is read by the old rule once: under the forge's caps its grade-I items give at
       most Awaken 1, and only where the type held the old recipe without its new kind.
     - **The owner's save:** backed up to <agents>/snapshots/save-pre-forgecutover-20261008-050058.json, never
       touched; a copy is test/fixtures/save-20261008-0438-w13-preforge.json (wave 13, in a Town, no items, 236 materials,
       Bright Spring and Warden's Horn bound): it loads with its gold 719, lives, score, 18 troops, materials and

273. **The whole suite runs only on main, in one dedicated worker; runner 2 is back as the main lane** (the owner,
     2026-10-08: "full suite test ini sepertinya kita jalankan di main saja dengan 1 worker sendiri", after asking
     what keeps him from seeing a worker's change in his game quickly; measured and implemented by main-suite, the
     orchestrator and test-runner; sdlc.md sections 2, 3, 6 and 11, testing.md, dev-workflow.md):
     - Why: one test runner served 5 workers, and 10-second analyze jobs waited 10-60 min behind 11-minute whole
       suites. The owner approved three options: short jobs first, runner #2 back (peak 4 `flutter_tester`
       processes), and a lighter merge gate.
     - The gate: a feature worker's READY is `git merge main` + `analyze lib test` + the test files its change touches
       (every file it added or changed, plus the existing files that cover the code it changed) + its shots, identity
       and export check. The orchestrator fast-forwards; then the worker `main-suite` runs the whole suite on that main.
       Merged workers wait idle until a `MAIN GREEN` covers their merge.
     - The queue: `runjob.py` refuses a `test` naming no `.dart` file unless the request is from `main-suite` or the
       orchestrator added `"allow_suite": true` (exit 2, not an INFRA line). Runner 2 is the main lane: the requests
       of `main-suite` go first; runner 1 stays the features' lane.
     - main-suite: long-lived, one suite at a time on a fixed mirror of main (`<agents>/mirrors/main-suite`,
       so `.dart_tool` and the build survive), merges that land during a run are covered by the next. GREEN is the
       suite passing and analyze at the 8 baseline infos; `MAIN GREEN <sha>` or `MAIN RED <sha>` (the failing tests,
       the first bad merge by bisecting on `main-bisect`, the last green) goes to the orchestrator. It fixes nothing:
       a red goes back to that merge's worker.

281. **The Boss Chest without Later: the player must take or skip it; Take sits in the button row, greyed until a card is
     picked** (the owner, 2026-10-08: "remove later button dari opsi chest boss jadi user wajib ambil dan button later
     itu di ganti dengan take yang aktif ketika user sudah pilih": take the Later button out of the boss chest's options
     so the player must take, and put a Take there that is active once the player has picked). Built by chest-take
     (lib/chest_popup.dart). ui-hud.md "Boss Chest" holds the popup; loot-items-relics.md "Peti Bos" the rules.
     - **Which chests:** every chest this one popup shows: a won boss wave's ("Boss Chest", `ChestKind.boss`) and an old
       save's catch-up ones ("Missed Chest 1/3", `ChestKind.catchUp`).
     - **The row** is Reroll, Skip and **Take**, a third each, in Later's place. Take is the popup's main action: the same
       `_button` as the row's others in the pack's green (`_btnGreen`, the old on-card Take's colour), greyed (`_btnWhite`,
       grey "Take", no press) until a card is picked. Its words are `Words.take`; the hint above already says what to do
       ("Tap a card to pick it", then "Tap Take to get it"), so no new string ("Pick a card first" was not needed).
     - **Picking:** a tap on a card picks it (lifted 6·f and lit, as the old first tap); a tap on another moves the pick;
       a tap on the picked one again keeps it and takes nothing. The second-tap take is gone with the on-card green Take,
       on purpose: with no Later to back out, a double tap on a phone mustn't take a card the player hasn't read, and
       one Take is the owner's design. A press elsewhere on the popup (a near miss of Take between the buttons included)
       now keeps the pick, where it used to let a lifted card down, so a miss never greys Take under the finger. Reroll
       and Skip are as they were (Skip's first press still lets the pick go; Reroll deals new cards, nothing picked).
     - **The cards** lose the bottom band the on-card Take sat in (4·f + 28·f), so they and the panel are shorter; on a
       phone with the Shadows on (`omensOn`) the band stays, for a revealed Shadow's name, so a card is as tall with
       marks as without (omen_look.dart); in landscape the marks row sits at the card's bottom.
     - **No waiting:** `_ChestView.later`, `Draft.chestMayWait`, `offerQueueMax` (2), `chestRefusals.full` ("Too many
       chests: open one", its red hint) and `Words.later` are gone. A chest is due whenever one waits (`_chestDue`), the
       popup opens between waves after the win's cheer and any Hero splash, and stays until Take or Skip; with more
       waiting the next opens on the next frame. The Auto countdown holds the whole time (`_chestHolds`), and a Town due
       after a boss wave is gone into only after it (town_look.dart's `calm`, which Later used to free).
     - **Start opens a waiting chest** (the follow-up: chest-take's first READY left Start in a boss win's 2.4 s cheer
       starting the wave, the chest waiting through it as the chip; the orchestrator, for the owner's "user wajib
       ambil", had the alternative built): Start pressed while a chest waits for its popup (`_startPress` →
       `_chestNow`) opens it at once, the cheer cut short, and starts no wave. While a new Hero's splash shows or waits
       it does nothing (the splash would draw under the popup; the chest opens after it by itself). Auto was already
       held (`_chestHolds`), so its wave comes only once the chest is taken or skipped. No chest can wait through a wave
       any more, so the "Chest!" chip is drawn only between waves (`whyNotChest` null): in the cheer and behind a Hero
       splash, where its tap does what Start does; its mid-wave case ("Only between waves") is gone.
     - **Unchanged:** the save (Later was never saved: a save from before this with chests waiting opens them one after
       another at load); telemetry (no Later event: `offerShown` / `offerPicked` / `offerRerolled` as before); the
       game's rules (`takeCard`, `rerollChest`, `skipChest`); the probes' auto-player (`draftPolicy` takes its chests in

297. **A troop healer's heal costs MP: 6 a heal; short of it, no heal** (the owner, 2026-10-09: "army/enemy healer
     harusnya ketika melakukan heal itu akan menggunakan mp-nya" (army and enemy healers should use their MP when they
     heal); of heal-mp's phase 1 options the owner picked "A: 6 MP/heal, habis = stop" (6 MP a heal, empty = stop)). Built by
     heal-mp together with 298 (one design: the same MP). units-and-combat.md "Stats", "Fighting rules" (Healers) and
     "Troop skills", ui-hud.md "Skills" and the Army detail's attributes hold it.
     - **Before:** only the healing necromancer paid for its heals (`necroHealCost` 8 of its 40 MP, decisions-log 43); a
       priest's heal was free, its MP (60, +3/s) only for its skills. So the monster half of the owner's rule already
       held, and stays as it was.
     - **The rule:** every heal a troop healer gives in a wave costs `healMp` 6 MP (`_castHeal`): 10% of a priest's base
       pool, flat, so awakening, a Hero and the aura (which raise the pool and its regen) make it heal more. Short of it
       (`_heal`), no heal: it smites the weakest undead in its range (free, as before) or waits where it stands. MP comes
       back only at its regen and what refills MP. Its smites and the after-wave heals stay free.
     - **Skill first** (the owner's pick in 298: "Priest: skill first, heals use the rest"): while a skill of its is ready
       and has a target, its heals leave it the MP (`_healWaits`: its Hero skill, its awakening skill, Healing Prayer).
     - **What the player sees:** the MP bar under its HP drains 6 with each heal; "No MP" (`Words.noMp`) pops over it in
       the MP bar's blue once a dry spell (`Unit.dry`, `Game.noMp`); the Army detail says MP "Pays for heals and skills"
       (`Words.healerMpHelp`) and Heal "HP back per heal, 6 MP"; the MP tooltip "Each heal: 6 MP".
     - **Measured in phase 1** (heal-mp's probe, 45 s of a wave, seeded): a priest's heals a second: a lone priest at
       wave 9 0.71, five at wave 14 0.58-0.70, 17 at wave 90 0.26 (they smite more than they heal there). Six MP a heal
       would have found the priest short on 31%, 0-12% and 0% of them. Balance is not tuned (the fast lane): the PROBE
       PLAN is in reports/heal-mp.md.
     - Not changed: saves (MP isn't saved), the telemetry, the healing necromancer and Mass Mend, the Mana Burn and Spell
       Tax omens (a heal is no skill, so Spell Tax doesn't raise its cost).
298. **The troops cast whenever they have the MP, the cooldown is over and a target** (the owner, 2026-10-09: "ini kenapa
     para army jarang pakai skill ya, harusnya selagi masi ada mp, dan skill avaliable para army spam aja skillnya" (why
     do the troops rarely use skills? as long as they have MP and the skill is available they should just spam it); of
     heal-mp's phase 1 the owner picked "Spam penuh" (full spam) and for the cut-ins "Dibatasi" (limited)). Built by heal-mp with
     297. units-and-combat.md "Troop skills", "Awakening skills" and "Hero skills", ui-hud.md "Skills" and the Hero's
     cut-in hold it.
     - **Why they were rare** (phase 1, the w89, w13 and w8 fixtures' waves): MP held a #10 skill back 0-6% of the time;
       its cooldown (10-16 s) 26-99%, and its rule (2-3 foes, a low HP) the rest. About 2-4 casts a troop a minute, the
       Healing Prayer 0.1-2, a Hero one a wave.
     - **#10 skills:** each costs `skillMpShare` 25% of its type's base MP pool (5 to 20; was 15-40) and comes again
       after `skillCooldown` 4 s, or 2 s after its own effect (Hold Fast 5, Rampage 6, Holy Shield 6; were 10-16 s); a
       target is enough (`wantsSkill`: a foe in its reach; Healing Prayer 2 troops below 90% round the most hurt; Holy
       Shield a fighting troop near not guarded that strongly).
     - **Awakening and Hero skills:** the same rule with their cooldowns halved (`awakenCdK`, `heroCdK` 0.5;
       Resurrection stays once a wave) and their costs kept; every crowd is 1, the caster's own low-HP gates are "hurt at
       all", a foe's HP worth is 0. What a skill names as its target stays (a strong foe, a dying or badly hurt ally, a
       fallen troop, Execute's foe under 25%), and so does every "above" that keeps a troop from leaping or giving HP
       while low (Skyfall, Sacrifice, Shared Wounds, Guardian Leap, Death Leap). The bigger skill keeps first claim on the
       MP (`_savingUp`, `_savingForAwaken`), else the cheap #10 skill would keep the pool under it. Last Stand's
       "hurt" is now any HP lost (`<`, it was `<=` 40%, so at 1 it would have cast at full HP); Skyfall's book line
       "Leaps where troops fight" (was "into a crowd").
     - **Oath of Spells:** its ×0.8 never goes under `cdFloor` 5 s nor over a skill's own, so with the #10 skills at
       4-6 s it leaves a 4 s one as it is and brings a 6 s one to 5; the awakening and Hero cooldowns still come ×0.8
       sooner (Cleave 12.5 → 10 s). `cdFloor` is kept (a question for the owner in the report: lower it to keep the
       oath's 20% on the #10 skills).
     - **Monster skills:** unchanged (the owner asked about the army; the champions' skills are the waves' difficulty).
     - **The screen** ("Dibatasi"): a skill's name pops on a troop's first cast of it a wave (`FirstCasts`); its look
       (ring, beam, zone) shows every cast; a Hero's cut-in at most once per Hero every 20 s and 3 s after any other
       (`HeroCutGate`, `heroCutEvery`, `heroCutGap`); the cast itself always happens.
     - **Measured** (the same fixtures, 45-120 s of a wave): casts a troop a minute about 10-15 (was 2-4; the cooldown is
       what holds them now); the waves end sooner (the w8 save's wave 9 won in 37 s, still on at 120 s before). The troops
       are clearly stronger; balance is not tuned (the fast lane): the PROBE PLAN is in reports/heal-mp.md.
     - **The wind-up** (299, skill-anims, agreed with heal-mp): a troop's or a Hero's skill will land on its animation's
       strike frame; MP and the cooldown are paid at the wind-up's start, where the cast is logged, and the want rules
       (`wantsSkill`, `wantsHeroSkill`, `wantsAwakenSkill`) change nothing, so the land can ask them again.

307. **Troops are drawn walking where the game moves them in jumps** (the owner, 2026-10-09: "ini beberapakali aku liat
     para army di pindahnya tidak natural langsung kaya lompat gitu" (a few times I've seen the troops move unnaturally,
     straight away like a jump) and "ketika auto buy troops juga aneh banget tropsnya harusnya animasi jalan ini kaya
     slide gitu" (with Auto Buy the troops look really odd: they should play the walk animation, but they slide); his
     recording at wave 30, 34 troops, x1, Auto Wave and Auto Buy on). Built by troop-motion with 308. ui-hud.md "Troops
     drawn moving" and formation-and-navigation.md "How the moves look" hold it.
     - **What caused it** (phase 1, a probe on a copy of his save: wave 30 replayed whole, 72 s, 16 ms frames through
       the Board, every troop's every tick split by what moved it and the strip it played; reports/troop-motion.md):
       1. jumps: the separation gives the yielder the whole gap to each neighbour, all of them in one tick, with no
          speed limit (17,586 troop-ticks; up to 36 units in a tick, 108× a walk; the y clamp at the field's edge up to
          12 more); 2. sideways slides: `_makeWay` steps a yielder aside at its own speed once per troop passing (31,937
          troop-ticks, up to 14.6 a tick: his hero knight walks 275 with its speed stat and boots); 3. the Auto Buy
          slide: `speedTo`'s catch-up pace is the fastest living melee's, 275 there, so catching-up archers and wizards
          and every Auto-Bought troop moved at 8.6-13× their walk, mostly in their attack or skill strips (an
          Auto-Bought archer crossed 178 units in 1.55 s without a walk frame); 4. the attack strip and 299's skill
          strips won over walking; 5. the walk strip played at 10 frames a second whatever the speed (a knight at 105,
          base 24). Board.update already clamps a frame to 0.1 s. The game's own work at that scene fits 60 fps
          (flutter_tester on the Mac, update and drawing without the GPU: p50 4.3 ms, p95 9.8, p99 15.8, two frames of
          4,494 over 33 ms), so the stalls in his recording are not the game's update or drawing; 308's readout shows
          his Mac's frames.
     - **The fix, visual only** (the orchestrator's "go 307 V1-V3"): the Board draws each troop at a body that follows
       its game position at max(3× its walk, its walking pace, the gap over 0.3 s), at most a 30 fps frame's worth a
       frame; carried troops, new or revived ones and ones put somewhere are drawn where the game has them; the body
       walks whenever it moves (over the attack and skill strips' tails, not over a wind-up), its stride 1-3× its type's
       base pace. Taps, plates, drops, bars, rings, bubbles and labels follow the body; a plain shot leaves it. The
       game's positions, fights and the w89 identity are untouched.
     - **Measured after** (the same replay, the drawn bodies): moves of more than 2 px a tick without the walk strip
       3,805 → 0; runs of 3 px or more without it ~1,700 → 22 (sub-pixel snaps, knockbacks' own slides); an
       Auto-Bought troop's first 3 s all walk (was mostly attack and skill strips); the largest drawn step 13 units a
       tick, the hero knight's own walk × 3. GIFs before and after: shots/troop-motion/before, after.
     - **Left to the owner** (gameplay, identity changes, not built): capping the catch-up pace (2× a troop's own walk
       instead of the fastest melee's 275) and the make-way step (one walk step a tick in all). With the bodies a
       catching-up wizard still runs at 275 with its legs at 3×. The owner capped both: 309.

311. **No troop walks faster than 6× its type's base walk: the speed stat stays, the walk is capped** (the owner,
     2026-10-09, asked about the Hero knight at 275, 11.5× its type's 24, whose feet still slid about 2× at 310's 6×
     stride, picked "Batasi kecepatan jalan" (cap the walk speed: the speed stat's and the boots' bonus capped, so the

     moving", "Field stats") follow it.
     - **The rule:** `walkMost` 6, `walkCap(type)` = 6 × its `troopTypes` speed (soldier and archer 132, knight 144,
       swordsman 168, lancer 156, priest 120, armored_axeman, wizard and knight_templar 108). Every troop, Heroes and
       plain, not monsters: `Unit.walkSpeed` = min(its speed stat, its cap). The stat itself (`Stats.speed`: boots, a
       Hero's ×3, the aura, an Artifact) is unchanged, so a charge, which goes at 3× the stat, a leap, Skyfall, Phantom
       Rush's dashes and every carry keep their speeds. A slow or a pin slows the capped walk.
     - **What reads it:** the walk itself (`_moveToward`: to a spot, to a foe, kiting, falling back, walking home), the
       catch-up pace (`speedTo`: min(2× its walk, its cap) against the fastest melee's walk), a tick's steps aside
       (`_makeWay`: one capped walk step in all), the stall detector's quarter step (`_watchStuck`), a
       necromancer's reach horizon (`decideSummon`, the troops' walks), Crippling Shot's "faster than the archer", the
       camera's meeting point (`BattleFocus`, the lead troop's walk) and the drawn body's walk test (body_look.dart;
       `bodyStride` is `walkMost`). What reads the stat: the charge (`charge`), the monsters' walks, Town folk (their
       type's base pace).

314. **The healing necromancer's choices stick: no standing pinned at the edge, no flipping between healing and
     backing off** (the owner, 2026-10-09: "ai necromencer healer juga masi suka diam bingung antara mau heal dan dan
     melarikan diri"). Built by necro-mend on 311 (phase 1 a probe, then the orchestrator's go on plan a-e).
     formation-and-navigation.md "The healing necromancer" holds the rules, units-and-combat.md "The healer" the
     short form.
     - **Why it stood still** (a probe through the Board at 1600×947, every tick of every healing necromancer: its
       choice, MP, margin, `rightLimit`, its move; on a copy of the owner's live save at wave 58,
       snapshots/save-necro-mend-w58-20261009-233957.json, waves 59 and 60, and on w89's wave 90):
       1. A late army's reach covers the whole field: an archer of the owner's army reaches about 1150 px, w89's
          archers 570-656 and wizards 370-430, and the view is about 324 wide. Every spot was "too close", so `_mend`
          backed off every tick; the back-off is capped at max(`rightLimit`, its x) (decision 123), so it stood at
          the right edge or just past it, not yet on, drifting to the top or bottom, and healed only a monster that
          came within its 64. Wave 59: 300 of 366 healer-seconds still with MP and a hurt monster about, the longest
          33-41 s each, 2.9 heals a healer-minute. One w89 healer waited 29 s right of the limit until it was alone.
       2. A rest spot the push couldn't get out of a reach (an escort's at most `escortReach` behind its boss, any at
          most `rightLimit`): it walked in to the margin, backed off a tick, walked in again, two turns every two
          ticks, standing still to the eye (x ±0.5 px), often short of MP. Wave 60: rest/back-off turns 305 a
          healer-minute, 660 of 985 healer-seconds still.
       3. A back-off held by the edge with the troop level with it had no y step: it didn't move at all.
       A heal spot safe at the pick but not on arrival (walk in / back off 0.3-11 a healer-minute) and cast or rise
       freezes (at most 2.7 s a wave) were minor.
     - **The rules now** (`Unit.mend`, `Mend`; `mendClear` half a tile, `mendCommit` 1 s, `mendTurns`):
       - a troop whose reach + `necroSafety` takes in both ends of the edge it may back off to doesn't count: it
         can't get away from it, so it heals under its fire (melee and short reaches still keep it away);
       - a back-off starts at the margin and goes on until it is `mendClear` clear; held by the edge it slides along
         it, up or down away from the troop; cornered, it holds and heals or swings at what it reaches;
       - the heal spot is on the ring at 0.9 × its range round the hurt monster, straight first, then 40° and 80° to
         either side, the first `mendClear` clear with a clear straight way there; a monster it walks to heal is kept
         `mendCommit` (needing then only a spot outside the reach); an escort's boss still first;
       - a rest spot is set off for only when half `mendClear` clear or more, kept while out of the reach, and not
         walked to by a way through a reach: else it holds (`Mend.hold`).
       Unchanged: its place at the back (rest a tile behind the rearmost monster, an escort's behind its boss), the
       anti-stall cap at max(`rightLimit`, its x) (decision 123), the swing, the walk on alone, heals don't stack (#78).
     - **Measured after** (the same probe; before → after; waves 59, 60 of the owner's save and w89's 90):

315. **This repository goes public, the Pixel Paint way: the art git-ignored and only encrypted in git, hooks that keep
     the two in step, a privacy check; a re-runnable switch to a fresh public history at path-of-hero** (the owner,
     2026-10-11, first through the Pixel Paint session: apply Pixel Paint's way with paid assets in a public repo; then
     "aku mau repo tower-defense juga ikut publik"; the owner's answers: history "Riwayat baru" (one fresh commit of today's
     code), the private docs "Repo privat terpisah", a clone without the password "Bisa, pakai gambar pengganti";
     after the audit: the whole-pack vaults stay private, the public repository is **path-of-hero** while
     triasbrata/tower-defense stays private as the archive, the decisions log stays public but scrubbed (no IP
     addresses, home folders, key or password file names, device ids; the owner's quotes stay), the commit identity unchanged).
     By public-repo; reports/public-repo.md has the audit, the licences, the design and the switch-over.
     - **The licences** (each pack's own text): none mentions encryption, all forbid redistributing the files (Pixel
       Crawler and the Mana Seed demo only selling). The owner already read Pixel Paint's packs (Kenmi's two, Zerie,
       GandalfHardcore) as allowed encrypted in a public repo, and the game vaults hold exactly what every itch build
       ships readable, so a leaked key exposes nothing new: the 7 game vaults go public. The 7 whole-pack vaults
       (about 19 MB, e.g. 20,974 icons of the paid Kenmi pack) would hand out the packs: they go to the private notes.
     - **`tool/asset_vault.py`** (assets.md "The asset vault"): `sync` (post-checkout/post-merge: unpack every vault whose
       files are unedited since the last sync, absent, or placeholders; warn and leave edited ones; a file that left its
       vault is deleted in a linked worktree but only listed in the main checkout, the game may run: `prune`),
       `hook pre-commit` (re-pack only a changed vault, refuse one that moved in git since the last sync, never pack
       placeholders, nothing without a key, refuse a licensed file forced past .gitignore), `hook pre-push` (with
       `poh.publicRoot`: only main and v* tags of the public history to `public`, that history nowhere else unless
       POH_PUSH_PUBLIC_HISTORY=1, the privacy check on what goes public), `commit` (--allow-empty for art alone),
       `resolve` (a vault both sides of a merge changed, file by file from the JSONs of HEAD, MERGE_HEAD and their
       base, theirs read from MERGE_HEAD's parts; a file both changed differently is named, `--take ours|theirs`; then
       asset_manifest.py and a re-pack), `install-hooks`, `--root DIR` (the private notes' pack vaults). The sync state
       is per worktree (`git rev-parse --git-path asset_vault.synced`); no tree file: the vault's tar sha256 is the
       fingerprint. `.githooks/` calls it. The key: `git config poh.vaultKeyFile` (a clone's own setting), the built-in
       default the neutral ~/.config/path-of-hero/asset-vault.key, so the public code names no key file.
     - **The Android signing's key.properties**: ANDROID_KEY_PROPERTIES, else android/key.properties; release-build.sh
       sets the variable from `git config poh.androidKeyProperties` (the same reason).
     - **`tool/gen_placeholders.py`** also draws the placeholder app icons, lists what it drew in `assets/.placeholders`
       (sha256 each), and refuses a file there that isn't its own (the real art, git-ignored in the public repo).
     - **`tool/privacy_check.py`** (`--staged`, `--rev`, `--dir`, `--message`, `--messages`): private-notes markers, IP
       addresses (not loopback or documentation ones), e-mail addresses (not noreply, example or licence texts), home
       folders with a real name, token shapes, key files by name, and the private terms from the private notes'
       `privacy-terms.txt` (never in the public tree; CI checks the shapes alone). In the pre-commit and pre-push hooks
       and CI; and on commit messages, which go public as much as the files (found while writing the agents' patches:
       their commit messages name the agents' folders): the commit-msg hook, and pre-push on the messages of the
       commits the public remote doesn't have yet.
     - **`scripts/test-release-build.sh` in a public clone** (found running it on the rehearsed public tree): the
       denied files' bytes came from old commits (8a4ab07, f03a899), which the fresh history lacks, and the
       allowlist's doc copy from docs/itch-page.md, which moves to the private notes. Now those 3 checks are skipped
       there with a note, and the allowlist is compared with `private/docs/itch-page.md` when present (215 checks
       with the private notes, 214 without, 224 before the switch).
     - **CI** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (path-of-hero only): the privacy check, the vault with POH_VAULT_KEY or
       placeholders and `-x art` (a fork's pull request), the tools' tests, analyze, a fast set; the whole suite on a
       push to main. release.yml's guards take path-of-hero and tower-defense.
     - **`scripts/switch_public.py`** turns a checkout of the final main into the public tree and writes the private
       notes beside it, so every doc, probe and vault change until the switch gets the same treatment: itch-page,
       sdlc and agent-workflow, marketing/, the agents' and itch scripts, the export, tool/asset_packs and asset_meta.py,
       raw_sprites/README.md and the pack vaults to the private notes; every doc's private sections to
       `<doc>.private.md`, its public blocks in, links to the moved docs unlinked; the docs and the Dart comment lines
       scrubbed; the probes' default folders from `test/probe_root.dart` (POH_PROBE_ROOT); public/next/ in place
       (README, CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG, CLAUDE.md, docs/README.md, the new docs/process.md); the art and the icons out
       of the index; then the privacy check with the private terms, asset_manifest.py --check, asset_vault.py check.
     - **Rehearsed** on a scratch clone of this branch (2026-10-11): SWITCH OK; the fresh commit has 1 commit, 1 root,
       582 files, none with a licensed file's sha256, the privacy check ok with 14 terms; 361 files untracked. A

     - **Not done here** (the owner's and the orchestrator's, at a time the owner picks: reports/public-repo.md "The

       checkout. Merging this branch needs `git config poh.vaultKeyFile <the vault key's file>` and

316. **The git hooks do nothing in a tree without `tool/asset_vault.py`, but pre-push refuses the push there** (found
     after 315, checking out the private notes: `git worktree add private private` printed "can't open file
     …/private/tool/asset_vault.py" and exited 1). By hooks-fix.
     - **Why it failed:** `core.hooksPath` is `.githooks`, relative, so `git worktree add` finds the post-checkout
       hook in the clone it is started from but runs it in the new tree, which for the private notes or a branch of
       the old history has no tool. `git worktree add` exits with that hook's status, so a script under `set -e`
       stopped there.
     - **Now** pre-commit, commit-msg, post-checkout and post-merge start with `[ -f tool/asset_vault.py ] || exit 0`:
       such a tree has no art and no vaults to keep in step. Nothing changes in a tree that has the tool. A command
       run inside a tree without `.githooks/` (the private notes) finds no hook at all, and no branch carries
       `.githooks/` without the tool (the hooks came after it), so in practice only the clone's post-checkout that
       `git worktree add` runs in the new tree is affected.
     - **pre-push fails closed** (on review: a skip there would let a push from such a tree past the public-history
       guard, where before the change it failed): without the tool it prints "pre-push: no tool/asset_vault.py in
       this tree; the public-history guard can't run" and exits 1. Push from a checkout that has the tool; the refs
       are the same.

320. **The awakening skills' cost in troops: Phantom Rush's swordsman a phantom while it dashes, a wind-up claims its

       one skill, the swordsman's Phantom Rush**: with it alone off the army lost 0.69 ± 0.19 fewer troops a wave at
       w41-70 (−15%; b 4.57), more than with every awakening skill off (−0.53 ± 0.18), and w21-40 −0.25 ± 0.08
       (−33%); every one of those falls a swordsman. The rush hops the swordsman, nearly always at full HP, through
       the monsters' front to the most wounded foe within 2.5 tiles, cut after cut for about a second, and every
       monster there makes it its nearest troop: **15% of the rushes (352 of 2,327; 21% on the owner's save) ended
       with the swordsman dead in the rush**, 295 of them from 75%+ HP, mostly to high elites, elites and mini bosses.
       Its fall rate in the 3 s after its own rush was 3.9 a fight-minute, 0.5 the rest of the time. The other five
       skills fielded (Unbroken, Spellbreaker, Lifeline, Singularity, Consecration) cost nothing measurable
       (Singularity helps late); not the MP (nothing waiting for the awakening skill's MP: −0.19 ± 0.13) and not 299's
       wind-up (−0.05 ± 0.16). For the rush, a smaller round (+0.53 ± 0.38), at most 2 cuts (±0) or only the foes at
       the front (+0.21) didn't help, nor would an HP gate (they die from full HP); untouchable while it dashes:
       −0.99 ± 0.22 (−22%); untargetable (the monsters don't pick it, areas and shots still hit): −0.68 ± 0.18.
     - **A second defect, no falls but wasted casts**: since 299 a troop's rule is asked again on the wind-up's blow,

       because the knight was healed back to full in the 0.3 s (its rule, 298: hurt at all).

322. **An army wiped mid-wave costs a heart and the wave is played again; the game is over when the hearts run out**
     (the owner, 2026-10-12, asked what should happen when the whole army dies, and picked "Kalah wave: −1 hati, ulang":
     an army wipe is no longer game over; the player loses 1 heart (2 lives), the wave's monsters are swept away and
     the same wave is played again, so he can buy troops again; 3 hearts = 3 chances). Why: the lives never mattered.
     The balance pass (318) counted 1,681 new-game waves that lost 17 lives, nearly all in a run's last wave, and every
     run ended in a wipe at full hearts, because the game was over "at 0 lives or when every troop is dead". By
     lives-rule (lib/wipe.dart; units-and-combat.md "An army wiped", ui-hud.md "An army wiped").
     - **The wipe** is checked at the end of `tick`, after the raised joined and before the win: a troop fell this
       wave, none is alive (one Resurrection raised in that tick counts), no Phoenix Plume rise is due, and a monster
       still lives or is queued. The last troop and the last monster falling together is a win. A wave begun with no
       troop is never a wipe: as before, only its leaks cost lives.
     - **It costs** `wipeLives` 2 lives (a heart; at 1 life the half). At 0 the game is over as by leaks: the monsters
       stay and cheer, the scoreboard. `over` is `lives <= 0` alone.
     - **The sweep:** the living and queued monsters go with no gold, loot or score. The ones on the field hop for joy
       2.4 s (the game-over hop), then vanish in the necromancer's summon circle (existing art; no new shape). Effects,
       zones, shots and what was left for later end as at a wave's end. What the wave paid as it went stays (kill gold,
       kill score, kills); its materials lying on the field are lost, since they come only with a win (else a replay
       would pay them twice).
     - **The replay:** `wave` goes back to the last won one, so between waves everything reads as after that win: the
       back line, a Town due (one left before the lost wave isn't due again; one marked after it waits for its win), the
       wave meter's next wave, "from wave 15 won". The next start rolls the same wave afresh (its number and tide, new
       dice). Its wave bonus and score, Shadow ease, Grudge target, Hero, boss chest and Town roll come once, when it is
       won. `lostWave` marks it: the Shadows' catch-up doesn't land twice on one wave number, and Lewati's skip buff
       owed for it is owed again. The Tavern's boosts count the lost wave (it was fought, as a game over counted it).
     - **Between:** "Replace fallen" lists the army (the Heroes go to Fallen Heroes as ever), Auto Buy buys it back as
       the gold allows, Auto Wave counts down as after a win (the Auto hold waits below 75% of the cap as ever). The
       message window says "Your army fell! -1 heart." / "Wave N again." and the heart pops. The game saves at once, so
       quitting keeps the heart lost. The free priest is a new game's gift and doesn't come again.
     - **Saves** (additive, `v` stays 3): `lostWave` while set (loaded only when it is the next wave). **Telemetry:**
       the event `wipe` (`lives`, `livesLost`, `foes`, `over`) and a wave record's `end` `wiped`; `eventVersion` and
       `telemetryVersion` 13. **The score:** the lives term (`lifeScore`) stays, but a game now always ends at 0
       lives, so it pays nothing. The battle log adds "Army fell: -1 heart, wave N again".
     - **What a run's end means now:** a run ends after three wipes, or fewer with leaks. The balance pass weighs where
       runs end and how many replays they take (lives-rule's probe plan).
325. **The Pusaka's ring under a bound type's troops is drawn in the sprites' pixels** (the owner, 2026-10-12: "ring
     putih atau kuning di bawah troops di buat jadi pixelated", make the white or yellow ring under the troops
     pixelated). Why: it was the field's one smooth line right under the troops, a 1 px anti-aliased oval among pixel
     art. The ring the owner sees is the Pusaka's (decisions-log 149), not a mark of Heroes or awakening: every troop of
     a type with a Pusaka bound wears it, in the Pusaka's colour; on the owner's save God's Thunder's lemon on the
     archers is the yellow (War Drum's tan on the lancers), and the seven bound Pusaka without a colour of their own (Moonwell, Ember Brand, Aegis Seal,
     First Cut, Hero's Cloak, Heartbeat, Finishing Blade) ring in cream, the white. The troops' ground shadows,
     the awakened ones' gold and white among them, were sprites in pixels already. By pixel-rings (lib/pusaka_look.dart;
     ui-hud.md "The Pusaka in battle").
     - **The same ring, in pixels:** the same 20 × 8 box centred 1 above the feet, the same colours at 90%, steady. Its
       cells (`pixelRingCells`) are a stepped line one cell thick, one world unit each like a sprite's pixels, built once
       at load as a white image with a clear pixel round it and drawn nearest, without anti-aliasing, flat in the
       Pusaka's colour, a whole number of units from the feet, so at any zoom its steps fall on the shadow's pixels and
       a screen pixel is the colour or nothing. The guide's K6 picture draws it the same way.
     - **No dearer:** one image draw per ring in a paint made once per Pusaka, as the oval was one draw. Measured on
       the owner's wave-30 save at 1600×947, 40 s of its wave with 29 rings a frame (test/probe_pixel_rings.dart): a
       frame's drawing 1.93 → 1.49 ms on average (95th percentile 3.91 → 2.36), rasterising it in the tests' renderer
       185 → 160 ms; the two runs shared a busy machine, so read it as no rise, not as a gain.
     - **Then every other ring, the halo and the reach (325b).** The first pass left the field's other smooth shapes
       for the owner to decide: the guard ring, the effects' rings (a Barrier's teal among them, Impale's and Ice
       Grip's dashed one), Spear Wall's brace ring, a Hero's soft halo and a dragged troop's reach disc. The owner asked
       for all of them, the halo and the disc too, as stepped pixel shapes (a glow as a few stepped bands of alpha, no
       smooth gradient). By pixel-rings (lib/pixel_shapes.dart; ui-hud.md "The field's rings in pixels"). One module
       now builds every shape once at load and draws it as the Pusaka's ring is drawn. The guard ring keeps 16 × 7 (an
       odd height, so its box sits half a unit higher, on whole units); the effects' nested rings go 18 × 8, 14 × 6,
       10 × 4, 6 × 2 (even, so each stays centred; they shrank by 3 × 1.2 before); the dashed ring turns as before in
       8 steps a dash; the halo is 4 bands of the old gradient's alpha, its pulse by whole units; the reach is a filled
       disc at the same 12%. Colours, alphas and pulses are as they were. The zones', the wind-ups', the skills' ground
       circles and reach rings, Holy Shield's dome and a new Hero's gold ring were the packs' sprites, in pixels already.
327. **A shot already fired is never lost mid-flight: it flies on to where its target went and lands there, an area
     shot hitting the monsters round that spot and a single one the unit standing on it** (the owner, 2026-10-12:
     "particle yang sudah terkirim jangan hilang di tengah jalan, biarkan tetap terkirim ke tempat posisi monsternya
     terakhir dan kalau itu attack area maka monster di sekitarnya juga ikut kena", a shot already sent must not vanish
     halfway: let it fly on to the monster's last place, and if it is an area attack the monsters round it are hit too;
     asked whether a single shot should then hit a monster standing on that spot: "mau"). Why: until then a shot whose
     target fell or leaked before it landed was dropped mid-air, so a wizard's fireball vanished whenever another troop
     took its target first and its splash never came. By shot-through (lib/game.dart's shot loop, `Shot.to`,
     `Shot.aim`, `landReach`, `_standingOn`; units-and-combat.md "A shot whose target went flies on").
     - **The flight:** the first tick its target isn't alive (fallen, or gone past the line) the shot keeps that place,
       frozen (`Shot.to`), and flies on to it at its own speed; the UI draws it towards that spot (`Shot.aim`).
     - **The landing**, as on a living target: its hit burst and ring at the spot. The unit of the target's side nearest
       the spot within `landReach` (half a tile, a line shot's `lineWidth`: the owner asked for the shot's own hit
       radius or tolerance, and a homing shot has neither, it lands on its target's very place) takes the shot as its
       target would have:
       its damage and source, `onHit`, the `landed` Fx, the relics' landing, kill gold. A splash shot hurts every unit of
       that side within its splash of the spot, the rest as splash (`Hit.extra`, a skill's `Hit.skill`). Nobody there: a
       single shot shows its look alone, a splash shot its splash alone.
     - **Symmetry:** the monsters' shots at troops do the same (a skeleton archer's arrow, Volley, Barbed Arrow, Spear
       Throw, Sticky Glob). The instant blows (melee and its splash, the troop skills' rings and thrusts, smites, chains,
       God's Thunder, zones) and the line shots are unchanged.
     - **A wave's end and a wipe:** a shot still in the air is `spent`: it flies on and lands its look and ring, and
       hurts nobody. Until then a monster's shot in the air at a living troop as the wave ended still hurt it between
       waves, and a wipe (322) cleared every shot at once.
     - **Cost:** nothing made a tick (`to` keeps the target's own `Point`); the spot's search runs once a landing, over
       the units, without a list.
     - **The w89 identity** (test/probe_pusaka_w89_identity.dart, on main with 320 merged, against its fccf102f golden):
       every stat, text, tooltip and preview line the same; only the fights move, since shots that were dropped now land
       and roll their dice. In the seven 45 s fights of wave 90 the kills at 45 s are +1 to +6 each (+25 in all) and the
       gold +230 to +7,533; in the three arms that play waves 90 and 91, five of the six waves end sooner (wave 90 171.7,
       161.2, 188.6 s to 177.2, 151.6, 180.4; wave 91 130.7, 126.3, 136.1 to 130.2, 121.1, 132.7), the kills alike (wave
       90's 215 to 221 in one arm, 221 to 219 in another), the troops fallen both ways (8 to 6, 0 to 1), and one Hero
       rolled after wave 90 is another (the dice moved on). Before 320 (on 1d151d71) it moved the same way: +17 kills in
       the fights, waves 1-6.5% sooner. The new golden: `<agents>/probes/shot-through/w89-on-e05b6e4b.txt`.
     - **Checks:** test/shots_test.dart (the cases above, a wave's end, a wipe), hit_source_test's list (the landing's
       `_hurt` calls name `on`); test/probe_shot_through_shots.dart's frames at 1600×947 (`<agents>/shots/shot-through/`:
       the fireball and Arcane Blast fly on past the fall and burst at the spot, the splash taking 22 and 33 off each orc
       beside it). Balance (the splash lands more often) is measured after the merge, by replaying saved waves.
